title: changelog guide: Angelica Changes
text:
# Angelica Changes
For those unaware, Angelica is the GTNH Optifine replacement, improving rendering across the board, and allowing in-built compatibility for shaders!

This mod is not new, but there are some changes for 2.9! This does not include the huge amount of effort to generally optimise rendering, or bug fixes

## Compact CTM
This one is for the texture developers out there! You may or may not have been aware, but it previously took 47 unique textures just to make glass look pretty! Angelica has changed this with built-in support for Compact CTM. Now you only need to make 5 files per block, meaning 9x less work, and nearly 10x less file space taken up, all with no loss to visual quality

## Advanced Color Tracing
> [!WARNING]
> This is not yet fully implemented into the pack, and work is still continuing. But hey, what is an update without a premature teaser for the next!
Lots of work is going on in the background to give Advanced Color Tracing as default in GTNH. Those of you using something like Euphoria Patches will already be familiar, but $$\text{soon}^{TM}$$ there will be full support for any shaders (or possibly without!)

  
    Colored lighting generated by lava

title: changelog guide: Bubble Columns
text:
# Bubble Columns
Bubble Columns have been backported from 1.13, using the same mechanics as in modern versions. For those who have never used them, please read below:

## Usage
Players and air-breathing mobs can enter a bubble column, which replenishes air supply at the same speed as if they left the water. Slower mining speed penalties still apply where relevant. Water-breathing mobs will suffocate when inside a bubble column.

Bubble columns can be created by placing either Magma Blocks Magma Block or Soul Sand Soul Sand, creating either a whirlpool, or upwards column respectively. These will then propel the player in the direction of the bubble column

title: changelog guide: Full Color System
text:
# Full Color System
What is life without a little Color! GTNH now has a fully built-in complete color system! This works with quests, signs, anvils, chat, and just about anywhere that text is rendered!

## Included Features
- All 16 classic colors - just type "\&" and a color code!
- RGB hex colors - any of 16 million colors
- Gradients - create smooth color transitions
- Rainbow text - hey, why not?
- Wavy text - animated bouncing text
- Bold, italic, underline and more - combined freely with any color

# Usage
Simply type the color before your text and everything will be that color until you either use another color, or reset with `\&r`.
## Vanilla Colors:

| Code | Color |
| -------------- | --------------- |
| `\&0` | Black |
| `\&1` | Dark Blue |
| `\&2` | Dark Green |
| `\&3` | Dark Aqua |
| `\&4` | Dark Red |
| `\&5` | Dark Purple |
| `\&6` | Gold |
| `\&7` | Gray |
| `\&8` | Dark Gray |
| `\&9` | Blue |
| `\&a` | Green |
| `\&b` | Aqua |
| `\&c` | Red |
| `\&d` | Light Purple |
| `\&e` | Yellow |
| `\&f` | White |

## Formatting:
| Code | Effect |
| -------------- | --------------- |
| `\&l` | __Bold Text__ |
| `\&o` | _Italic Text_  |
| `\&n` | Underlined Text |
| `\&m` | ~~Strikethrough Text~~ (Strikethrough) |
| `\&k` | Obfuscated Text (Not rendered for clarity)|

One special type of gradient has its own special code! Type `\&q` for Rainbow effects!

title: changelog guide: GuideNH
text:
# GuideNH
GuideNH is a brand new mod to 2.9, designed to provide more accessible in-game information that was previously buried either in the quest book, or on external sites such as the wiki.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This is not intended to __replace__ the wiki, but instead provide vital in-game information to get started

## Usage
Hovering your mouse on the left side brings up the "Navigation" bar. This will show the "top-level" categories defined by the guides. Guides are generally sectioned into relevant mods (for example, AE2 guides under AppliedEnergistics2), but there are some exceptions, such as the changelog you are now reading!

From here, those categories expand to show the guides within that category. The category index page can also be clicked for a basic overview of the category, and links to all sub-pages

Pages can be bookmarked from the right side of the Navigation bar, and the home page (accessed on the header-bar) will show any recommended guides, alongside your history!

Searching also is in-built, allowing you to find what you need without searching.

Guide authors can also set an item or block as the "item_id" for the page, allowing you to "Hold [G] to open guide" either in the inventory, or in NEI itself.

## Features
The list of features is frankly too long to properly list here, so please accept this semi-random collation of things simply to showcase the range of ideas that can be rendered in this mod:

This _is_ an __example__ of ~~the same~~ different ___formats___

  - $$\dot{m}$$: Current Flow Rate
  - $$\dot{m}^*$$: Optimal Flow Rate
  - $$\eta$$: Efficiency

 

## Technical Details
GuideNH works using Markdown pages, with YAML frontmatter and MDX-Style runtime tags. Pages are specified as being under a certain language by placing under a language folder such as `_en_us`.

For a full list of tags, and how specifics of navigation and more are handled, check the Wiki!

title: changelog guide: Mechanical Armor
text:
# Mechanical Armor
Mechanical Armor is a new set of powerful tech-based armor that can scale with your progression! First constructed in HV, you can unlock new augments, frames and energy cores as you progress through the tiers to become more powerful as you go.

Different frames will have different numbers of **Movement**, **Protection**, **Utility**, and **Prismatic** slots, which determine which augment types can be placed into the armor! Choose your frames wisely to make use of those critical slots!

Expect this armor set to cover the same range and abilities as the current tech armors (NanoSuit, QuantumSuit etc.) with similar tiering

This guide will not go in depth on the specifics, those are for you to discover as you progress!

title: changelog guide: Beam Crafter
text:
# Beam Crafter

The Beam Crafter is a ZPM tier multiblock that uses beams of particles provided by any other source to bombard fluids and liquids in the inputs to craft some other output.

## Construction:
The Beam crafter is a single multiblock unlike the Beamline. Beamline pipes are used to route the created beams into the Beam Input HatchBeam Input Hatch. The length of these pipes has no effect on any attributes of the machine, or the beams themselves.

### Requires:
- 1 Beam CrafterBeam Crafter
- 224-228 Shielded Accelerator CasingShielded Accelerator Casing
- 26 Tiered Glass (any) bartworks:BW_GlasBlocks:5
- 16 Grate Machine CasingGrate Machine Casing
- 2 Beam Input HatchBeam Input Hatch
- 1+ Energy Hatch (any collider casing) ULV Energy Hatch
- 0+ Input Bus (any collider casing) Input Bus (ULV)
- 0+ Input Hatch (any collider casing) Input Hatch (ULV)
- 0+ Output Bus (any collider casing) Output Bus (ULV)
- 0+ Output Hatch (any collider casing) Output Hatch (ULV)

## Usage:
If a valid craft is detected with the items and fluids provided, a craft will start. Only at this point will the Beam Crafter begin to accept particles through the beamline input hatches. If the correct particles are present in this beam, they will be consumed to provide progress to the craft. The recipe does __not__ stop if the particle beams are interrupted, but progress will halt. Energy is consumed constantly whilst the craft is underway, regardless of the particle amount being provided.

The machine will buffer particles, but only whilst running as otherwise it cannot accept particles.

## Routing:
Alongside the Beam Crafter, there are three new logistical multiblocks designed for routing beams. They are the Beam Mirror, Beam Splitter, and Beam Stabilizer.
- Beam MirrorBeam Mirror - Allows the rotation of a beam by either 90, or 180 degrees
- Beam Splitter Beam Splitter - Allows the splitting of a mixed stream of particle packets into 4 separate configurable lines
- Beam Stabilizer Beam Stabilizer - Acts as a small buffer, allowing the conversion of an intermittent high rate beam into a constant beam of lower amount

title: changelog guide: Endothermic Fridge
text:
# Endothermic Fridge

The Endothermic Fridge (EnF) is a ZPM tier multiblock for mass cooling hot ingots and fluids. The ENF is a direct upgrade from the Vacuum FreezerVacuum Freezer because it runs up to 1,200% speed, offers 256 parallels, supports Multi-Amp and Laser Energy Hatches for serious overclocking, and has unlimited tier skips. The EnF replaces the Mega Vacuum Freezer. That means it can run any recipe regardless of voltage tier as long as there is enough power. The speed slowly increases up to 1.5x during activity and decreases back to   1.0x while idle. Optionally, enable cryotheum cooling in the GUI of the controller to 5x the rate at which the speed modifier increases at the cost of 250-375 L/s of gelid cryotheum. Upgrade the structure with infinity cooled casings to unlock subspace cooling, which further multiplies both the speed of the machine and consumption rate of gelid cryotheum at the cost of exotic coolants. The EnF only outperforms the Cryogenic Freezer Cryogenic Freezer if it can take full advantage of its 256 parallels (4+ overclocks) or use subspace cooling. It is also worth noting that the Cryogenic Freezer has been buffed to accommodate these new changes with double the parallels (8->16), and higher speed (220%->300%) 

## Construction:
The EnF is available in two tiers but the only structural difference between them is the infinity cooled casings Infinity Cooled Casing added to the T2 structure. The glass can be any tier and has no effect on the operation of the machine. Buses/hatches may replace any fridge casing anywhere on the structure. Multi-Amp and Laser Energy Hatches are supported for serious overclocking regardless of glass tier. Use the Multiblock Structure Hologram ProjectorMultiblock Structure Hologram Projector to visualize/build the structure with subchannel "glass" to specify the tier of the glass and the number of projectors held in a single stack to specify the tier of the machine.

The 208 infinity cooled casings require 255k (L) infinity, 240k (L) spacetime, and 59.9k (L) hypogen to build. It is recommended to wait until hypogen is craftable in the Dimensionally Transcendent Plasma Forge Dimensionally Transcendent Plasma Forge instead of relying on the Mk-IV Fusion Reactor recipe.
### T1 Requires:
- 1 Endothermic FridgeEndothermic Fridge
- 750-773 Fridge CasingFridge Casing
- 351 Frost Proof Machine CasingFrost Proof Machine Casing
- 148 Tungstensteel Reinforced BlockTungstensteel Reinforced Block
- 148 Tungstensteel Pipe CasingTungstensteel Pipe Casing
- 146 Callisto Ice Frame BoxCallisto Ice Frame Box
- 135 Robust Tungstensteel Machine CasingRobust Tungstensteel Machine Casing
- 51 Coolant DuctCoolant Duct
- 40 Ledox SheetmetalLedox Sheetmetal
- 18 Tiered Glass (any) bartworks:BW_GlasBlocks:15
- 1+ Energy Hatch (any fridge casing) ULV Energy Hatch
- 1 Maintenance Hatch (any fridge casing) Maintenance Hatch
- 0+ Input Bus (any fridge casing) Input Bus (ULV)
- 0+ Input Hatch (any fridge casing) Input Hatch (ULV)
- 0+ Output Bus (any fridge casing) Output Bus (ULV)
- 0+ Output Hatch (any fridge casing) Output Hatch (ULV)

### T2 Requires:

- 1 Endothermic FridgeEndothermic Fridge
- 750-773 Fridge CasingFridge Casing
- 208 Infinity Cooled CasingInfinity Cooled Casing
- 148 Tungstensteel Reinforced BlockTungstensteel Reinforced Block
- 148 Tungstensteel Pipe CasingTungstensteel Pipe Casing
- 146 Callisto Ice Frame BoxCallisto Ice Frame Box
- 143 Frost Proof Machine CasingFrost Proof Machine Casing
- 135 Robust Tungstensteel Machine CasingRobust Tungstensteel Machine Casing
- 51 Coolant DuctCoolant Duct
- 40 Ledox SheetmetalLedox Sheetmetal
- 18 Tiered Glass (any) bartworks:BW_GlasBlocks:15
- 1+ Energy Hatch (any fridge casing) ULV Energy Hatch
- 1 Maintenance Hatch (any fridge casing) Maintenance Hatch
- 0+ Input Bus (any fridge casing) Input Bus (ULV)
- 0+ Input Hatch (any fridge casing) Input Hatch (ULV)
- 0+ Output Bus (any fridge casing) Output Bus (ULV)
- 0+ Output Hatch (any fridge casing) Output Hatch (ULV)

### Wallsharing:
EnFs may wallshare each of their sides to save on casings and buses/hatches. That does NOT include any of the infinity cooled casings. 

## Usage:
The EnF is a direct upgrade from the Vacuum Freezer because it runs up to 1,200% speed, offers 256 parallels, supports multi-amp and laser energy hatches for serious overclocking, and has unlimited tier skips. That means it can run any recipe regardless of voltage tier as long as there is enough power. For example, a ZPM 256A laser energy hatch can run UIV recipes.

The speed modifier of the EnF increases up to 1.5x during activity and decreases back down to 1.0x while idle, as seen below. It takes 5 minutes of continuous activity to achieve the maximum speed modifier but only 20 seconds to lose it all. Optionally, enable cryotheum cooling in the GUI of the controller to 5x the rate at which the speed modifier increases at the cost of 250-375 L/s gelid cryotheum. The consumption rate scales linearly with the speed modifier, but it allows the EnF to achieve the maximum 1.5x speed modifier in just 1 minute instead. Running out of gelid cryotheum while cryotheum cooling is enabled causes the machine to immediately shut down and void the current recipe.

- +0.00833 speed modifier per 5 seconds while active (cryotheum cooling disabled), 5 minutes to max
- +0.04167 speed modifier per 5 seconds while active (cryotheum cooling enabled) 1 minute to max
- -0.025 speed modifier per second while idle, 20 seconds to min

## Subspace Cooling
Upgrade the EnF structure with infinity cooled casings to unlock subspace cooling, which instantly multiplies the speed of the machine at the cost of exotic coolants. If cryotheum cooling is enabled, the speed boost also applies to the consumption rate of gelid cryotheum. Note that this stacks multiplicatively with the 1.5x speed modifier from earlier to reach up to 1,200% speed. The time to max is still 5 minutes without cryotheum cooling and 1 minute with cryotheum cooling because these speed boosts are applied immediately. The exotic coolants do not stack and running out after supplying them causes the machine to immediately shut down and void the current recipe. 

| Exotic Coolant | Input Rate | Speed Boost | Max Speed | Gelid Cryotheum |
| --------------- | --------------- | --------------- | --------------- | --------------- |
| None | 0 L/s | 1.0x | 150% | 250 - 375 L/s |
| Molten Infinity | 20 L/s | 2.0x | 300% | 500 - 750 L/s |
| Molten Spacetime | 20 L/s | 4.0x | 600% | 1,000 - 1,500 L/s |
| Molten Eternity | 20 L/s | 8.0x | 1,200% | 1,500 - 3,000 L/s |

title: changelog guide: Exo-Foundry
text:
# Exo-Foundry

The Exo-Foundry is a UEV tier multiblock for casting liquid metals into molds at a massive scale. The Exo-Foundry is a direct upgrade from the Mass Solidifier Mass Solidifier because it can run significantly faster with a higher energy discount and many more parallels. The exact values vary significantly with the amount and number of modules installed. There are seven modules in total and each one grants a unique bonus to the machine but there are only 2/3/4 slots depending on the tier of the structure. The modules can all be different, or potentially the same to stack bonuses. There are also four module pairings that offer one-time bonuses for even better performance. 

## Construction:
The Exo-Foundry is available in three tiers. The only structural difference between them is the magnetic chassis blocks and the only functional difference between them is the number of module slots (2/3/4). Buses/hatches may replace any primary Exo-Foundry casing anywhere on the structure. The minimum casing requirement supports up to 25 inputs for the 35 total molds. Multi-Amp and Laser Energy Hatches are supported, but the Exo-Foundry cannot overclock beyond the voltage tier of the energy hatch without the Hypercooler Hypercooler Casing or Heliocast Reinforcement Heliocast Reinforcement Casing modules. There is no maintenance or muffler hatch. Right-click the controller with a screwdriver to disable animations. Use the Multiblock Structure Hologram Projector Multiblock Structure Hologram Projector to visualize/build the structure with subchannel "chassis" to specify the tier of the magnetic chassis blocks.

Select which modules to use in the GUI of the controller and then use the Multiblock Structure Hologram Projector to build them. They appear as rings around the central column and their stats are summarized under "display machine information" in the GUI of the controller. The ordering has no effect on the operation of the machine. Remove modules by shift left-clicking them in the selection menu and then physically destroying them with a Vajra Vajra or other tool.

The Exo-Foundry runs at 150% speed and offers 16 parallels per voltage tier without any modules, as seen in the following table. That is slower, less efficient, and more restrictive than the Mass Solidifier at maximum speed, but those are only the base stats of the machine and are improved significantly with every installed module. The effective voltage for determining parallels is NOT capped by the tier of the energy hatch like overclocks are, but there must be multiple energy hatches regardless of the number of amps. 

In the following table, "SCB" refers to the Superdense Casting Basin modules, and "SCB+" refers to the same module with pairing bonuses, both of which will be explained later in this section.

The Heliocast Reinforcement Heliocast Reinforcement Casing and Sentient Overclock Sentient Overclocker Casing modules both increase the overclock factor of the machine which is a unique mechanic that simply increases the speed bonus with every overclock. For example, an imperfect overclock consumes 4x the power for 2x the speed but increasing the overclock factor by 0.35 causes the Exo-Foundry to consume 4x the power for 2.35x the speed instead. 

## Superdense Casting Basins Superdense Casting Basin Casing
The SCB module (UEV) adds 12 parallels per voltage tier on top of the base 16 parallels per voltage tier, and reduces the minimum number of casings by 36. That is a total of 28 parallels per voltage tier and enough space for 61 inputs for the 35 total molds. There is no limit on the amount of SCB modules per Exo-Foundry. The UC module (UXV) multiplies the power consumption by 4x, multiplies the speed by 2x, and increases the minimum number of casings by 20. Pairing the UC with the Hypercooler module unlocks Realized Potential which is a one-time bonus that allows eternity to be used as a coolant for up to 3 additional overclocks, multiplies the power consumption by 2x, and multiplies the speed by 2x.

There are four unique pairings of modules that provide additional bonuses to the Exo-Foundry. These have all been described in the module subsections above, but summarized here for reference. title: changelog guide: Exothermic Hearth
text:
# Exothermic Hearth

The Exothermic Hearth (ExH) is a ZPM tier multiblock for mass smelting dusts into ingots, crafting silicon boules, and heating up various materials. It replaces the previous Mega Electric Blast Furnace. The ExH is a direct upgrade from the Electric Blast Furnace Electric Blast Furnace because it offers up to 512 parallels, supports Multi-Amp and Laser Energy Hatches for serious overclocking, and has unlimited tier skips. That means it can run any recipe regardless of voltage tier as long as there is enough power and heat. The number of available parallels slowly increases up to 512 during activity and decreases back down to 256 while idle. Optionally, enable pyrotheum heating in the GUI of the controller to 6x the rate at which parallels are gained at the cost of 250-500 L/s of blazing pyrotheum. The ExH gains a 5% energy discount for every 900K over the recipe requirement and one perfect overclock for every 1,800K over the recipe requirement. The ExH only outperforms the Volcanus Volcanus if it can take full advantage of its 512 parallels (4+ overclocks).

## Construction:
The ExH has two tiered components. The heating coils determine the maximum tier of recipes, the energy discount, and the number of perfect overclocks. The glass determines the maximum tier of the energy hatch. UMV tier glass removes all restrictions. Buses/hatches may replace any hearth casing anywhere on the structure, except for the muffler hatch which is limited to the center casing on the top layer of the structure. Multi-amp and laser energy hatches are supported, but the latter requires at least UV tier glass. Use the Multiblock Structure Hologram Projector to visualize/build the structure with subchannels "coil" and "glass" to specify the tier of those components.

- 1 Maintenance Hatch (any hearth casing)Maintenance Hatch

- 0+ Input Bus (any hearth casing)Input Bus (ULV)
- 0+ Input Hatch (any hearth casing)Input Bus (ULV)
- 0+ Output Bus (any hearth casing)Output Bus (ULV)
- 0+ Output Hatch (any hearth casing)Output Hatch (ULV)

### Wallsharing:
ExHs may wallshare each of their sides to save on casings and buses/hatches. That does NOT include any of the heating coils or glass. 
## Usage:
The ExH is a direct upgrade from the Electric Blast Furnace because it offers up to 512 parallels, supports multi-amp and laser energy hatches for serious overclocking, and has unlimited tier skips. That means it can run any recipe regardless of voltage tier as long as there is enough power and heat. For example, a ZPM 256A laser energy hatch can run UIV recipes if the heat capacity is high enough. The glass tier only limits the voltage tier of the energy hatch, NOT the voltage tier of recipes.

The number of available parallels slowly increases up to 512 during activity and decreases back down to 256 while idle, as seen below. It takes 30 minutes of continuous activity to achieve the maximum 512 parallels but only 4 minutes and 16 seconds to lose it all. Optionally, enable pyrotheum heating in the GUI of the controller to 6x the rate at which parallels are gained at the cost of 250-500 L/s of blazing pyrotheum. The consumption rate scales linearly with the number of additional parallels, but it allows the ExH to achieve the maximum 512 parallels in just 5 minutes instead. Running out of blazing pyrotheum while pyrotheum heating is enabled causes the machine to immediately shut down and void the current recipe.

- +0.711 parallels per 5 seconds while active (pyrotheum heating disabled), 30 minutes to max
- +4.267 parallels per 5 seconds while active (pyrotheum heating enabled), 5 minutes to max
- -1 parallel per second while idle, 4.26 minutes to min

## Heat Capacity
Lastly, the ExH gains a 5% energy discount for every 900K over the recipe requirement and one perfect overclock for every 1,800K over the recipe requirement. There is also a +100K heat bonus for every voltage tier above MV.

title: changelog guide: High Temperature Gas-Cooled Reactor
text:
# High Temperature Gas-Cooled Reactor

The High Temperature Gas-Cooled Reactor (HTGR) is an IV tier multiblock that decays TRISO TRISO Fuel (Uranium 235) balls through fission for their valuable byproducts. The HTGR must be primed with at least 100 TRISO balls and 51,200L of helium to start processing, but having any less than the maximum 10,000 TRISO balls and 512,000L of helium reduces efficiency and increases power consumption. Optionally, supply IC2 coolant and/or distilled water to drastically accelerate the decay process and reduce the maximum duration from 1,000 seconds to only 10 seconds. The TRISO consumes up to 0.14% of the TRISO balls and 0.05% of the helium at the very beginning of each operation, but then uses as little as 1,536 EU/t to produce up to 5,000 L/t of hot coolant and 160,000 L/t of steam for the next 10 seconds. Burned out TRISO balls can be recycled in an Industrial Centrifuge for most of the original inputs back and a few additional outputs such as sunnarium, indium, lutetium dust, and lanthanum. The peak fuel throughput is 5,094 TRISO balls per hour.

The hot coolant is used by the Thermal Boiler Thermal Boiler, Large Heat Exchanger Large Heat Exchanger, or Whakawhiti Wera XL Whakawhiti Wera XL to produce superheated steam, or the Extreme Heat Exchanger to produce supercritical steam. The steam is then used to generate power in Large Steam Turbines. Expect upwards of 111A of LuV power at maximum efficiency.

The HTGR is very similar to the Thorium High Temperature Reactor (THTR). The difference is that the THTR runs for significantly longer and produces hardly any byproducts. In other words, use the HTGR for resources and the THTR for power. 

## Construction:
The HTGR consists of four individual structures. The exact locations of these structures are fixed in reference to the controller and all four are necessary for the structure to form. The large purple sphere is the reactor which has an input bus on top for TRISO balls and output bus on bottom for burned out TRISO balls Burned Out TRISO Fuel (Thorium). The tall vertical structure in the middle is the primary coolant tower which has an input hatch on the side for IC2 coolant and an output hatch on the top for hot coolant. The smaller vertical structure on the edge is the secondary coolant tower which has an input hatch near the top for distilled water and an output hatch near the bottom for steam. The helium input hatch, energy hatch, and maintenance hatch are all limited to the top three casings above the pump at the center of the structure. Multi-Amp and Laser Energy Hatches are not supported and there cannot be more than one regular energy hatch. Use the Multiblock Structure Hologram ProjectorMultiblock Structure Hologram Projector to visualize/build the structure. 

### Requires:
- 1 High Temperature Gas-cooled ReactorHigh Temperature Gas-cooled Reactor
- 273 Beryllium Integrated Reactor CasingBeryllium Integrated Reactor Casing
- 272 Pressure Containment CasingPressure Containment Casing
- 164 Tungsten Frame BoxTungsten Frame Box
- 162 Graphite Moderator CasingGraphite Moderator Casing
- 45 Tungstensteel Pipe CasingTungstensteel Pipe Casing
- 41 Insulated Fluid Pipe CasingInsulated Fluid Pipe Casing
- 30 Titanium Pipe CasingTitanium Pipe Casing
- 24 Cable CasingCable Casing
- 23 IV Machine CasingIV Machine Casing
- 20 Refined Graphite BlockRefined Graphite Block
- 17 Steel Pipe CasingSteel Pipe Casing
- 3 Pump Machine CasingPump Machine Casing
- 2 Motor Machine CasingMotor Machine Casing
- 1 Processor Machine CasingProcessor Machine Casing
- 1 Energy Hatch (any top casing on pump) ULV Energy Hatch
- 1 Maintenance Hatch (any top casing on pump) Maintenance Hatch
- 1 Input Bus (one for TRISO balls) Input Bus (ULV)
- 3 Input Hatch (one for IC2 coolant, one for distilled water, one for helium) Input Hatch (ULV)
- 1 Output Bus (one for burned out TRISO balls) Output Bus (ULV)
- 2 Output Hatch (one for hot coolant, one for steam) Output Hatch (ULV)

### Wallsharing:
HTGRs cannot wallshare any significant part of their structure due to the restrictions on the location of the buses/hatches and the inability to rotate or flip the controller. Not even the reactor portion can be shared because it is not perfectly symmetrical. 

## Usage:
The HTGR has two operating modes, listed below. Switch modes by right-clicking the controller with a screwdriver while the machine is idle.

- Normal - Stores TRISO balls and helium internally, and starts processing when the minimum conditions are met.
- Emptying - Returns all internally stored TRISO balls to the output bus.

The HTGR uses helium gas to stabilize the fission decay of TRISO balls inside the reactor. IC2 Coolant and distilled water are optional but highly recommended because they drastically accelerate the decay process to burn through fuel quicker. The end product is burned out TRISO balls which are recycled in an Industrial Centrifuge for some of the original resources back, and a few additional ones to be used elsewhere. If present, the IC2 coolant is converted into hot coolant and the distilled water is converted into steam at a rate proportional to the amount of TRISO balls and helium. 

## Fuel:
The HTGR uses TRISO balls (NOT pellets) for fuel. There are 9 different types in total, but they can all be used in the same machine at the same time if necessary. The minimum amount of fuel to begin processing is 100 TRISO balls, but having any less than the maximum 10,000 TRISO balls reduces the efficiency of the machine, as seen in the following equation and graph.

TRISO balls have their own material stats based on what they are made of. In the NEI tooltip, this is shown as "Properties: [x], [y], [z]" as shown by hovering here: kubatech:htgr_item_burnerd_triso_fuel:3. These properties are Base ($$b$$), Multiplier ($$m$$), and Exponent ($$e$$) respectively, and are directly related to the power generation, and processing time as is detailed further into this chapter:

The efficiency cannot be increased while the machine is active and cannot exceed 100%. Maintenance issues reduce the maximum efficiency by 20% each. 

 

The efficiency of the HGTR is directly proportional to the duration of each operation, and the stats of the material used, as seen in the following equation.

  Where:
  $$\eta$$: Processing Time Modifier

  Where:
  $$\eta$$: Processing Time Modifier
  $$e$$: Exponent statistic of used TRISO ball

The efficiency of the HGTR is also directly proportional to the amount of TRISO balls consumed/burned per operation, as seen in the following equation. That is a maximum of 14.15 TRISO balls per operation, but the rate (without coolant) is fixed at 51 per hour regardless of the duration since both variables scale linearly with efficiency.

The HGTR outputs the same number of burned out TRISO balls. Centrifuge the TRISO balls for a variety of useful byproducts, as seen in the following tables. Most of the inputs are returned for making more fuel and there are a few additional outputs to be used elsewhere. Most notably, glowstone TRISO balls produce sunnarium, silver TRISO balls produce indium, thorium TRISO balls produce lutetium, and caesium TRISO balls produce lanthanum. 

## Coolant:
The only mandatory coolant in the HGTR is helium. The minimum amount of helium to begin processing is 51,200L but having any less than the maximum 512,000L increases the power consumption of the machine, as seen in the following equation. The maximum power consumption is 61,440 EU/t and the minimum power consumption is 1,536 EU/t. The HGTR consumes exactly 0.05% of the current helium at the start of each operation so the reactor needs to be slowly refilled over time.

Optionally, supply IC2 coolant and/or distilled water to drastically accelerate the decay process of the TRISO balls. IC2 coolant skips 7% of the total duration per second, distilled water skips 3% of the total duration per second, and together they skip 10% of the total duration per second. That means a full 1,000 second operation can finish in under 10 seconds and still consumes the same amount of TRISO balls. Although terribly inefficient for power generation, this is extremely useful for breeding and harvesting byproducts. The base 51 TRISO balls per hour increases up to 5,094 TRISO balls per hour.

The amount of IC2 coolant and distilled water used by the HGTR depends on the current amount of TRISO balls and the current amount of helium, as seen in the following table. The IC2 coolant is converted into hot coolant at a perfect 1:1 ratio while the distilled water is converted into steam at a 1:160 ratio. 

## Power:
Despite high sustainment costs, the HGTR outputs an impressive 5,000 L/t of hot coolant and 160,000 L/t of steam for up to 10 seconds per operation. The throughput of the coolant alone is slightly greater than the Thorium High Temperature Reactor Thorium High Temperature Reactor, 72x greater than the output of a Fluid Reactor, and 26x greater than the output of a Deep Earth Heating Pump Deep Earth Heating Pump. It is also more than enough to generate supercritical (SC) steam in an Extreme Heat Exchanger and superheated (SH) steam in a Thermal Boiler, Large Heat Exchanger, or Whakawhiti Wera XL. The only problem is that so much hot coolant requires many heat exchangers and a massive supply of distilled water, as seen in the following table. The EHE is recommended over the WWXL because the supercritical steam yields more power overall, even if it is more machines to build.

Conversion Ratios

- 1 L/t Hot Coolant = 200 L/t SC Steam (EHE) or 200 L/t SH Steam (Thermal Boiler, LHE, WWXL)
- 200 L/t SC Steam = 200 L/t SH Steam = 200 L/t Steam
- 160 L/t Steam = 1 L/t Distilled Water

Though the output of hot coolant and steam is up to 5,000 L/t and 160,000 L/t respectively, the output rate is directly related to the stats of the TRISO balls being used via the following equation:

  Where:
    $$b$$: Material Base Stat
    $$m$$: Material Multiplier Stat
    $$e$$: Material Exponent Stat

title: changelog guide: L.A.T.E.X.
text:
# L.A.T.E.X.

The Laminated Application and Thermal Enclosure eXpert (LATEX), the mouthful that it is, is an HV tier multiblock for coating cables. The LATEX is a direct upgrade from the singleblock assembler for cable coating because it runs at 200% speed, only uses 85% of the EU/t normally required, and offers 8 parallels per voltage tier. There is also an additive 6.25% rubber discount based on the tier of the item pipe casings and the unique opportunity to insert an elastic singularity inside the controller to double the amount of parallels, gain another 25% rubber discount, and unlock the ability to use multi-amp and laser energy hatches. 

## Construction:
The LATEX has one tiered component. The item pipe casings determine the overall rubber discount of the machine. Buses/hatches may replace any casing anywhere on the structure. The glass must be tiered for the structure to form but has no effect on the operation of the machine. Multi-amp and laser energy hatches are not supported unless there is an elastic singularity in the controller, but there can be multiple regular energy hatches for overclocking. title: changelog guide: Large Hadron Collider
text:
# Large Hadron Collider

The Large Hadron Collider (LHC) is a UV tier multiblock that accelerates charged particles and collides them for new particle outputs. The LHC is required for progression in various stages of UV and beyond. The LHC gains "efficiency" bonuses based on how many cycles have been completed previously.

## Construction:
The LHC consists of two rings. The smaller one is the particle accelerator, which consumes power to increase the overall beam energy of the machine. The larger ring is the particle collider, which produces new particles from the collision energy of the beam. The LHC has four modules available, and each goes on a designated side of the structure. The difference between them is the type of particles that they produce in their Filtered Beam Output HatchFiltered Beam Output Hatch. Multi-Amp and Laser Energy Hatches are supported. The neonite blocks are optional and can be any color. Use the Multiblock Structure Hologram ProjectorMultiblock Structure Hologram Projector to visualize/build the structure where the number of the projectors held in a single stack determines how many modules to build.
### Base Structure Requires:
- 1 Large Hadron ColliderLarge Hadron Collider
- 5,664 Collider CasingCollider Casing
- 73 Neonite (any color, optional) Neonite
- 20 Shielded Accelerator GlassShielded Accelerator Glass
- 16 Shielded Accelerator CasingShielded Accelerator Casing
- 1 Beam Input HatchBeam Input Hatch
- 1+ Energy Hatch (any collider casing) ULV Energy Hatch

### Electromagnetism Module Requires:
- 523 Collider CasingCollider Casing
- 148 Charged Matter Sensor CasingCollider Casing
- 126 Shielded Accelerator GlassShielded Accelerator Glass
- 11 Neonite (any color, optional) Neonite
- 2 Filtered Beam Output HatchFiltered Beam Output Hatch

### Weak Interaction Module Requires:
- 515 Collider CasingCollider Casing
- 160 Advanced Total Lepton Assimilation Snare CasingAdvanced Total Lepton Assimilation Snare Casing
- 126 Shielded Accelerator GlassShielded Accelerator Glass
- 13 Neonite (any color, optional) Neonite
- 2 Filtered Beam Output HatchFiltered Beam Output Hatch

### Strong Force Module Requires:
- 517 Collider CasingCollider Casing
- 158 Absolute Lattice Integrated Chromodynamic Encapsulator CasingAbsolute Lattice Integrated Chromodynamic Encapsulator Casing
- 140 Shielded Accelerator GlassShielded Accelerator Glass
- 11 Neonite (any color, optional) Neonite
- 2 Filtered Beam Output HatchFiltered Beam Output Hatch

### Gravity Module Requires:
- 511 Collider CasingCollider Casing
- 144 Localized Horizon Curvature Binder CasingLocalized Horizon Curvature Binder Casing
- 126 Shielded Accelerator GlassShielded Accelerator Glass
- 17 Neonite (any color, optional) Neonite
- 2 Filtered Beam Output HatchFiltered Beam Output Hatch

## Total Requirements:
- 1 Large Hadron ColliderLarge Hadron Collider
- 7,730 Collider CasingCollider Casing
- 538 Shielded Accelerator GlassShielded Accelerator Glass
- 160 Advanced Total Lepton Assimilation Snare CasingAdvanced Total Lepton Assimilation Snare Casing
- 158 Absolute Lattice Integrated Chromodynamic Encapsulator CasingAbsolute Lattice Integrated Chromodynamic Encapsulator Casing
- 148 Charged Matter Sensor CasingCollider Casing
- 144 Localized Horizon Curvature Binder CasingLocalized Horizon Curvature Binder Casing
- 125 Neonite (any color, optional) Neonite
- 16 Shielded Accelerator CasingShielded Accelerator Casing
- 8 Filtered Beam Output HatchFiltered Beam Output Hatch

### Wallsharing:
Though an LHC can *technically* be wallshared, it is not advisable for many reasons, mainly the fact that you should never really need more than one!

## Usage:
The LHC has two modes of use, Accelerator Mode and Collider Mode. The controller includes a GUI for configuring a Target Beam Energy (eV), and Max Acceleration Cycles. These parameters cannot be changed in operation of the machine, or it will shut down.

In the GUI, there are two extra panels that can be used. One is a calculator, allowing the user to tinker with different hypothetical input and target values. The other is a Particle Probability Table, where a target Collision Energy can be provided, and probabilities of each particle are given for each module on the LHC.

### Accelerator Mode:
The Accelerator Mode is used to accelerate the beam in the smaller LHC ring. It increases the energy stored in the beam by the following equation, until either the target beam energy is reached, or the maximum number of cycles is reached. This operation runs once per second.

If the target beam energy is reached, the beam rate is multiplied by 1.3 repeatedly on subsequent cycles. The power of the machine starts at 1A of UV per beam rate, and increases quadratically with the number of completed cycles as below. When the target beam cycle count is reached, the mode will automatically switch to Collider Mode. Since the power scales based on the cycles, the more cycles run the closer the machine gets to being a perfect 4/4 overclock.

  Where:
  - $$R_0 = $$ Initial Rate
  - $$a = $$ Multiplication Factor
  - $$N = $$ Cycle Count

Hover on the above equation for a tooltip showing what each term means.

### Beams:
For those of you that have used the cyclotron in the past, you may notice that the LHC does not output particles as simple "items". Instead, they are now internally stored as "particle packets" that exist within beams, similar to the concept used for data packets in the Research Station. These packets have four attributes; type, energy, rate, and focus. Focus is not used in the LHC or Beam Crafter directly.

Beams are transferred using the Beam PipeBeam Pipe from an output hatch to their destination.

### Collider Mode:
The Collider Mode is automatically switched to upon either the target beam energy being reached, or the max cycle count being reached. The __collision energy__ is simply $$\text{Beam Energy} \times 2$$. The particles in the output beam are determined by two factors:
1. The installed modules on the multi
2. The collision energy of the beam

Assuming you have the correct modules installed for a particle, any particles with a rest mass _lower_ than the collision energy have a chance to be in the output beam. The rest mass of particles can be found through NEI in the tooltips of the particles. NEI will also show any required modules to get that specific output. Multiple modules may allow for the creation of the same particle. The Filtered Beam Output HatchFiltered Beam Output Hatch can be used to blacklist certain particles from appearing in the output beam.

Once your beams are made, you can use beamline pipes to route them to their destination, usually a Beam Crafter Beam Crafter.

----------
For a more detailed look at both the LHC, and the accompanying Beam Crafter, feel free to take a look at the video guide produced by the author himself.

If you want an even more detailed look, head on over to the wiki page, where the wiki team have written an amount of documentation that would make even CERN blush!

# Large Neutralization Engine

The Large Neutralization Engine (LNE) is an EV tier multiblock acid generator for higher voltage tier requirements. The LNE is a direct upgrade from the singleblock acid generators because it offers up to 500% efficiency, can output more than 1A of power, and has configurable fuel consumption rates. Bases can be used to improve the efficiency of the machine. Power is extracted via a dynamo hatch on the back, and Multi-Amp and Laser Energy Hatches are supported. The LNE has its own danger system in Toxic Residue. If this ever exceeds the capacity of the controller, the multiblock will explode!. Save on fuel by automatically toggling the LNE with an RS latch connected to a Lapotronic Supercapacitor Lapotronic Supercapacitor

## Construction:
The LNE has one tiered component. The "main casing" used determines the machine's tier, which in turn determines the Base Decay and Capacity of the machine. The input hatches, input buses, dynamo, and toxic residue sensor hatch (to be explained) may replace any of the "main" casings. Use the Multiblock Structure Hologram Projector Multiblock Structure Hologram Projector to visualize/build the structure.
| Tier | Casing |

| 1 | Strengthened Inanimate Machine Casing Strengthened Inanimate Machine Casing |
| 2 | Precise Stationary Machine Casing Precise Stationary Machine Casing |

## Usage:
The LNE generates power from acids. A wide variety of acids are available, and many of the available acids have had their EU values tweaked, so it is well worth double checking some of your old favourites. title: changelog guide: Nanochip Assembly Complex
text:
# Nanochip Assembly Complex

The Nanochip Assembly Complex (NAC) is a UEV tier multiblock for mass circuit assembling. The NAC is a direct upgrade from the Circuit Assembly Line Circuit Assembly Line for crystal, wetware, bioware, optical, pico, and quantum circuits because it offers unlimited parallels, runs 2/2 perfect overclocks, and does not start processing unless there is enough energy available for the full duration of a recipe. The NAC also supports Multi-Amp and Laser Energy Hatches for incredibly high throughput.

All processing and circuit assembling is done by the modules that surround the control room at the center of the structure. There are 11 unique modules to choose from and 12 module slots. A few of the modules have their own unique challenges or costs, but most are relatively straightforward. Items and circuit components (CCs) are routed between modules with vacuum conveyor hatches and vacuum conveyor pipes, which have unlimited storage capacity and throughput. Crafting enough of the same circuit type calibrates the NAC to that particular circuit line and grants additional bonuses. 

## Construction:
The NAC consists of a large control room surrounded by 12 module slots. The control room is for both the inputs and outputs to the machine while the modules are for processing circuit components (CCs). Multi-amp and laser energy hatches are supported, but there can only be one and it must be inside or under the control room. Power is automatically distributed from the control room to all modules in the order that it is requested, similar to the Space ElevatorSpace Elevator. The only exception is the Nanochip Assembly MatrixNanochip Assembly Matrix which has a lower priority than all other modules for filling its energy buffer. There is no maintenance hatch. Use the Multiblock Structure Hologram ProjectorMultiblock Structure Hologram Projector to visualize/build the structure.

Modules are their own multiblocks with their own controller and construction requirements. Replace one of the Nanochip Mesh Interface CasingNanochip Mesh Interface Casing on the top edge of any module slot and use the Multiblock Structure Hologram Projector to visualize/build them. They can face any direction, but cannot be built upside-down. If done correctly, the module's controller should say "Connected to Main Complex" once the NAC is enabled. 
### Requires:
- 1 Nanochip Assembly ComplexNanochip Assembly Complex
- 3,956 Nanochip Reinforcement CasingNanochip Reinforcement Casing
- 2,226 Nanochip Complex GlassNanochip Complex Glass
- 1,708-1,720 Nanochip Mesh Interface CasingNanochip Mesh Interface Casing
- 721 Nanochip Computational Matrix CasingNanochip Computational Matrix Casing
- 53 Naquadah Frame BoxNaquadah Frame Box
- 32 Nanochip Firewall Projection CasingNanochip Firewall Projection Casing
- 1 Energy Hatch (any side interface casing in control room) EV 4A Wireless Energy Hatch
- 0+ Input Bus (any side interface casing in control room) Input Bus (ULV)
- 0+ Output Bus (any side interface casing in control room) Output Bus (ULV)

## Vacuum Conveyor System
Unique to the NAC are Vacuum Conveyor Input (VCI) Vacuum Conveyor Input and Vacuum Conveyor Output (VCO) Vacuum Conveyor Output hatches which move items or CCs between modules. These are similar to optical transmission and reception hatches because they must be colored to work and the connections must be 1-to-1. The hatches are machine-specific so they cannot transfer CCs between NACs. The vacuum conveyor pipes that join the hatches must be colored as well and can bend freely. It is highly recommended to use the gregtech:gt.metaitem.01:32468gregtech:gt.metaitem.01:32468 for coloring everything.

Both hatches can hold up to 16 unique item stacks at a time with no upper limit on capacity and no transfer limit between connections. This allows for incredibly high throughput that easily scales into the end game. Items stored inside the hatches cannot be interacted with directly, but there is an option to empty/unpackage stored items to an AE2 storage cell or to simply delete all stored items. Fluids do not enter the vacuum conveyor system and must be routed directly to the module(s) that use them.

There are two ways to properly filter or split items to ensure that they are routed to the correct module. The first is filtering everything before it enters the NAC and the second is using the Nanopart SplitterNanopart Splitter module. The latter uses a module slot but it allows for custom routing based on input color, output color, item type, and/or supplied redstone level. 

----------

## Modules:
The NAC only ever packages and unpackages circuit components (CCs) on a fixed 5 second cycle. The modules are what actually process and assemble the circuits. There are 11 unique modules to choose from and 12 module slots around the control room, but not all modules are required and there is no limit on the number of each one. Despite the additional processing, modules are a direct upgrade from the Circuit Assembly Line because they have unlimited parallels, run 2/2 perfect overclocks down to 5 seconds for every voltage tier above the recipe tier, and do not start processing unless their energy buffer is large enough for the craft. That means they have incredibly high throughput and cannot powerfail or void items. Note that the overclocks are calculated before parallels to increase the speed of longer recipes.

The general workflow of the NAC is listed below. The image is also provided for reference although it is a slight oversimplification since not everything (ie. spliced frameboxes) is routed to the Nanochip Assembly Matrix. See the calibration section below for a more detailed walkthrough of setups. 
1. Insert items through a colored input bus (regular or stocking) in the control room
2. The NAC packages the items into CCs and transfers them to a VCO hatch of the same color
3. Filter the packaged CCs with a Nanopart Splitter module if not done beforehand to route them to the correct module.
4. The modules turn the packaged CCs into processed components (PCs) which cannot be unpackaged or leave the NAC
5. Join the PCs in the Nanochip Assembly Matrix to create circuit CCs and route them back to the control room
6. The NAC unpackages the circuit CCs and transfers them to an output bus for retrieval

  
    An overview of the Nanochip Assembly Complex by Fox
  

## Nanochip Assembly Matrix Nanochip Assembly Matrix

The Nanochip Assembly Matrix assembles circuit CCs from processed components (PCs). This module is always the final step before sending the circuit CCs to the control room to be unpackaged into real circuits. The Nanochip Assembly Matrix has the lowest priority out of all the modules for filling its energy buffer and the 2/2 perfect overclocks down to 5 seconds is based on recipe casing tier rather than recipe voltage tier. Both are displayed in NEI and are often different from each other.

The inputs to the Nanochip Assembly Matrix can be in separate VCIs and do not all need to be the same color. There is also no restriction on the ordering of components despite recipes appearing identical to Assembly Line recipes. The output color is based on the first ingredient which is often the circuit board or encasement PC.

- 1 Nanochip Assembly MatrixNanochip Assembly Matrix
- 25 Nanochip Reinforcement CasingNanochip Reinforcement Casing
- 24 Nanochip Complex GlassNanochip Complex Glass
- 20 Component Assembly Line Casing (Tiered) Component Assembly Line Casing (LV)
- 12 Naquadah Alloy Frame BoxNaquadah Alloy Frame Box
- 8 Nanochip Mesh Interface CasingNanochip Mesh Interface Casing
- 3 Naquadah Alloy SheetmetalNaquadah Alloy Sheetmetal
- 0+ Vacuum Conveyor Input (any base interface casing) Vacuum Conveyor Input
- 0+ Vacuum Conveyor Output (any base interface casing) Vacuum Conveyor Output

| Pico | UEV   |

## Nanopart Splitter Nanopart Splitter

The Nanopart Splitter filters and organizes all CCs. Open the rules manager through the GUI of the controller to set custom routing rules based on input color, output color, item type, and/or supplied redstone level. At the very least, there must be one or more input colors selected and one or more output colors selected. The Nanopart Splitter cannot filter purely based on item type or even the unpackaged versions of CCs. If there are multiple valid filters for a single item type, it is split evenly between them.

The Splitter Redstone Input is an optional hatch that replaces any nanochip mesh interface casing on the top of the structure and acts as an external redstone receiver. The strength of the incoming redstone signal is associated with the configured channel in the GUI of the hatch for managing rules.

## Part Preparation Apparatus Part Processing Apparatus

The Part Preparation Apparatus processes SMD CCs. This module is required for all circuit lines.

## Full-Board Immersion Device Full-Board Immersion Device

The Full-Board Immersion Device processes circuit board CCs by cleaning them in their corresponding immersion fluid. Recipes do not consume any of the immersion fluid but rather increase the impurity up to 100%. A higher impurity increases the power consumption of the module up to 300% until it is drained, either manually through the GUI of the controller or by triggering the auto-flush at a configured percentage level. The auto-flush must be between 1-100% so the tank eventually needs to be refilled.

There are four immersion fluids available, but the internal tank can only hold one at a time. Supply between 500,000L and 1,000,000L of immersion fluid through a regular input hatch to get started. Excess immersion fluid is NOT consumed and having any less than the maximum increases the rate at which impurity increases, as seen in the following equation. The total item count carries over between iterations so impurity is added once every 1,000 items regardless of recipe or batch size.

## Ultra-High Energy Etching Array Ultra-high Energy Etching Array

The Ultra-High Energy Etching Array processes crystal CCs with its own laser source hatch. In a fully calibrated crystal NAC, the power consumption of the module is divided by $$\log_4(\text{Amps})$$ of the laser source hatch and the duration of recipes are divided by $$\text{Voltage Tier} - 9$$. This module is not required for the optical or pico/quantum circuit lines.

## Accelerated Biological Coordinator Accelerated Biological Coordinator

The Accelerated Biological Coordinator processes living CCs. It does not consume any growth catalyst medium in a fully calibrated wetware NAC, and does not consume any sterilized bio catalyst medium in a fully calibrated bioware NAC. This module is not required for the crystal, optical, or pico/quantum circuit lines.

## Optically Optimized Organizer Optically Optimized Organizer

The Optically Optimized Organizer processes optical CCs by cleaning them in two types of purified water between grade 3 and grade 8, inclusive. Each purified water grants a bonus to the module, as seen in the following table. Similar effects stack multiplicatively with one another and all effects are applied twice in a fully calibrated optical NAC. This module is not required for the crystal, wetware, bioware, or pico/quantum circuit lines. 

| Water | Cost | Bonus |
| --------------- | --------------- | --------------- |
| Grade 3 | 1,000 L/s | x0.8 Water Cost |
| Grade 4 | 800 L/s | x0.6 Water Cost |
| Grade 5 | 800 L/s | x0.9 Duration |

----------
## Calibration:
The NAC records every circuit crafted in the Nanochip Assembly Matrix (NAM) to track the frequency of each circuit type out of the past 100,000 circuits. The circuit history is only updated once every 1,000 circuits and replaces the oldest information first. View the current circuit history and the progress towards the next 1,000 circuits through the GUI of the controller.

Once enough of the same circuit type is crafted, the NAC is calibrated to that circuit line and gains up to three stacking bonuses, as seen in the following tables. Only one calibration can be active at a time and higher tiers have higher priority over lower ones. Every calibration tier has its own unique prefix that is added to the name of the machine inside the GUI of the controller to help identify the one that is currently active. It is recommended to build one NAC per circuit line to maximize the calibration bonuses. 

The specifics on calibration are very specific to each circuit type, and are too detailed to explain here, so take a look at the NAC Wiki Page for more information!

title: changelog guide: Spinmatron-2737
text:
# Spinmatron-2737

The Spinmatron-2737 is a ZPM tier multiblock for mass centrifuging dusts, liquids, and other items into their sub components or constituent elements. In standard mode, the Spinmatron is a direct upgrade from the Industrial Centrifuge Industrial Centrifuge because it runs at 300% speed, only uses 70% of the EU/t normally required, and offers 4 parallels per sum of turbine tier. Non-huge turbines contribute fewer parallels and should be avoided. It also has unlimited tier skips which mean it can run any recipe regardless of voltage. The Spinmatron requires $$\text{Recipe Tier} \times 10 L/s$$ of kerosene to function OR the same amount of biocatalyzed propulsion fluid to further multiply the number of parallels by 1.25.

The Spinmatron also has three modes (Light, Standard, or Heavy) which affect its performance and capabilities. Light mode grants a +100% speed bonus but the maximum recipe tier is limited to $$\text{Voltage Tier} - 3$$. Standard Mode is described above. Heavy Mode divides the number of parallels by 32, requires a T3 structure, and requires biocatalyzed propulsion fluid. Heavy mode should only be used in the cases that specifically require it. 

## Construction:
The Spinmatron has four structure tiers correlating to the material of the frame boxes and central rotor blocks. Each structure tier grants 2 additional turbine slots inside the controller for increasing the maximum number of parallels. Buses/hatches may replace any vibration-safe casingVibration-Safe Casing anywhere on the structure. The glass can be any tier and has no effect on the operation of the machine. Multi-amp and Laser Energy Hatches are supported, but overclocks are limited to hatch tier + 1. Use a screwdriver on the controller to disable animations. Use the Multiblock Structure Hologram ProjectorMultiblock Structure Hologram Projector to visualize/build the structure with subchannel "glass" to specify the tier of the glass and the number of projectors held in a single stack to determine the overall structure tier.

The turbines themselves do NOT go in the rotor assemblies. Instead, place them in the controller under the chamber controller settings. They will still visually appear in the rotor assemblies without actually being placed there. Right-click the controller with a screwdriver to switch between static and animated turbine textures. The chamber controller settings also have the option to enable T2 biocatalyzed propulsion fluid; the Spinmatron does not automatically detect when it is present inside the machine instead of kerosene. 

### Requires:
- 1 Spinmatron-2737Spinmatron-2737
- 550-711 Vibration-Safe CasingVibration-Safe Casing
- 264 SC Turbine CasingSC Turbine Casing
- 160 PBI Pipe CasingPBI Pipe Casing
- 144 Chamber GrateChamber Grate
- 81 Tiered Glass (any) bartworks:BW_GlasBlocks
- 56 Central Rotor Block (tiered by multi tier) Block of Naquadah Alloy
- 54 IsaMill GearboxIsaMill Gearbox
- 24 Turbine ShaftTurbine Shaft
- 9 Frame Box (tiered by multi tier) Pikyonium 64B Frame Box
- 8 Rotor Assembly Rotor Assembly
- 1+ Energy Hatch (any vibration-safe casing) ULV Energy Hatch
- 1 Maintenance Hatch (any vibration-safe casing) Maintenance Hatch
- 0+ Input Bus (any vibration-safe casing) Input Bus (ULV)
- 0+ Input Hatch (any vibration-safe casing) Input Hatch (ULV)
- 0+ Output Bus (any vibration-safe casing) Output Bus (ULV)
- 0+ Output Hatch (any vibration-safe casing) Output Hatch (ULV)
### Wallsharing:
Spinmatrons may wallshare each of their sides to save on casings, rotor assemblies, and buses/hatches. However, that does not include the turbines themselves because they are stored inside the controller. 

## Usage:
In standard mode, the Spinmatron is a direct upgrade from the Industrial Centrifuge because it runs at 300% speed, only uses 70% of the EU/t normally required, and offers 4 parallels per sum of turbine tier. Huge turbines are the most effective since large/normal/small turbines only contribute 75%/50%/25% of their tier value to the overall sum. For example, a Spinmatron with two huge adamantium turbines (Tier 10) has a total of 4 x (10+10) = 80 parallels.

The Spinmatron has three operating modes, listed below. Change modes under "display machine information" in the GUI of the controller. Light mode is excellent for lower tier recipes such as combs and impure dusts. Standard mode is ideal for higher tier recipes above the $$\text{Voltage Tier} - 3$$ restriction. And heavy mode should only be used in the cases that specifically require it.

- Light Mode - Grants a +100% speed bonus, but the maximum recipe tier is limited to $$\text{Voltage Tier} - 3$$.
- Standard Mode - No change to the original description.
- Heavy Mode - Divides parallels by 32, requires at least a T3 structure, and requires biocatalyzed propulsion fluid instead of kerosene.

title: changelog guide: Steam Hearth
text:
# Steam Hearth

The Steam Hearth is a Steam tier multiblock for smelting, blasting, and smoking raw materials. The Steam Hearth is a direct upgrade from the singleblock steam furnace because it runs at 125% speed, only uses 62.5% of the steam normally required, and offers 8 parallels. There are two tiers of the machine: basic (T1) and high-pressure (T2). As with the other steam-age multiblocks, the high-pressure version consumes twice the amount of steam to run twice as fast. There are also three modes to pick from. The default Smelting mode can process any recipe without any restrictions or additional benefits. The Blasting mode restricts the machine to ores/metals for twice the speed and steam usage. The Smoking mode restricts the machine to food items for twice the speed and steam usage. The Steam Hearth is superseded by the Multi Smelter Multi Smelter in HV. 

## Construction:
The only structural difference between the basic and high-pressure Steam Hearth is the material of the casings. Steam is only accepted through a Steam Hatch Steam Hatch (NOT an input hatch), much like other steam tier multiblocks. The steam input and output bus do not auto-push or auto-pull from adjacent inventories and therefore require hoppers, EnderIO item conduits, or conveyor modules for automation. Use the Multiblock Structure Hologram Projector Multiblock Structure Hologram Projector to visualize/build the structure where the number of projectors held in a single stack determines the tier of the machine (1=Basic, 2=High Pressure).

Assuming plates are made in a Steam Forge Hammer Steam Forge Hammer and rods are made with a file, a basic Steam Hearth (with the necessary hatches) requires 395 bronze ingots and 9 brick blocks to build. A high-pressure Steam Hearth requires 359 steel ingots, 63 bronze ingots, and 3 brick blocks to build. 
### Requires:

__Basic (T1) Requires:__
  - 1 Steam HearthSteam Hearth
  - 2-6 Bronze Plated BricksBronze Plated Bricks
  - 4 Bronze Gear Box CasingBronze Gear Box Casing
  - 4 Bronze Pipe CasingBronze Pipe Casing
  - 3 Bronze Firebox CasingBronze Firebox Casing
  - 1+ Steam HatchSteam Hatch
  - 1+ Input Bus (Steam)Input Bus (Steam)
  - 1+ Output Bus (Steam)Output Bus (Steam)

__High-Pressure (T2) Requires:__
  - 1 Steam HearthSteam Hearth
  - 2-6 Solid Steel Machine CasingSolid Steel Machine Casing
  - 4 Steel Gear Box CasingSteel Gear Box Casing
  - 4 Steel Pipe CasingSteel Pipe Casing
  - 3 Steel Firebox CasingSteel Firebox Casing
  - 1+ Steam HatchSteam Hatch
  - 1+ Input Bus (Steam)Input Bus (Steam)
  - 1+ Output Bus (Steam)Output Bus (Steam)

### Wallsharing:
Steam Hearths may wallshare each of their sides to save on casings and buses/hatches. This is highly recommended because it saves a significant amount of bronze and steel. Sharing also works with other steam tier multiblocks that use the same type of casing. 

## Usage:
The Steam Hearth is a direct upgrade from the singleblock steam furnace because it runs at 125% speed, only uses 62.5% of the steam normally required, and offers 8 parallels. Upgrading to high-pressure (T2) doubles both the processing speed and steam consumption, as seen in the following table. Expect to use the Steam Hearth up to HV because of its large bonuses over singleblock machines.

The Steam Hearth has three unique modes, listed below, to further increase the throughput of the machine by specializing in particular recipes. Notice that these modes mimic the vanilla furnace, blast furnace, and smoker. Switch modes in the GUI of the controller, or by using a screwdriver on the controller.

- Smelting - No restrictions or additional benefits. The default universal mode.
- Blasting - Restricted to ores/metals for twice the speed and steam consumption.
- Smoking - Restricted to raw foods for twice the speed and steam consumption.

The following tables summarize the steam consumption and speed for both tiers of the Steam Hearth and the three different modes. For reference, a vanilla furnace smelts 0.10 items per second and a vanilla blast furnace/smoker smelts 0.20 items per second. 
### __Basic (T1)__
|  | Smelting | Blasting | Smoking |
| --------------- | --------------- | --------------- | --------------- |
| Max Steam | 800 L/s | 1,600 L/s | 1,600 L/s |
| Max Speed | 0.78 Items/s | 1.54 Items/s | 1.54 Items/s |

### __High-Pressure (T2)__

title: changelog guide: Baubles
text:
# Baubles
In an effort to consolidate the inventory, the __Tinker's Inventory Tab__ has been disabled. To accommodate this change, the following additions have been made:

- Added new __universal__ bauble slots, which accept _most_ of the baubles in the game

- Added the ability for set Tinker's items to be put inside Bauble slots:
- - Travel Belt - slot type: universal
- - Travel Glove - slot type: universal
- - Heart Canisters - custom slots that stack up to 10!

- Moved the ability to equip torches and blocks into Custom Cosmetic Armor - you can now wear your dirt hat in style! This also works with Dynamic Lighting

  
    An example of some baubles in their new homes! *Ranzu says hi!*

title: changelog guide: Better Grave Recovery
text:
# Better Grave Recovery
Keep dying to infernal mobs and sick of rearranging your inventory?

__Say less__

The OpenBlocks graves Gravestone have been reworked to work like modern gravestones!

Retrieving your items can now either be done by Left Mouse Button, or by Shift + Right Mouse Button with an empty hand. All your extra backpacks, and tools will be properly ordered as they were before your untimely death! This also includes auto-equipping all baubles, armor, and backpacks!

Right clicking a grave with an empty hand will show a death message associated with how the player died. Other players will not be able to accidentally open your grave

> [!NOTE]
> The old system of dropping on the floor is still available, and is achieved by right clicking whilst holding a shovel

title: changelog guide: Bigger Input Buses
text:
# Bigger Input Buses
There are two main changes being made to larger sized input/output buses as outlined below

# Higher Tier Input Buses

  
    The UI of a UHV Input Bus
  

In exchange for a sacrifice of Super Buses, you can now craft Input and Output Buses right the way up to UHV!

Following on from previous buses, the new ones will have n2 slots, where __n__ is the voltage tier (ULV=1)

Super buses already made/placed will remain, however will be uncraftable.

# Quantum/Compressed Buses
As part of a general revamp for non-AE2 logistics, a new set of input/output buses have been added! The Quantum Bus Quantum Input Bus (UMV) and the Compressed Bus Compressed Input Bus (ULV) are more enhanced equivalents of "regular" I/O buses in that they can now hold more than a stack per slot!

title: changelog guide: Chaos Locator
text:
# Chaos Locator
As many lategame players are aware, flying to the Chaos Guardian location is a long and painful endeavour, not to mention the hundreds of chunks generated by getting there!

Chaos Guardians always spawn on Chaos Islands, which generate at x and z coordinates that are both multiples of 10,000 (such as x=10,000 and z=0). With the Chaos Locator Chaos Locator, this is a problem of the past!

Simply using this item will allow the player to enter two numbers for x and z in the GUI, and will teleport the player to (10,000 x X-Coord , 10,000 x Z-Coord), so no more pain (apart from the beast that awaits you there...)

This even works cross-dimensionally!

title: changelog guide: Combo Keybinds
text:
# Combo Keybinds
Do you like to have every keybind set at once, but hate having to rely on strange buttons such as NUMPAD=? Do you have a smaller factor keyboard and just don't have enough keys to keep up with all the new options?

Now this is a thing of the past, as we have combination keybinds! This massively increases the amount of __reasonable__ keybinds you can have at once!

  
    An example of some combo keybinds!
  

> [!NOTE]
> Combo Keybinds do not work in interfaces. This is a limitation due to the order of handling within GUIs themselves and is unfortunately unavoidable

title: changelog guide: Cover Changes
text:
# Cover Changes
A few changes have been made to the use of Covers for both GregTech machines and their pipes and cables. They are outlined below

# Breaking Covers on Machines
Sometimes the smallest changes can feel the largest!

Breaking a block with a cover on will now drop the cover if holding Shift whilst breaking. Just breaking will keep the same behaviour

# Dyed Glass Covers
Ever wished you could add **dyed glass** (or other translucent covers) onto your pipes and machines? Well now you can!

By crafting an AE2 Facade with your favourite colour of dyed glass and placing it on your:
- Pipes
- Cables
- Frames
- Machines

# Renaming
Though a minor change, the Advanced Redstone Receiver/Transmitter (Internal) has now been renamed to the Wireless Machine Controller Cover Wireless Machine Controller Cover

title: changelog guide: Changes to Dynamo Hatches
text:
# Changes to Dynamo Hatches
There are two main changes to dynamo hatches that are outlined below.

## 256A Dynamo Hatches for UV+
Tired of having multiple 64A dynamos on your Active Transformers? Use these instead!

UV 256A Dynamo Hatch
UHV 256A Dynamo Hatch
UEV 256A Dynamo Hatch
UIV 256A Dynamo Hatch
UMV 256A Dynamo Hatch
UXV 256A Dynamo Hatch

Now you can use 256A dynamo hatches from UV and beyond! This will cut down slightly on the duplication of hatches, and allow more effective packing of amps into wires in the late game!

Unfortunately this also comes with a slight nerf to Multi-Amp Hatches across the board, but you win some and you lose some I guess!

## Buffered Dynamo Removal
Have you ever used a IV Dynamo Hatch [Buffered] and wondered why you couldn't just use a TecTech 4A dynamo version? Well now you can! These old relics of the past are now deprecated, and have been completely replaced with 4A dynamo hatches starting at IV.

For players with crafted buffered versions, they can be crafted simply into a 4A hatch.

title: changelog guide: Fewer Recipes?
text:
# Fewer Recipes?
Have you ever gone to craft a chest in an assembler, and wondered why there are more recipes than particles in the known Universe? Well today is your lucky day!

Thanks to adding OreDictionary support in all GregTech machine inputs, we now have much more condensed recipe lists!

(recipes for Chest)
> [!NOTE]
> Piston recipes now accept any OreDictionary version of cobblestone, and GregTech Planks also have OreDictionary support!

title: changelog guide: Freecam
text:
# Freecam
Now in 2.9, we have a Freecam mod! Perfect for all you show-offs who want that perfect angle to showcase your newest building madness!

## Features:
- Creative and Static (no drifting) movement options
- Camera hitbox is below half a block, so it can even fit under a half slab
- Tripod System: Save camera positions by holding the _toggle_ button and pressing a number key
- Four collision modes:
- - Full
- - Ignore Transparent (non-opaque blocks)
- - Ignore Openables (doors, trapdoors etc.)
- - None (no-clip)
- Config options for fullbright, removing fog, hand rendering, and initial perspective

## Default Controls:
- F4 - Toggle Freecam (Currently bound: )
- F4 + 1-9 - Open or switch to Tripod slot (Currently bound:  + 1-9)
- F4 + C - Toggle player/camera controls (Currently bound: )
- F4 + R - Reset all Tripods (Currently bound: )
- Mouse Wheel Scroll - Adjust Flight Speed
> [!NOTE]
> Server Owners can force collision mode, or disable the mod entirely for players

title: changelog guide: InGame Info Toggling
text:
# InGame Info Toggling
InGame Info (The information in the top left by default) now has support for a second config file!

This means that you can keep two different HUD layouts and swap between them at any time in-game!

Add an optional second file (`\config\InGameInfo2.xml`) and use the toggle key to cycle: primary -> secondary -> OFF!

title: changelog guide: JourneyMap Mob Icons
text:
# JourneyMap Mob Icons
Over its lifetime, GTNH has seen a huge variety of mobs added to the pack, many of which had no compatibility with JourneyMap. With 2.9, nearly every mob in the pack has its own custom icon, and will be visible on your mini-map! Hopefully this stops you getting so caught off guard by things crawling in the dark...

  
    An example subset of some mobs added to JourneyMap!

title: changelog guide: Matter Manipulator Improvements
text:
# Matter Manipulator Improvements
A few nice changes have been made to how the Matter Manipulator Matter Manipulator MKIII works! They are outlined below

# Advanced Copy Options (Smart Copy)
The Copy/Paste radial menu now comes with an __Advanced Options__ sub-menu with three new toggles:
- __Link to External Hubs (MKII+)__: When copying wireless connectors linked to a hub _outside_ of the copied region, pasted connectors will remain linked to that hub!
- __Auto-P2P Interfaces (MKII+)__: Replaces ME interfaces with P2P ME Interface tunnels. The source will receive an "input-side" tunnel, and the pasted version will get the "output-side" tunnel, with frequencies automatically matched. Patterns will remain at the source, so you can replicate processing set-ups that all route to that single set of patterns! (This also works with Fluid P2P Interface tunnels)
- __Auto-Proxy CRIBs (MKIII)__: Replaces Crafting Input Buses in the copied structure with Crafting Input Proxies linked back to the original bus! Again, the linking is automatic!

  
    The new Smart Copy menu
  

# Decorative Block Support
For those of you obsessed with your Carpenter's Blocks, Project Red, or Forge Microblocks, the Matter Manipulator now fully supports them!

Copying and pasting these blocks has historically been impossible to get right, but now they will not only save their orientation, but will preserve decorative covers!

## OpenComputers Cable Support
Cable Mode now works with OpenComputers cables. Right click a cable to select, then start drawing lines, just like with GregTech/Applied Energistics cables!

title: changelog guide: Non-AE2 Item Logistics
text:
# Non-AE2 Item Logistics
This is a much less "visible" change, but a huge one potentially for lategame players (and beyond!) as it allows easier movement of items without reliance on Applied Energistics.

This includes faster pipes, bigger buses, and other useful tools to allow mass movement of items without lag!

Many machines can now move more than 1 stack per tick without causing lag. High tiers of conveyors can move hundreds of thousands of items each tick, working fully with both GT and Applied Energistics systems. Some extra parts of this change include:
- Rebalancing and buffing conveyors significantly
- Adding AppliedEnergistics integration to conveyors directly
- Adding new GregTech buses (called Quantum Bus and Compressed Bus) that can hold more than one stack per slot!
- Buffing GregTech item pipes
- Huge performance improvements across the board!

title: changelog guide: Ore Changes
text:
# Ore Changes
There are a few nice changes that have been made to how ores generate, and are interacted with by players! They are outlined below
# Ore Stats Page

  
    The new "Vein Stats" page
  

The Vein Stats page in NEI has had a nice overhaul! This encompasses the "Vein Stats", "Small Ore Stats" and "Underground Fluid Stats" pages.

Along with a fresh new look, hovering over a world containing an ore will show the chance for the vein to generate per ore chunk in that world!

The new page still retains the same information present from the previous design, but now can display more than one vein type within a usual page if your GUI scale allows for it.

Ores from the likes of __BartWorks__ have also been refactored to use the same system. No more odd behaviour depending on which ore you are searching for.

# Ore Generation Changes
- Ores generated by both Bartworks and GT++ have now been reworked to mimic the way GregTech ore veins generate
- Asteroids are more common, but now smaller to compensate
- New Ice Asteroids have been added in the asteroid belts
- Veins are now less likely to be erased by the air
- Some of the missing ore veins have been added to NEI for ease of finding and consistency

title: changelog guide: Instantly Connecting Pipes
text:
# Instantly Connecting Pipes
Ever had to connect up a long pipeline and got frustrated by the awkward delay between placing a pipe and it actually registering the connection? Well cry no more!

title: changelog guide: Singleblock Power Buttons

title: changelog guide: Power Goggles Customization

title: changelog guide: Quality of Life
text:
# Quality of Life
This is one of the biggest categories of changes coming to 2.9, touching nearly every aspect of the pack to make life easier in some way. This list does not include the incredible amount of minor tweaks or bug fixes as they are too plentiful to mention.

# List of Quality of Life Changes:

title: changelog guide: Quest Book Changes
text:
# Quest Book Changes
The quest book has a fresh new look! Lines connecting quests now show arrows to help visualise the flow of quests, and which way the dependencies are going! Hovering over a quest will animate all lines connected to it. There is also a new button on the left sidebar to toggle the arrows if you prefer the old style.

Though there are some obvious changes to the quests (Coins page removal as an example), the Quest Dev team have been working tirelessly to make sure the entire quest book operates as smoothly as possible.

> [!NOTE]
> The animation can be disabled in the config if you so desire

title: changelog guide: Recipe Counting
text:
# Recipe Counting
Have you ever wondered "How many recipes has this machine made in its lifetime?" Well now you can find the answer! Using the portable scanner on a machine controller will show a recipe counter, showing how many recipes that machine has finished!

  
    An example of the scanner being used

title: changelog guide: Shared Prospecting
text:
# Shared Prospecting
Visual Prospecting has received a huge quality of life improvement by overhauling how it works in multiplayer. New prospects found will instantly now be shared to all members of the same team (GTNH Team to be specific)! For those players who have used Shared Prospecting in the past, the functionality is effectively the same, but working and optimised.

Additionally, underground fluid prospecting has been made easier to distinguish by adding colored overlays to each fluid, using the same colors as are found in the higher tier prospector's tools!

As part of this overhaul,

| Command | Permission Level | Effect |
| --------------- | --------------- | --------------- |
| `/vp_client_cache_reset` | - | Resets the clientside cache of prospects |
| `/vp team info [detailed]` | 0 | Shows info regarding your team |
