title: gregtech guide: Multiblock Machines
text:
# Multiblock Machines

> [!NOTE]
> Some links are broken due to their pages not being available at this time. Help support GTNH's development by contributing to the guide!

A **Multiblock** is a machine built from two or more blocks. Sizes range from small Thermal Refineries to massive superstructures like the Forge of the Gods. They typically serve a very specific purpose and are always better than their singleblock equivalent (ie. runs faster, better recipes), if one exists. Most multiblocks have their own unique casings and structure, but the input/output (I/O) of items, fluids, and energy is nearly universal. Items are transferred via buses, fluids are transferred via hatches, and power is transferred via energy/dynamo hatches. There is also the maintenance hatch for repairing the machine and the muffler hatch for releasing pollution. Use the tooltip and/or the Multiblock Structure Hologram Projector to see which buses/hatches are necessary and where they fit into the overall structure.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Not all multiblocks in GTNH are from GregTech. There are a select few from other mods (ie. Railcraft Boilers and Smelteries) that do not follow any of the information on this page. Visit their individual pages for more details.

---

# Construction

Although multiblocks come in a variety of shapes, sizes, and casings, there are many common components for the I/O of items, fluids, and energy. The following subsections describe the purpose and function of each one. Note that multiblocks rarely require ALL of these to form and that there may be restrictions on their amounts and locations. Always check the tooltip and Multiblock Structure Hologram Projector for detailed information about a multiblock's construction requirements.

## Controller

The controller is the heart of the multiblock. It determines the placement and orientation of the entire structure as well as the operational settings of the machine. Right-click the controller to open the GUI which contains (1) the name of the machine at the top, (2) the status of the machine, (3) a sound toggle, (4) a few configurable parameters, (5) the power panel, and (6) any manual overrides. A short description of each of the configurable parameters and manual overrides is provided below.

- **Void Mode** - Determines the behavior of the multiblock when there is no room in the output bus and/or output hatch. Choose to void only items, only fluids, or both. Void nothing means temporarily pause the machine until there is enough room for all products.
- **Input Separation** - Prevents SOLID ingredients in different input buses from being used in the same recipe, including any programmed circuits. This is particularly useful for multiblocks with a high potential for recipe conflicts.
- **Batch Mode** - Run multiples of the same recipe as one large recipe. This does NOT provide any sort of time discount or increase the throughput of the machine. The purpose is to reduce lag and improve TPS by lowering the number of recipe checks.
- **Lock Recipe** - Prevent the multiblock from running other recipes. This can be set while a multiblock is currently running, or prior to the desired recipe.
- **Update Structure** - Force a structure check. Multiblocks already do periodic structure checks, but this can save a few seconds (or minutes) of waiting.
- **Power Switch** - Enable or disable the multiblock. This does NOT interrupt active recipes.

There are two options inside the power panel. The first is setting the maximum number of parallels which defaults to the maximum available. There is not much reason to ever lower it or manually set the value, unless there is a very specific scenario that requires absolute precision over energy efficiency. The second option toggles powerfail events which includes the message in chat and the blinking powerfail icon that appears when looking at the controller from a distance. In multiplayer, use the first command to invite other players to the same SpaceProject team and share powerfail information. Use the second command to immediately clear all powerfail icons from the world.

```
/sp invite 
/powerfails clear
```

There are also a few unique interactions and shortcuts to changing the operational settings of the machine without having to enter the GUI. All of these involve right-clicking the controller with some sort of GregTech tool in hand. This reduces the durability of the tool, but it works very well with the Ring of Loki to quickly configure many machines at the same time.

- **Wrench** - Rotate the controller and therefore the entire structure. Sneak right-click to flip the controller horizontally.
- **Screwdriver** - Enable/disable input separation. Also used to change the mode of certain multiblocks.
- **Wire Cutters** - Enable/disable batch mode.
- **Soft Mallet** - Enable/disable the machine.
- **Hammer** - Enable/disable sound muffling.
- **Soldering Iron** - Set the strength (strong/weak) of the redstone signal from covers. This is not exclusive to controllers.

## Buses

Chest **Input Bus** / Chest **Output Bus**

Input and output buses are for inserting and extracting SOLID ingredients, respectively. Fluids and gases cannot be supplied via cells, buckets, or similar containers. Input buses do not automatically pull from adjacent inventories, but output buses automatically push to adjacent inventories, if one exists. The tier of the bus determines the available capacity or total number of item slots:

| Tier | ULV | LV | MV | HV+ |
|------|-----|----|----|-----|
| Slots | 1 | 4 | 9 | 16 |

Right-click an input bus with a screwdriver to enable/disable the filter which prevents any ingredients without a use in the multiblock from entering the bus. Sneak right-click the input bus with a screwdriver to enable/disable sorting and limiting mode. Sorting mode constantly pushes items to the top-most slots while limiting mode prevents more than one stack of an item from entering the bus. There is also a filter in the GUI of output buses to lock them to specific items (drag from NEI).

- **Super Buses** - An upgrade from regular input/output buses although the only difference is their slot capacity. Regular buses are capped at 16 slots while super buses range from 32-160 slots. The problem, however, is that they are much more expensive and require a Tier+3 regular input bus to craft. The LV super bus, for example, is crafted from five LV conveyor modules, two LV motors, and an EV input bus.

- **Stocking Input Bus (ME)** and **Output Bus (ME)** - An even better upgrade from regular input/output buses because they connect directly to an AE2 network for seamless I/O of items. Right-click with wire cutters to allow ME channels to connect to any side, including other buses/hatches. The advanced version even supports auto-pull which allows it to stock itself with any item in the network.

## Hatches

Cauldron **Input Hatch** / Cauldron **Output Hatch**

Input and output hatches are for inserting and extracting FLUID ingredients, respectively. Input hatches do not automatically pull from adjacent inventories, but output hatches automatically push to adjacent inventories, if one exists. The tier of the hatch determines the available capacity. Input hatches can technically "hold" much more than these amounts by placing a stack of large fluid cells into their inventory.

| Tier | ULV | LV | MV | HV | EV | IV | ... |
|------|-----|----|----|----|----|----|-----|
| Capacity | 8,000 L | 16,000 L | 32,000 L | 64,000 L | 128,000 L | 256,000 L | ... |

Right-click an output hatch with a screwdriver to change whether to output steam and/or other fluids. Alternatively, set the filter in the GUI of the output hatch to lock it to a specific fluid (drag from NEI).

- **Quadruple Input Hatches** - An upgrade from regular input hatches that can hold up to four different fluids simultaneously at 1/4th the capacity of a regular input hatch of the same tier. These pair nicely with quadruple fluid pipes for transporting multiple fluids around.

- **Stocking Input Hatch (ME)** and **Output Hatch (ME)** - An even better upgrade from regular input/output hatches because they connect directly to an AE2 network for seamless I/O of fluids. Right-click with wire cutters to allow ME channels to connect to any side, including other buses/hatches. The advanced version even supports auto-pull which allows it to stock itself with any fluid in the network.

## Energy & Dynamo Hatches

Block of Redstone **Energy Hatch** / Block of Redstone **Dynamo Hatch**

These are for inserting and extracting power at a specific voltage tier. More specifically, a standard energy hatch can supply up to 2A of power to a multiblock and a standard dynamo hatch can extract up to 1A of power from a multiblock. Be very careful to use the correct voltage and amperage with these hatches otherwise cables could burn, ingredients could void, and machines could explode.

- **Buffered Dynamo Hatches** - A small upgrade from standard dynamo hatches and can extract up to 4A of power from a multiblock. These also have a slightly larger internal buffer for storing power when there is nowhere for it to go. *(Deprecated as of 2.9 - instead, use a 4A Multi-Amp hatch.)*

- **Multi-Amp Hatches** - An upgrade from standard energy/dynamo hatches and can transfer up to 64A of power to/from a multiblock. Whether these are allowed or not highly depends on the multiblock.

- **Laser Hatches** - Unlocked much later on and can transfer millions of amps to/from a multiblock via laser vacuum pipes. Again, whether these are allowed or not highly depends on the multiblock.

## Maintenance Hatch

Iron Door **Maintenance Hatch**

This hatch is for repairing any maintenance issues -- random occurrences that increase the power consumption of the multiblock by 10% each. There are six different maintenance issues in total and having all of them simultaneously is enough to shut the multiblock down. Each one generates a very specific message in the controller and corresponds to a very specific GregTech tool. WAILA also displays **HAS PROBLEMS** in red text while looking at the controller.

Repair maintenance issues by opening the maintenance hatch, picking up the necessary tool, and left-clicking the center button. This consumes a small amount of durability and/or charge with every use.

| Maintenance Issue | Tool to Fix |
|-------------------|-------------|
| "Pipe is loose" | Wrench |
| "Screws are loose" | Screwdriver |
| "Something is stuck" | Soft Mallet |
| "Platings are dented" | Hammer |
| "Circuitry burned out" | Soldering Iron |
| "That doesn't belong there" | Crowbar |

There is a 1 in 6,000 chance every 50 seconds of runtime for a new maintenance issue to appear. That is an average of 300,000 seconds or 83.3 hours of runtime between maintenance issues. Disabled or idle multiblocks do not increase runtime and therefore do not generate any maintenance issues or increase the likelihood thereof. Multiblocks without maintenance hatches ignore the mechanic entirely.

There are a few different types of maintenance hatches and methods to repair them, listed below. Maintenance hatches may be wallshared between machines, although repairs must still be made for each one individually.

- **Tool Box (LV)** - Holds up to nine tools and applies all of them simultaneously when a maintenance hatch is right-clicked from OUTSIDE its internal GUI. This consumes durability and/or charge of all tools inside regardless of the issue(s) present. Soldering material for the soldering iron may also be stored in and used from the Tool Box. Can be automated with a Dynamism Tablet and needs a maintenance cover.

- **BrainTech Aerospace Advanced Reinforced Duct Tape (MV)** - A single use item that solves all maintenance issues simultaneously. The tape visually appears around the maintenance hatch but that does not prevent future maintenance issues or reduce the chances of them occurring.

- **Wand Focus: Maintenance (HV)** - A reusable Thaumcraft wand focus from Electromagic Tools that solves all maintenance issues simultaneously at the cost of 25 ignis, 25 terra, and 25 ordo. Vis discounts and the frugal focus upgrade can reduce the cost of these repairs.

- **Drone Downlink Module (IV)** - Automatically repairs any maintenance issues if there is an active Drone Centre within range of the hatch. Tier 1 and Tier 2 drones have a chance to crash and be destroyed every second, but fixing maintenance issues is completely free. It also allows remote control over connected multiblocks which is very useful after a widespread power outage.

- **Auto Maintenance Hatch (LuV)** - Automatically repairs any maintenance issue at the cost of 4 duct tape, 2 lubricant cells, 4 steel screws, and 2 HV circuits. The internal inventory has four total slots, or one for each type of item.

- **Auto-Taping Maintenance Hatch (UV)** - Automatically repairs any maintenance issue at no cost. The permanent solution to maintenance.

## Muffler Hatch

Dispenser **Muffler Hatch**

This hatch releases pollution from the machine. There must be at least one block of air in front of the muffler hatch in order for the multiblock to function. Even pipes and wires are considered an obstruction. The amount of pollution generated depends on the multiblock and the tier of the muffler hatch:

| Tier | LV | MV | HV | EV | IV | LuV | ZPM | UV | UHV |
|------|----|----|----|----|----|-----|-----|----|-----|
| Pollution | 100% | 87% | 75% | 62% | 50% | 37% | 25% | 12% | 0% |

If pollution is disabled, muffler hatches are still required, but their tier is no longer relevant.

## Wallsharing

A unique property of GregTech multiblocks is their ability to wallshare parts of their structure to save on casings, glass, coils, buses/hatches, and more. Simply overlap structures to allow multiple machines to use the same block(s) simultaneously. There are *very* few exceptions where that is not beneficial to the player and is therefore extremely useful throughout the entire game, whether building a second Electric Blast Furnace or a second Eye of Harmony.

Maintenance and muffler hatches are always safe to share, but be careful when sharing energy hatches because they can only pull up to 2A of power. Ensure that the recipes for a multiblock do not exceed 1A of power and repair maintenance issues as soon as possible, or else the additional power cost could cause both machines to powerfail.

---

# Usage

Although multiblocks operate very similarly to singleblock machines, there are a few distinct differences. First and foremost is that multiblocks **void** ingredients when they power fail. There is no restarting the recipe like in singleblocks; the ingredients just disappear, permanently. The multiblock also shuts down and has to be manually restarted. Periodically check your energy storage to prevent this from happening and turn off multiblocks or stop using them when energy levels are low. Also ensure that the entire multiblock is chunkloaded to avoid the controller loading in before the energy hatches.

## Overclocking

An overclock occurs when the supplied power is at least 1 voltage tier higher than required by the recipe. Singleblocks can only achieve this with higher tier machines, but multiblocks can use higher tier and/or multiple energy hatches. The player first encounters overclocking when using the Electric Blast Furnace; two energy hatches are needed to supply 4A of LV power, simulating 1A of MV power. There are two different types of overclocks and the one used depends on the multiblock itself. Those under "mixed" can use both in the same recipe or depend on an upgrade. Those under "unique" follow their own special rules and do not fit into either category.

- **Imperfect Overclocks** - Consume 4x the power for 2x the speed (4/2). This is the standard behavior of most multiblocks. For example, consider a recipe that normally takes 128 EU/t and 60s to run for a total of 153,600 EU. An imperfect overclock changes that to 512 EU/t and 30s to run for a total of 307,200 EU. Notice that the total energy is doubled which means the extra speed may not always be worth the additional power cost. Alternatively, build more of the same multiblock at the same voltage tier to provide the same effect for half the power.

- **Perfect Overclocks** - Consume 4x the power for 4x the speed (4/4). The total energy remains the same so there is no downside to increasing the supplied voltage/amperage. The only reason to build multiple of the same multiblock with perfect overclocks is when there is not enough room for additional energy hatches. Very few multiblocks allow perfect overclocks.

Overclocking is only possible down to 1 tick because that is the smallest unit of time in Minecraft, but nearly every multiblock in GTNH is capable of subticking or increasing its number of parallels by a corresponding amount to simulate additional overclocks. The only exception is the Advanced Assembly Line which is capped at 1 tick per slice.

## Parallels

A parallel is a multiple of a recipe that runs concurrently with the original. Parallels increase the throughput and power consumption of a multiblock without increasing the overall length of the recipe. Two parallels, for example, double the EU/t to process twice the number of inputs simultaneously. The total EU remains the same, as with perfect overclocks, which means parallels are perfectly energy efficient and very powerful. Note that adding parallels is NOT the same as increasing the batch size -- the latter is only for saving TPS and does not increase the throughput of the multiblock.

- **Batch Size** - More recipes per iteration, same EU/t, longer duration.
- **Parallels** - More recipes per iteration, higher EU/t, same duration.

Parallels are calculated AFTER energy discounts and BEFORE overclocks. Consider a recipe that consumes 2,000 EU/t over 16 seconds in the Volcanus which offers 8 parallels and only uses 90% of the EU/t normally required. The energy discount first reduces the base recipe to 1,800 EU/t over 16 seconds. If there is enough power for the maximum number of parallels then the multiblock consumes 8 x 1,800 = 14,400 EU/t over 16 seconds. If there is still enough power and high enough coils to grant a perfect overclock then the multiblock consumes 4 x 14,400 = 57,600 EU/t over 4 seconds. Lastly, one imperfect overclock increases the power consumption to 4 x 57,600 = 230,400 EU/t over 2 seconds.

```
EU/t = Base EU/t x EU Usage x Parallels x 4^Overclocks
```

## Troubleshooting

If a multiblock is not working, the first thing to do is open the controller for a clue on what is wrong. The following are some common error messages and what they could mean. If all else fails, reread the tooltip and the construction requirements on the wiki before rebuilding the entire multiblock with the Multiblock Structure Hologram Projector.

### \*\* HAS PROBLEMS \*\*

- Needs Maintenance
  - Use tools inside Maintenance Hatch GUI, **OR**
  - Right-click with Tool Box on Maintenance Hatch
    - Must have full complement of tools
    - Soldering Iron must be charged
    - Needs soldering material (consumable)
- Volcanus with no Pyrotheum - causes voiding & maintenance issues
- Cryogenic Freezer with no Cryotheum - causes voiding & maintenance issues

### \*\* INCOMPLETE STRUCTURE \*\*

- Multiblock built incorrectly
  - Missing parts - left-Shift over controller in NEI
  - Parts are in the wrong position
  - Exceeds maximums or does not meet minimums
  - Wrong casings - some blocks are visually similar
  - Energy Hatch is insufficient tier
  - Mixed coils or casing types
  - Controller is facing the interior of the multiblock
  - Something inside a multi that should be hollow
- Structure not recognized
  - Not built in one chunk or fully chunkloaded
  - Break and replace Controller

### Does Not Turn On

- No power
  - Power line has breaks / not connected
  - A cover is blocking power transmission somewhere
  - Transformers are not oriented properly
  - Energy Hatch input isn't facing power
  - Generator(s) aren't turned on and connected
  - Generator(s) out of fuel
  - Battery Buffer has no batteries
  - Batteries are not charged
  - Battery and Buffer tier don't match
- Incorrect recipe
  - Liquids aren't in Input Hatch
  - Items aren't in Input Bus
  - Programmed Circuit not set in Input Bus / Controller
  - Wrong ingredients, verify by metadata
  - Coils/Casings/Energy Hatch insufficient tier for recipe
  - Blocked by unusable recipe items in buses/hatches
- Disabled
  - Hit with Soft Mallet
  - Press power button in controller
- No Energy Hatch - add at least one Energy Hatch to accept power
- Structure insufficient - multiblock configuration doesn't meet recipe's needs; gas/liquid needs an output in a different location

### Turns On then Voids / Shuts Down

- Insufficient power
  - Not enough power generation - check recipe
  - Too much power being used by other machines
  - Not enough power delivered due to cable loss
  - Over-limited by diode or transformer
  - Battery Buffers only output 1A per battery
  - Recipe is overclocking, consuming more power than expected
  - Not all Energy Hatches are connected to power
  - Not enough Energy Hatches to accept power (2A max each)
- Muffler Hatch blocked
  - Muffler is not pointing out
  - Muffler does not have an air block above it
  - Advanced Muffler Hatches need air filters
- Missing Consumables
  - Turbine item for Air Filters and Turbines
  - Cryotheum for Cryogenic Freezer
  - Pyrotheum for Volcanus

### Wrong Output

- Incorrect circuit set
- Input separation not enabled on a multi-bus setup
- Water/Lava conditions not met for the Rock Breaker

### Voids at Random / Runs Intermittently

- Power loss - another machine is competing for amps, or power production is inconsistent
- Job Done - no ingredients left to process, or no pollution in chunks for Air Filter

### Needs More Power

- Insufficient Energy Hatch tier
- Insufficient casing/hull tier for recipe

### Overflowed

- Coil / heat casings mismatch

### Not Enough Output Space

- Output doesn't have enough slots for the recipe
- Output is full/missing
- Missing an output for directional products
  - EBF needs a hatch on top for gas and a hatch on bottom for fluids

### No Valid Recipe Found

- No combination of valid items / wrong item
- Missing input hatch/bus

text:
# Active Transformer

The Active Transformer (AT) is a ZPM-tier multiblock for transforming power from any voltage tier to any other voltage tier with virtually unlimited amperage throughput. 

The AT is a direct upgrade from singleblock transformers and buck converters because it supports multi-amp and laser energy/dynamo hatches, can change input/output voltage without building a new machine, and supports multiple input/outputs with different voltages. 

The only downside is that there is a 0.004% power loss for all EU that passes through the machine. 

| Property | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Unlock Tier | ZPM |
| Structure Size | 3×3×3 |
| Power | Any Hatches allowed, includes Multi-Amp and Laser Hatches |
| Overclocks | None |
| Maintenance | No maintenance needed |
| Pollution | Produces no pollution |

## Crafting and Construction

### Crafting
(recipes for Active Transformer)

(recipes for High Power Casing)

The AT requires 1 Superconducting Coil Block(You can press  while hovering over the Item link to see the recipes for this). You can craft this with recipes that match your current superconductor tier.

### Structure
AT can rotate in any direction, include up and down.

| Component | Quantity and placement |
| --- | --- |
| Active Transformer | 1, Front center, 2nd layer. |
| High Power Casing | 5-24 |
| Superconducting Coil Block | 1, Center of the structure |
| LV Energy HatchCan use Regular, Multi-Amp, Laser | 1+, Any casing. |
| LV Dynamo HatchCan use Regular, Multi-Amp, Laser | 0+, Any casing. |

### Wallsharing

ATs may wallshare each of their sides to save on casings and even split power. At full throughput, the input EU/t is divided evenly between ATs sharing the same energy hatch or laser target hatch. If one is full or no longer consumes power then the difference is split amongst the remaining ATs.

## Usage
The AT receives power from Energy Hatches and outputs power via Dynamo Hatches, similar to the Lapotronic Supercapacitor. The voltage and amperage do NOT matter. 

This means that your input/output voltage and amperage are entirely influenced only by the Energy/Dynamo Hatches' voltage and maximum amperage, and that no excess power is voided or new power is generated.

Since ATs can have multiple inputs and outputs, they can integrate multiple power supplies into a single unit or distribute integrated power across multiple machines through several Dynamo Hatches or Laser Source Hatches.

Until Laser Vacuum Mirror becomes available at UHV+, AT is mainly used to redirect the laser power lines.

# Advanced Assembly Line

The Advanced Assembly Line (AAL) is an IV tier multiblock for running Assembly Line recipes in parallel by leveraging item pipelining; ingredients are consumed slice-by-slice instead of all at once, much like a real Assembly Line. That means the maximum number of parallels corresponds to the number of solid ingredients in a recipe. 

The AAL supports multi-amp and laser energy hatches for serious overclocking and massive parallel operation, but **CANNOT** tier skip and is harder to automate compared to regular Assembly Line, which makes AAL specialized in late-game mass production like stargate material rather than early-game progression. 

| Property | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Unlock Tier | IV |
| Structure Size (LxWxH) | 3x5-16x4 |
| Power | Any Hatches allowed, includes Multi-Amp and Laser Hatches |
| Overclocks | Unique |
| Maintenance | Need Maintenance |
| Pollution | Produces no pollution |

## Crafting and Construction

### Crafting
(recipes for Advanced Assembly Line)

(recipes for Grate Machine Casing)

(recipes for Solid Steel Machine Casing)

(recipes for Assembly Line Casing)

(recipes for Assembler Machine Casing)

### Structure
The only structural difference between the AAL and the Assembly Line is the controller. 

AAL can be rotated or flipped.

The glass can be any tier and has no effect on the operation of the machine. 

Use the Multiblock Structure Hologram Projector to visualize/build the structure with subchannel "glass" to specify the tier of the glass and subchannel "length" to specify the number of slices $$(\text{Slices} = \text{Length} + 4)$$

#### Base Structure (Minimum requirements)
| Component | Quantity and placement |
| --- | --- |
| Advanced Assembly Line | First slice, 3rd layer |
| Borosilicate Glass BlockAny Tiered Glass | 10, Both sides of 2nd layer |
| Grate Machine Casing | 8, Both sides of 3rd layer |
| Solid Steel Machine Casing | 0-12, Both sides of 1st layer and center of 4th layer |
| Assembly Line Casing | 5, Center of 2nd layer |
| Assembler Machine Casing | 5, Center of 3rd layer |
| LV Energy HatchCan use Regular, Multi-Amp, Laser | 1+, Any 4th layer Casing |
| Maintenance HatchMaintenance Hatch | 1+, Any 1st layer side casings |
| Data Access HatchData Access Hatch | 1, Any both sides of 3rd layer but **NOT** on first slice |
| Input Bus (LV)Input Bus | 5, Center of 1st layer |
| Input Hatch (LV)Input Hatch | 0+, Any 1st layer side casings |
| Output Bus (LV)Output Bus | 1, Any 1st layer on last slice |

#### Each Additional Slice

Each additional slice (1 length) requires these blocks:

| Component | Quantity and placement |
| --- | --- |
| Borosilicate Glass BlockAny Tiered Glass | 2, Both sides of 2nd layer |
| Grate Machine Casing | 2, Both sides of 3rd layer |
| Solid Steel Machine Casing | 0-3, Both sides of 1st layer and center of 4th layer |
| Assembly Line Casing | 1, Center of 2nd layer |
| Assembler Machine Casing | 1, Center of 3rd layer |
| Input Bus (LV)Input Bus | 1, Center of 1st layer |

In any slice, LV Energy HatchCan use Regular, Multi-Amp, Laser can replace 4th layer casing and Solid Steel Machine Casing in 1st layer can be replaced with Input Hatch (LV)Input Hatches.

Note that the Output Bus (LV)Output Bus must be moved to the last slice when you extend AAL slices.

### Wallsharing

AALs may wallshare each of their sides to save on casings, glass, and buses/hatches. That includes any input hatches, maintenance hatches, data access hatches, and output buses. Sharing a data access hatch is particularly valuable for saving TPS and reducing the number of Data Bank multiblocks needed to operate.

## Usage

The AAL starts processing once the contents of the buses/hatches align with a stored data stick, much like the regular Assembly Line. Every recipe must pass through N slices on the machine, where N is the number of solid ingredients. Each slice takes $$\text{T} = (\text{base duration} / \text{N})$$ seconds to process the ONE type of item in its input bus before continuing to the next slice for the next item. This repeats until all ingredients are consumed and the final product is sent to the output bus for retrieval. All fluids are consumed at the very start of processing.

The AAL supports parallel processing by allowing the next recipe to begin once the first slice is done with the first recipe. This creates a staggered pattern that allows every slice to work simultaneously, if there are enough resources available.

If the next slice is missing the required item in its input bus, the current slice enters the **STUCK** state which halts the entire machine until the missing item is found/returned. The status light on the face of the controller turns orange to indicate that the machine is STUCK. Use WAILA to locate where exactly the problem occurred.

The scene on the right shows how the AAL processes the same recipe simultaneously slice by slice, why the AAL gets stuck, and how to resolve it.

### Laser Overclocks

The energy consumption of the AAL is the number of active slices times the base EU/t, similar to parallels. The AAL then runs up to N imperfect overclocks where N is the difference between the voltage tier of the lowest tier energy hatch and the voltage tier of the recipe. 

Further overclocks are all laser overclocks, which consume more power and scale even worse than an imperfect overclock. The first one is 2x speed for 4.3x the power and each additional one increases the power multiplier by 0.3, scaling infinitely.

- Imperfect Overclocks - 2x speed for 4.0x power (2/4.0).
- 1st Laser Overclock - 2x speed for 4.3x power (2/4.3).
- 2nd Laser Overclock - 2x speed for 4.6x power (2/4.6).
- 3rd Laser Overclock - 2x speed for 4.9x power (2/4.9).

The increased power cost of laser overclocks means that upgrading the energy hatch(es) is not always going to overclock the machine. It all depends on the recipe's base EU/t and the maximum number of parallels. 

Consider the UIV field generator recipe as an example. There can be up to 14 slices active simultaneously and each one consumes 15/16A of UEV power for a total of 13.1A. That means a 16A UEV energy hatch is enough to cover the base cost of the recipe, but does not grant any laser overclocks. Upgrading to a 64A energy hatch grants one laser overclock because that is greater than 13.1 x 4.3 = 56.4A, but upgrading to a 256A energy hatch does NOT grant a second laser overclock because that is less than 56.4 x 4.6 = 259A. The following table lists the amperage needed for a given number of laser overclocks for on-tier recipes (i.e. UEV recipes with one UEV laser energy hatch) that consume 15/16A of power.

| 9 | 64 | 256 | 1,024 | 16,384 | 65,536 | 262,144 | 1,048,576 | 16,777,216 |

# Advanced Coke Oven

The Advanced Coke Oven Brick Advanced Coke Oven (ACO) is an MV tier multiblock for burning logs into charcoal. 

The ACO is a direct upgrade to the basic Coke Oven because it is 90x faster, but it requires a burnable fuel such as the very charcoal that it produces and it does not produce creosote oil. Therefore, the ACO's maximum output is 1 charcoal per second, but its net output is 15 charcoal per 16 seconds. 

The ACO does not consume power and is initially faster than the Pyrolyse Oven, but that quickly changes as better heating coils and energy hatches are unlocked. 

The ACO is superseded by the Industrial Coke Oven in EV.

| Property | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Unlock Tier | MV |
| Structure Size (LxWxH) | 3x3x4 |
| Power | None |
| Overclocks | None |
| Maintenance | No maintenance needed |
| Pollution | Produces 80 gibbl/s pollution |

## Crafting and Construction

### Crafting

(recipes for Advanced Coke Oven Brick)

(recipes for Advanced Coke Oven Brick)

### Structure

The ACO consists of a single type of block and does not have a controller or any buses/hatches. The Multiblock Structure Hologram Projector does not visualize/build the structure, but it is very easy to build.

ACO cannot be rotated at all.

| Component | Quantity and placement |
| --- | --- |
| Advanced Coke Oven Brick | 34, 3x3x4 with hollow 1x1x2 center |

### Wallsharing

As a Railcraft multiblock, **the ACO cannot wallshare any part of its structure** and must be at least one block apart from other ACOs to form.

## Usage

The ACO produces one charcoal per second from logs. That is 90x faster than the basic Coke Oven, but it requires a burnable fuel such as the very charcoal that it produces and it does not produce creosote oil. Charcoal has a burntime of 1600 ticks which fuels the ACO for 16 seconds, resulting in a net loss of only 1/16 of the total output. The ACO can also turn coal into coal coke, sugar charcoal into sugar coke, and cactus charcoal into cactus coke (1 second each).

Inputs can be inserted into any block on any side of the structure and outputs can be extracted from any block on any side of the structure. The ACO does not auto-pull from adjacent inventories but it does auto-push. 

The scene on the side shows an example of a self-feeding loop using EnderIO conduits.

### Charcoal Rate Comparison

The Pyrolyse Oven is another option for turning logs into charcoal in the early game that can be overclocked, boosted with nitrogen, and scales with the tier of its heating coils. 

To help the player decide between the ACO and the Pyrolyse Oven, the following table compares their average charcoal per second for various recipes, heating coils, and overclocks. The cells highlighted green mean the Pyrolyse Oven is faster than the ACO and the cells highlighted in red mean the Pyrolyse Oven is slower. Note that the ACO does not consume any EU, but it also produces no fluid byproducts, which may also be a deciding factor depending on your current situation.

# Algae Farm

The Algae Farm is an MV tier multiblock for cultivating different types of algae. The Algae Farm requires no inputs other than power to run and produces no pollution. # Alloy Blast Smelter

The Alloy Blast Smelter (ABS) is an IV tier multiblock for smelting dusts into molten alloys. Compared to Industrial Mixing Machine and Zyngen, processing the dusts to molten alloy directly makes ABS handle basic alloy recipes faster and more efficiently. However, unlike those machines, ABS cannot tier skip - makes the ABS suited to mass production rather than tier progression.

The ABS can even be used to smelt some of the tougher alloys such as Indalloy 140, which have no recipe in any other machine. 

There are no tiered components or any sort of bonuses and there is no tier skipping, even when overclocking with multiple energy hatches. 

The minimum casing requirement is very low to allow for many buses/hatches since there are 12 unique programmed circuits to handle all ABS Recipes. The ABS is superseded by the Mega Alloy Blast Smelter in UV.

text:
# Amazon Warehousing Depot

The Amazon Warehousing Depot(AWD) is an IV tier multiblock for packaging and unpackaging various items.

The AWD is a direct upgrade from the singleblock packager and unpackager because it can process both types of recipes, runs up to 900% speed, only uses 75% of the EU/t normally required, and offers 16 parallels per voltage tier.

Input separation should be enabled on the AWD for using different schematics within the same machine.

| Property | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Unlock Tier | IV |
| Structure Size (LxWxH) | 3x5x3 |
| Power | Regular |
| Overclocks | Imperfect |
| Maintenance | Need Maintenance |
| Pollution | Produces 40 gibbl/s pollution, and require Muffler Hatch |

## Crafting and Construction

### Crafting

(recipes for Amazon Warehousing Depot)

(recipes for Supply Depot Casing)

(recipes for Iron Frame Box)

### Structure

The AWD has one tiered component - The item pipe casings, which determine the speed bonus of the machine.

The glass can be any tier and has no effect on the operation of the machine.

AWD can be rotated or mirrored.

Multi-amp and laser energy hatches are not supported, but there can be multiple regular energy hatches for overclocking. Use the Multiblock Structure Hologram Projector to visualize/build the structure with subchannels "item_pipe" and "glass" to specify the tier of those components.

| Component | Quantity and placement |
| --- | --- |
| Amazon Warehousing Depot | 1, Front right, 2nd layer |
| Supply Depot Casing | 4-15 |
| Tin Item Pipe CasingTiered Item Pipe Casing | 3 |
| Borosilicate Glass BlockAny Tiered Glass | 3 |
| Iron Frame Box | 2 |
| LV Energy HatchOnly Regular Hatches allowed | 1+, Can replace Supply Depot Casing |
| Maintenance HatchMaintenance Hatch | 1+, Can replace Supply Depot Casing |
| Muffler Hatch (LV)Muffler Hatch | 1+, Can replace Supply Depot Casing |
| Input Bus (LV)Input Bus | 1+, Can replace Supply Depot Casing |
| Output Bus (LV)Output Bus | 1+, Can replace Supply Depot Casing |

### Wallsharing

AWDs may wallshare each of their sides except for the right side (controller is in the way) to save on casings, frame boxes, and buses/hatches. No recipe uses more than 1A of power so it is possible to share one energy hatch between two machines.

## Usage

The AWD has two operating modes, listed below. Switch between modes in the GUI of the controller or by right-clicking the controller with a screwdriver. The packager mode is useful for the tiny and small piles of dust from the Electric Implosion Compressor and for creating scrap boxes. The unpackager mode is a nice-to-have for recycling certain items such as old Lapotronic Supercapacitor capacitors.

- Packager - Runs ONLY packager recipes.
- Unpackager - Runs ONLY unpackager recipes.

Input separation should be enabled on the AWD to prevent SOLID ingredients in different input buses from being used in the same recipe, including any schematics. That means a single AWD with many input buses can support many different schematics simultaneously. Just don't forget to stay above the minimum number of supply depot casings.

### Speed Upgrades from Item Pipe Casing

AWD can be upgraded by using higher-tier Item Pipe Casing. The speed bonus for each Item Pipe Casing is listed below. 

| Item Pipe Casing | Speed |
| --- | --- |
| Tin Item Pipe Casing | 200% |
| Brass Item Pipe Casing | 300% |
| Electrum Item Pipe Casing | 400% |
| Platinum Item Pipe Casing | 500% |
| Osmium Item Pipe Casing | 600% |
| Quantium Item Pipe Casing | 700% |
| Fluxed Electrum Item Pipe Casing | 800% |
| Black Plutonium Item Pipe Casing | 900% |

title: gregtech guide: Assembly Line
text:
# Assembly Line

The Assembly Line (assline or AL) is an IV tier multiblock for crafting LuV+ tier components. 

The machine is built as a series of slices and inputs must be inserted in the exact order in which they appear in NEI. 

Recipes are also NOT implicit and must be explicitly shared with the AL via Data Stick. This is unlike any multiblock the player has encountered up to this point and requires more advanced techniques for automation. For normal assembler recipes, see the Precise Auto-Assembler MT-3662 or Large Scale Auto-Assembler v1.01. 

The AL is generally superseded by the Advanced Assembly Line with its parallel processing and support for multi-amp and laser energy hatches, but AL's tier skipping prevents AAL from fully replacing AL, since AAL cannot do tier skipping.

| Property | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Unlock Tier | IV |
| Structure Size(LxWxH) | 3x5-16x4 |
| Power | Regular |
| Overclocks | Imperfect |
| Maintenance | Need Maintenance |
| Pollution | Produces no pollution |

## Crafting and Construction

### Crafting
(recipes for Assembly Line)

(recipes for Grate Machine Casing)

(recipes for Solid Steel Machine Casing)

(recipes for Assembly Line Casing)

(recipes for Assembler Machine Casing)

### Structure

The AL is built as a series of slices with an input bus at the bottom center of each one to hold a single unique input. The total number of slices required therefore depends on the total number of inputs in the recipe. For example, the LuV motor has five solid inputs and therefore needs five slices to craft. The order in which the ingredients are inserted is the same order in which they appear in NEI.

AL can be rotated and mirrored, and the first slice is where controller exists.

The glass can be any tier and has no effect on the operation of the machine. 

Multi-amp and laser energy hatches are not supported, but there can be multiple regular energy hatches for overclocking. The AL can only tier skip ONE time (ie. IV energy hatches can run up to LuV recipes). 

Use the Multiblock Structure Hologram Projector to visualize/build the structure with subchannel "glass" to specify the tier of the glass and subchannel "length" to specify the number of slices $$(\text{Slices} = \text{Length} + 4)$$.

The input buses can be any tier but it is recommended to use Input Bus (ULV) because their limited capacity(1 slot) is very useful for automation. 

Advanced Stocking Input Bus (ME) set to auto-pull and linked input buses do **NOT** work if they make more than one item type visible per slice. 

At max length, the output bus should replace a solid steel machine casing on layer 1 of the last slice instead of replacing the final input bus. 

Only four input hatches are required because no recipe uses more than four fluids, and Quadruple Input Hatch (EV) Quadruple input hatches do **NOT** work, but there can be gaps between the input hatches if necessary.

#### Base Structure (Minimum requirements)
| Component | Quantity and placement |
| --- | --- |
| Assembly Line | First slice, 3rd layer |
| Borosilicate Glass BlockAny tiered glass | 10, Both sides of 2nd layer |
| Grate Machine Casing | 8, Both sides of 3rd layer |
| Solid Steel Machine Casing | 0-12, Both sides of 1st layer and center of 4th layer |
| Assembly Line Casing | 5, Center of 2nd layer |
| Assembler Machine Casing | 5, Center of 3rd layer |
| Data Access HatchData Access Hatch | 1, Any both sides of 3rd layer but **NOT** on first slice |
| LV Energy HatchOnly Regular Hatches allowed | 1+, Any 4th layer Casings |
| Maintenance HatchMaintenance Hatch | 1+, Any 1st layer side Casings |
| Input Bus (LV)Input Bus | 5, Center of 1st layer |
| Input Hatch (LV)Input Hatch | 0+, Any 1st layer side Casings |
| Output Bus (LV)Output Bus | 1, Last slice's 1st layer side Casings |

#### Each Additional Slice

Each additional slice (1 length) requires these blocks:

| Component | Quantity and placement |
| --- | --- |
| Borosilicate Glass BlockAny tiered glass | 2, Both sides of 2nd layer |
| Grate Machine Casing | 2, Both sides of 3rd layer |
| Solid Steel Machine Casing | 0-3, Both sides of 1st layer and center of 4th layer |
| Assembly Line Casing | 1, Center of 2nd layer |
| Assembler Machine Casing | 1, Center of 3rd layer |
| LV Energy HatchOnly Regular Hatches allowed | 0+, Any 4th layer Casings |
| Input Bus (LV)Input Bus | 1, Center of 1st layer |

Note that the Output Bus (LV)Output Bus must be moved to the last slice when you extend AL slices.

### Wallsharing

ALs may wallshare each of their sides to save on casings, glass, and buses/hatches. That includes any input hatches, maintenance hatches, data access hatches, and output buses. Sharing a data access hatch is particuarly valuable for saving TPS and reducing the amount of data sticks needed.

## Usage

### Scanning Recipes

Simply inserting the inputs of a recipe into the AL (and in the correct order) is not enough for the machine to start processing. Recipes must be explicitly shared with the AL via Data Stick scanned with the necessary information in a singleblock scanner.

To scan the recipe for an Electric Motor (LuV), for example, insert both an IV motor and data stick into a scanner, as seen in the recipe below. The output is a data stick specifically for LuV motors and goes in the Data Access Hatch on the AL. The IV motor is consumed in the process. All data stick recipes and the items to scan for them are visible through NEI. Note that recipes may change with updates of GTNH and would require the player to update their data sticks.

 

Later in the game, the scanner is replaced by the Research Station and Quantum Computer. These two multiblocks work together to unlock the recipes for some of the most advanced items in GTNH.

### Data Access Hatches
There are four types of data access hatches, listed below. There can only be one per AL but they can be safely wallshared between machines.

- Data Access Hatch - Holds up to four data sticks
- Advanced Data Access Hatch - Holds up to sixteen data sticks
- Automatable Data Access Hatch - Holds up to sixteen data sticks and allows for input/output of data sticks.
- Assembly Line Reception Connector - Reads any number of data sticks from a Data Bank.

### Troubleshooting

1. **No Valid Recipe Found.** There are numerous reasons for this error such as missing items, missing fluids, ingredients in the wrong order, more than one output bus, etc. Check that all items are in the correct input bus/hatch.
1. **No Data Sticks Found.** The controller cannot find any data sticks. Either the data access hatch is empty or the data sticks are not scanned with a recipe. Holding shift shows what item the data stick is scanned with, similar to an AE2 pattern.
1. **Recipes keep overlapping.** You likely forgot to either insert a blocking card or enable blocking mode on an interface that stores patterns.

## References

- GTNH Wiki: Assembly Line

text:
# Bacterial Vat

The Bacterial Vat (BV) is an HV tier multiblock for mass fermenting fluids.

Bacteria contained within the vat break down organic compounds into something new, such as Saccharomyces Escherichia turning grape juice into wine. The species of bacteria, and therefore the recipe, is determined by placing a petri dish with a culture inside the controller block of the machine.

The fermenting process itself is closely tied to the carrying capacity of the environment, meaning the output hatch should stay as close as possible to 50% capacity for maximum growth and productivity.

Although the BV is mandatory for progression in UV, the player can later craft all the necessary fluids in the Quantum Force Transformer.

| Property | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Unlock Tier | HV |
| Structure Size (LxWxH) | 5x5x4 |
| Power | Regular |
| Overclocks | Imperfect |
| Maintenance | Need Maintenance |
| Pollution | Produces no pollution |

## Crafting and Construction

### Crafting
(recipes for Bacterial Vat)

(recipes for Clean Stainless Steel Machine Casing)

Radio Hatch is skippable and only needed for recipes that require radiation.

(recipes for Radio Hatch)

### Structure

The BV has one tiered component. The glass determines the **maximum recipe tier, but not the maximum energy hatch tier**.

BV can be rotated or flipped.

Multi-amp and laser energy hatches are not supported, but there can be multiple regular energy hatches for overclocking.

Only one output hatch and one radio hatch are allowed.

Use the Multiblock Structure Hologram Projector to visualize/build the structure with subchannel "glass" to specify the tier of the glass.

| Component | Quantity and placement |
| --- | --- |
| Bacterial Vat | 1, Front bottom center |
| Clean Stainless Steel Machine Casing | 19-45, Whole 1st and 4th layer |
| Borosilicate Glass BlockTiered Glass | 32, 2nd and 3rd layer with a hollow center |
| LV Energy HatchOnly Regular Hatches allowed | 1+, Can replace any casing |
| Maintenance HatchMaintenance Hatch | 1+, Can replace any casing |
| Input Bus (LV)Input Bus | 0+, Can replace any casing |
| Input Hatch (LV)Input Hatch | 1+, Can replace any casing |
| Output Bus (LV)Output Bus | 0+, Can replace any casing |
| Output Hatch (LV)Output Hatch | 1, Can replace any casing |
| Radio Hatch | 0-1, Can replace any casing |

### Wallsharing

BVs may wallshare each of their sides to save on glass, casings, and buses/hatches. That includes both the output hatch and the radio hatch which helps simplify automation setups and save on radioactive materials. If sharing between four machines, one hatch can go on top and the other can go on bottom.

No recipe uses more than 1A of power so it is possible to share one energy hatch between two machines.

## Usage
BV recipes have 4 Requirements to operate: Glass Tier, Voltage, Culture and Radioactive.

You can check these requirements on NEI. For example, the recipe below requires:
- EV+ Glass Tier
- HV+ Voltage
- Need at least 83 sievert
- Requires Petri Dish with a Culture

Note that this is an HV recipe, although it requires at least EV tiered glass to operate.

### Culture
All BV recipes require a specific petri dish with a culture inside the controller block. Petri dishes are acquired from the Basic Bio LabBio Lab, an HV+ singleblock machine for all biotechnology related recipes.

You can check Basic Bio LabBio Lab guide for more information about how to produce a petri dish with a culture.

### Radio Hatch
A few exotic and alien species of bacteria require radiation to survive which is supplied through a radio hatch containing rods or long rods of radioactive materials.

A Radio Hatch is similar to an input bus except it continuously consumes items regardless if a recipe is running or not. Fortunately, the radio hatch can be disabled at any time with a machine controller cover.

The radioactive material inside the radio hatch determines the strength of the radiation in sieverts (sv), but the built in radiation shutter can reduce that by a custom amount. There is no benefit to reducing the sieverts other than needing to have an exact amount for a specific recipe, since material with high sieverts usually has shorter lifespans.

You can control radiation shutter by clicking the screwdriver button on top left of the radio hatch GUI.

Different materials also have different lifespans, but most are quite short. The following table lists a few of the many radioactive materials by their strength, lifespan, and mass.

  | Material | Strength | Lifespan | Mass |
  |----------|----------|-----------|------|
  | Bismuth Rod | 83 sv | 198.80 s | 1 kg |
  | Long Bismuth Rod | ^^ | 397.60 s | 2 kg |
  | Thorium Rod | 90 sv | 98.75 s | 1 kg |
  | Long Thorium Rod | ^^ | 197.50 s | 2 kg |
  | Uranium 235 Rod | 92 sv | 80.850 s | 1 kg |
  | Uranium 238 Rod | ^^ | ^^ | ^^ |
  | Long Uranium 235 Rod | ^^ | 161.70 s | 2 kg |
  | Long Uranium 238 Rod | ^^ | ^^ | ^^ |
  | Plutonium 239 Rod | 94 sv | 66.20 s | 1 kg |
  | Plutonium 241 Rod | ^^ | ^^ | ^^ |
  | Long Plutonium 239 Rod | ^^ | 132.40 s | 2 kg |
  | Long Plutonium 241 Rod | ^^ | ^^ | ^^ |
  | Americium Rod | 95 sv | 59.90 s | 1 kg |
  | Long Americium Rod | ^^ | 119.80 s | 2 kg |
  | Naquadah Rod | 130 sv | 14.40 s | 1 kg |
  | Long Naquadah Rod | ^^ | 28.80 s | 2 kg |
  | Enriched Naquadah Rod | 140 sv | 10.65 s | 1 kg |
  | Long Enriched Naquadah Rod | ^^ | 21.70 s | 2 kg |
  | Naquadria Rod | 150 sv | 7.85 s | 1 kg |
  | Long Naquadria Rod | ^^ | 15.70 s | 2 kg |
  {: widths="200, 60, 60, 60"}

You can enable sound muffling by clicking the sound button in hatch GUI or right-clicking the radio hatch with a hammer.

### Output rate

The BV is a closed system with a limited carrying capacity (K) for bacteria to grow. All closed systems follow a sigmoidal population curve meaning the growth rate is initially slow due to a small starting population, increases in rate as the population grows, and then slows down again as the finite resources in the environment become a limiting factor. **Maximum growth in a closed system occurs at K/2**.

The size of the output hatch on the BV is equivalent to the carrying capacity (K) of the bacterial culture. Very little growth occurs when the output hatch is empty or when the output hatch is close to full. Ideally, the output hatch stays as close as possible to 50% capacity for maximum growth and productivity. More specifically, both the input AND output fluids are multiplied by up to x1,001 based on how close the output hatch is to K/2 or half-full. The solid ingredients and culture are not affected. The multiplier (m) is calculated with the following equation where Fill% is the current fluid level out of the maximum capacity.

This equation is quadratic to reflect the derivative of the sigmoidal population curve. The ceiling operator, however, adds a small buffer around K/2 that rounds up values close to the maximum multiplier, which means the output hatch does not have to be perfectly 50% capacity to achieve the x1,001 gain. Larger output hatches have a larger buffer, but initially require more fluid to reach K/2. It is recommended to start with a very small output hatch and work up to larger sizes as more output fluid is obtained. The following table lists all the different output hatches and their thresholds for earning the maximum x1,001 multiplier (m). The graph visually depicts the general relationship based on the percentage fill level.

  
| Hatch | Minimum | K/2 | Maximum | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ULV | 3,874 L | 4,000 L | 4,126 L | 252 L |
| LV | 7,748 L | 8,000 L | 8,252 L | 504 L |
| MV | 15,495 L | 16,000 L | 16,505 L | 1,010 L |
| HV | 30,989 L | 32,000 L | 33,011 L | 2,022 L |
| EV | 61,977 L | 64,000 L | 66,023 L | 4,046 L |
| IV | 123,953 L | 128,000 L | 132,047 L | 8,094 L |
| LuV | 247,905 L | 256,000 L | 264,095 L | 16,190 L |
| ZPM | 495,810 L | 512,000 L | 528,190 L | 32,380 L |
| UV | 991,619 L | 1,024,000 L | 1,056,381 L | 64,762 L |
| UHV | 1,983,237 L | 2,048,000 L | 2,112,763 L | 129,526 L |
| UEV | 3,966,474 L | 4,096,000 L | 4,225,526 L | 259,052 L |
| UIV | 7,932,947 L | 8,192,000 L | 8,451,053 L | 518,106 L |
| UMV | 15,865,893 L | 16,384,000 L | 16,902,107 L | 1,036,214 L |
| UXV | 31,731,785 L | 32,768,000 L | 33,804,215 L | 2,072,430 L |
| Giant | 48,418,862 L | 50,000,000 L | 51,581,138 L | 3,162,276 L |
{: widths="55, 85, 85, 85, 75"}

  

Note that the multiplier (m) is calculated at the very start of a recipe. This is important when the BV is running continuously because the output from the previous recipe factors into the calculation of the multiplier (m) for the next one. Ideally, the range of optimal production should be greater than the amount of output fluid to guarantee the maximum multiplier.

## References
- GTNH Wiki - Bacterial Vat

Beam Crafters may wallshare each of their sides to save on casings and glass. However, it is not possible to share the beam input hatches due to the restrictions on their locations.

## Usage
The Beam Crafter is the final step in the Large Hadron Collider and captures one or more of the output particle beams for recipes. More specifically, it permanently buffers up to 2B of each particle type and only ever consumes them when a recipe requires them.

There is no passive decay and it does not matter which beam input hatch the particles enter through. **However, particles are only added to the buffer while the Beam Crafter is actively processing a recipe.**

Beam Crafter recipes start immediately upon receiving any valid inputs and only finish when the machine receives enough of the required particles, similar to how the Research Station consumes computation. Therefore, the duration of recipes is strictly determined by the rate at which particles are consumed. It could be instantaneous if there are enough particles stored in the buffer, or last forever if the collision energy of the LHC is not high enough to produce the required particles.

title: gregtech guide: Beam Line
text:
# Beam Line

The **Beam Line** is a series of four ZPM tier multiblocks chained together that engraves wafers with a photon beam and ultra precise masks.

The line begins with the Source Chamber which generates a particle beam from one of seven different source materials.  
The Linear Accelerator (LINAC) then accelerates the particle beam to increase its total energy at the cost of focus.  
The Synchrotron accelerates the particle beam even more until it produces a photon beam from the radiation of the high speed particles.  
The Target Chamber captures the photon beam and carefully focuses it onto wafers to engrave them. 

Each multiblock requires its own power but most of it should be concentrated into the Synchrotron to increase the processing speed of the final recipe. The only other input is coolant for the LINAC and Synchrotron which both perfectly recycle it into hot coolant.

Beam Line can be an alternative method for wafer engraving. Compared with Hyper Intensity Laser Engraver (HILE), Beam Line offers advantages such as the ability to perform serious overclocking using Multi-Amp/Laser Hatches from the point of construction (while HILE can do this on UEV+) and eliminating the need for intermediate processes like Large Chemical Reactor (LCR), but it requires a large amount of material to build, and to produce all wafers, a total of **5** distinct Beam Line multiblocks must be constructed. In addition, while it can save indium and sunnarium by bypassing the LCR, it uses borax and lanthanum as materials instead.

| Property | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Unlock Tier | ZPM |
| Structure Size (LxWxH) | Varies |
| Power | Varies |
| Overclocks | Varies |
| Maintenance | Need Maintenance |
| Pollution | Produces no pollution |

## Crafting and Construction

You can check each multiblock's documents to see how to craft and construct the Beam Line multiblocks.
- Source Chamber
- Linear Accelerator
- Synchrotron
- Target Chamber

### Crafting

Beam Line requires Beam Input Hatch, Beam Output Hatch and Beam Pipe to connect between different Beam Line multiblocks.

(recipes for Beam Input Hatch)

(recipes for Beam Output Hatch)

(recipes for Beam Pipe)

### Structure
Connect the 4 multiblocks in order by using Beam Pipe to make the Beam Line work. Pipes do not need to be colored but they cannot cross or bend.

1. Source Chamber
1. Linear Accelerator
1. Synchrotron
1. Target Chamber

> [!WARNING]
> ALL Beam Line multiblocks require LuV+ Tier Glass Block to operate.

Optionally, you can use the Beam Mirror, Beam Splitter, and/or Beam Stabilizer on UV+ to redirect or optimize the particle beam as necessary. They really only assist with the Large Hadron Collider but they are fully compatible with the Beam Line as well.

## Usage

### Recipes

Beam Line (more precisely, the Target Chamber) recipes in NEI have only a photon, a mask, and doped wafers as input and engraved wafers as output. However, the photon is symbolic and not an actual item or input for the recipe. It is only there to establish that the final particle beam must specifically be a photon beam, not an electron beam or anything else. 

There are also a few extra requirements listed at the bottom of the recipe concerning the characteristics of the particle beam. The energy must be within a particular range, the focus must be greater than or equal to a certain value, and the base amount or rate determines the processing speed of the recipe.

To process the recipe, you must manage Beam Line multiblocks to meet the requirements that recipe demands.

#### Workflow
The general workflow for processing Beam Line recipes is listed below and explained in much more intricate detail in the following subsections about each of the individual multiblocks. 

1. The Source Chamber sets the initial stats of the particle beam based on the input or source material and the voltage of the machine. Check the machine's guide for more details about the particles that each material can create.  
  &b✓ Energy  &b✓ Focus  &b✓ Rate
1. The Linear Accelerator (LINAC) accelerates the particle beam to boost its overall energy at the cost of focus.  
  Increase the length of the LINAC or give it more power to strengthen the effect and reach higher energy levels.  
  Supply cooling fluids to preserve the focus as much as possible in the process. The cooling fluid is returned in a heated state and can be recycled after proper treatment.  
  &a↑ Energy  &c↓ Focus  &7→ Rate
1. The Synchrotron accelerates the particle beam again until it produces a photon beam from the radiation of the high speed particles.  
  Upgrade the antenna casings to keep the beam energy high and increase the beam rate more efficiently.  
  Supply cooling fluids to again preserve the focus as much as possible in the process. The cooling fluid is returned in a heated state and can be recycled after proper treatment.  
  Increasing the power supply increases the rate of the beam without decreasing its energy and focus, which makes the Beam Line easily upgradeable by only increasing the tier and throughput of the Synchrotron's Energy Hatches.  
  Upgrading the Synchrotron's energy hatches is the only way to increase the beam's rate, which determines recipe processing times.  
  &c↓ Energy  &c↓ Focus  &a↑ Rate
1. The Target Chamber captures the final photon beam and does the actual laser engraving.  
  The Target Chamber does not change any of the characteristics of the beam after it leaves the Synchrotron. It only checks that the beam energy and beam focus meet any recipe requirements and uses the beam rate to determine the duration of the recipe. 

### Craftable Wafers
The wide range of beam energy, focus, and rate requirements means that a single Beam Line is not enough for all possible recipes. 

At a minimum, there must be five Beam Lines with varying LINAC lengths, energy hatches, and coolant. The following table lists the recipes that the Beam Line can process, by group.

| Output By Group || Min Power | Beam Energy || Min Focus |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ^^ | ^^ | Min | Max | ^^ |
| 1 | Logic IC (Wafer) | 1,920 EU/t (EV) | 0.5 eV | 4 eV | 35 |
| ^^ | Random Access Memory Chip (Wafer) | 1,920 EU/t (EV) | 2 eV | 4 eV | 40 |
| ^^ | Simple SoC Wafer | 1,920 EU/t (EV) | 2 eV | 4 eV | 25 |
| ^^ | ULPIC Wafer | 1,920 EU/t (EV) | 2 eV | 4 eV | 30 |
| ^^ | LPIC Wafer | 1,920 EU/t (EV) | 2 eV | 4 eV | 30 |
| 2 | SoC Wafer | 1,920 EU/t (EV) | 3 eV | 10 eV | 45 |
| ^^ | QBit Wafer | 1,920 EU/t (EV) | 3 eV | 10 eV | 50 |
| ^^ | NanoCPU Wafer | 1,920 EU/t (EV) | 5 eV | 10 eV | 50 |
| ^^ | PIC Wafer | 1,920 EU/t (EV) | 5 eV | 10 eV | 50 |
| ^^ | Central Processing Unit (Wafer) | 1,920 EU/t (EV) | 6 eV | 12 eV | 45 |
| ^^ | NAND Memory Chip (Wafer) | 1,920 EU/t (EV) | 7 eV | 12 eV | 40 |
| ^^ | NOR Memory Chip (Wafer) | 1,920 EU/t (EV) | 8 eV | 10 eV | 40 |
| 3 | ASoC Wafer | 1,920 EU/t (EV) | 100 eV | 200 eV | 50 |
| ^^ | HPIC Wafer | 1,920 EU/t (EV) | 100 eV | 200 eV | 50 |
| ^^ | UHPIC Wafer | 1,920 EU/t (EV) | 190 eV | 200 eV | 50 |
| 4 | Engraved Lapotron Chip | 30,720 EU/t (LuV) | 1,000 eV | 3,000 eV | 50 |
| ^^ | NPIC Wafer | 1,920 EU/t (EV) | 1,000 eV | 4,000 eV | 50 |
| ^^ | Crystal Processing Unit | 30,720 EU/t (LuV) | 1,000 eV | 3,000 eV | 50 |
| ^^ | Crystal SoC | 30,720 EU/t (LuV) | 2,000 eV | 7,000 eV | 50 |
| 5 | PPIC Wafer | 1,920 EU/t (EV) | 1,500 eV | 10,000 eV | 50 |
| ^^ | QPIC Wafer | 1,920 EU/t (EV) | 3,200 eV | 9,000 eV | 50 |
| ^^ | FPIC Wafer | 1,920 EU/t (EV) | 6,000 eV | 14,000 eV | 50 |
| ^^ | Raw Advanced Crystal Chip | 30,720 EU/t (LuV) | 3,000 eV | 9,000 eV | 55 |
| ^^ | Living Crystal Chip | 30,720 EU/t (LuV) | 5,000 eV | 12,000 eV | 60 |
| ^^ | Crystal SoC (Ce:LuAG) | 30,720 EU/t (LuV) | 5,000 eV | 12,000 eV | 60 |
| ^^ | Raw Advanced Crystal Chip (Ce:LuAG) | 30,720 EU/t (LuV) | 6,000 eV | 14,000 eV | 70 |
{: widths="10, 300, 110, 65, 65, 50"}

As you can see - there are 5 groups for processing, organized by their energy range:
- Group 1 (2-4 eV)
- Group 2 (8-10 eV)
- Group 3 (190-200 eV)
- Group 4 (2,000-3,000 eV)
- Group 5 (6,000-9,000 eV)

Upgrade only the energy hatches on the Synchrotron to scale the throughput of the Beam Lines. Most of the other variables are designed specifically to stay within a particular energy range or above a minimum focus.  
The voltage of the Target Chamber is simply a minimum requirement that has no effect on the operation of the machine, since it does not increase the beam's rate, only its energy.

> [!TIP]
> You may have noticed, but SoC Wafer and QBit Wafer from Group 2 can also be included in Group 1, if Group 1's energy is larger than 3 eV! Just keep an eye on minimal focus requirements.

The Beam Splitter filters and/or splits an input particle beam into 1-4 parts and never shuts down unless manually disabled. Particle beams also do not suffer any penalties or lose any energy/focus when passing through the machine. Only the rate is split evenly between all valid outputs. Fractional rates are always rounded down.

The Beam Splitter perfectly complements the Large Hadron Collider because the latter generates many different types of particles from the same beam output hatches and it would be wasteful for those to all go to the same Beam Crafter.

There is no possible way to join particle beams together so recipes are going to be split across machines and therefore the particles should be too.

# Beam Stabilizer

The Beam Stabilizer is a UV tier multiblock that temporarily buffers particle beams and re-releases them at a custom rate. The Beam Stabilizer does not require any power or maintenance to run, and particle beams passing through also do not suffer any penalties or lose any energy/focus. Only the rate is reduced to the value set in the GUI of the controller, but nothing is ever lost. 

The Beam Stabilizer is completely optional, but may assist with the Beam Line and/or the Large Hadron Collider. Also try the Beam Mirror and Beam Splitter before processing recipes in the Beam Crafter.

### Wallsharing
Beam Stabilizers may wallshare each of their sides to save on casings. However, it is not possible to share the beam input hatch or beam output hatch due to the restrictions on their locations.

## Usage
The Beam Stabilizer temporarily buffers particle beams and re-releases them at a custom rate. It does not require any power or maintenance to run and never shuts down unless manually disabled. Particle beams also do not suffer any penalties or lose any energy/focus when passing through the machine. Only the rate is reduced to the value set in the GUI of the controller, but nothing is ever lost.  
For example, if an electron beam with a rate of 100 enters a Beam Stabilizer with a target beam rate of 40, then the machine first outputs two beams with a rate of 40 and then a beam with a rate of 20.

The buffer has a maximum capacity of 100k particles and ignores any particle beams that do not have the same particle type, energy, or focus. The only stat that could be different is the input beam rate which means the Beam Stabilizer could use the Beam Splitter to filter particle beams prior to them entering the machine. Particles are not added to the buffer or removed from the buffer while the machine is disabled.

# Bose-Einstein Condensate Containment Field

The Bose-Einstein Condensate Containment Field is a UIV tier multiblock for storing entangled condensate in the BEC Line--similar to a fluid tank. 

Entangled condensate is generated in the Entanglement Apparatus and transferred to the Containment Field via BEC hatches. 

Stored condensate is exposed to all Observation Array on the current network and only ever leaves the machine when requested by an IO Node for a recipe.

| Property | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Unlock Tier | UIV |
| Structure Size (LxWxH) | 45x45x17 |
| Power | Any Hatches allowed, includes Multi-Amp and Laser Hatches |
| Overclocks | None |
| Maintenance | No maintenance needed |
| Pollution | Produces no pollution |

## Crafting and Construction
### Crafting
(recipes for Bose-Einstein Condensate Containment Field)

(recipes for Electromagnetic Waveguide)

(recipes for Coherence-Preserving Plasma Conduit)

(recipes for Peace Enforcement Casing)

(recipes for Condensate Guidance Coil)

(recipes for Fine-Structure Constant Manipulator)

(recipes for Electromagnetically-Isolated Casing)

(recipes for Condensate Transformative Coil)

### Structure

The Containment Field has no tiered components. 

Multi-amp and laser energy hatches are supported for greatly increasing the capacity of the machine. 

The Containment Field can be rotated or flipped.

Use the Multiblock Structure Hologram Projector to visualize/build the structure.

Unique to the Containment Field is the Bose-Einstein Condensate Detector Hatch which emits a redstone signal if the set condition inside its GUI is true.  
There is a filter for specifying a particular type of entangled condensate, a comparison operator, and a threshold value.  
For example, emit a redstone signal if entangled infinity condensate is greater than or equal to 100,000L. Leave the filter blank to sum all stored condensates together.

| Component | Quantity and placement |
| --- | --- |
| Bose-Einstein Condensate Containment Field | 1, Front center, 3rd layer |
| Electromagnetic Waveguide | 1236 |
| Coherence-Preserving Plasma Conduit | 1045 |
| Peace Enforcement Casing | 896 |
| Condensate Guidance Coil | 568 |
| Fine-Structure Constant Manipulator | 508 |
| Electromagnetically-Isolated Casing | 439-442 |
| Condensate Transformative Coil | 324-343 |
| LV Energy HatchCan use Regular, Multi-Amp, Laser | 1+, Can replace any Electromagnetically-Isolated Casing |
| Bose-Einstein Condensate Hatch | 1-4, Replaces the Electromagnetically-Isolated Casing on each of the four sides of layer 9 |
| Bose-Einstein Condensate Detector Hatch | 0+, Can replace any Electromagnetically-Isolated Casing |

### Wallsharing

Containment Field may wallshare each of their sides to save lots of blocks, but since the capacity can be increased virtually infinitely with a single Containment Field via the GUI, more than one is generally not built.

## Usage

The Containment Field is the second step in the BEC Line and stores entangled condensate until it is requested by an IO Node for a recipe. Condensate both enters and leaves the Containment Field through BEC hatches on the sides of the structure and is exposed to all Observation Array on the current network. Optionally, use a Maxwell Gate to filter and limit the direction of condensate flow--similar to a diode and fluid filter.

The field strength of the Containment Field is set manually in the GUI of the controller by clicking the "Edit Parameter" button(or with OpenComputers) and determines both the maximum capacity and passive power consumption of the machine; every 1 unit of field strength increases the maximum capacity by 1L at the cost of 1 EU/t. It is not possible to filter or partition the storage based on condensate type.

The maximum capacity is only a soft cap since excess condensate can still enter the Containment Field, but 11% of all condensate is voided each second until it falls back below the maximum capacity. This penalty applies evenly to all stored condensates and never prioritizes any one over the others.  
Avoid this penalty by setting the field strength really high, or by using an unfiltered Bose-Einstein Condensate Detector Hatch to disable the Entanglement Apparatus with a machine controller cover when condensate levels get too high.

> [!CAUTION]
> The Containment Field voids all of its contents if it ever powerfails or is manually disabled. Keep it running at all times while in use unless it is absolutely necessary to shut it down.

If multiple Containment Fields are available on the same network, then the condensate inserted into network is split proportional to their total field strength.  
For example, if one Containment Field has a 150,000 field strength and another has a 50,000 field strength, then the former receives 75% of the condensate and the latter receives only 25% of the condensate.

### OpenComputers Integration

The Containment Field is automatable with OpenComputers and has a few additional functions/methods compared to standard GregTech multiblocks, as seen below. These can be used to dynamically change the field strength of the Containment Field based on the current condensate levels as an extra protection against voiding.

```lua
-- List all available methods for the Containment Field
local component = require('component')
local bec_storage = component.bec_storage

for k,v in pairs(bec_storage) do print(k,v) end

-- Returns all stored condensate as a table mapping fluid names to amounts
bec_storage.getStoredCondensate()

-- Returns the field strength of the Containment Field as a number
bec_storage.getFieldStrength()

-- Sets the field strength of the Containment Field from a number
bec_storage.setFieldStrength(strength)
```
```lua
---@meta

-- Stub for the OpenComputers `bec_storage` component.

---@class BecStorageComponentProxy: ComponentProxy
BecStorageComponentProxy = {}

---Get all condensates stored in **current** Containment Field.
---@return table[string, number] table of condensates stored.
function BecStorageComponentProxy.getStoredCondensate() end

---Get the current field strength of the Containment Field connected.
---@return number current field strength.
function BecStorageComponentProxy.getFieldStrength() end
  
---Config the field strength of the Containment Field. number below 0 will be interpreted as 1.
---@param  strength number
function BecStorageComponentProxy.setFieldStrength(strength) end
```

# Bose-Einstein Condensate Entanglement Apparatus

The Bose-Einstein Condensate Entanglement Apparatus is a UIV tier multiblock for converting fluids into entangled condensate in the BEC Line--similar to an input hatch. 

The Entanglement Apparatus does not overclock but it has unlimited parallels to process as much as possible based on the amount of power provided.  
Multi-amp and laser energy hatches are supported for serious throughput and the Entanglement Apparatus can even entangle different fluids simultaneously but the processing time is always going to be the max duration of the active recipes.  
The EU quota in recipes is simply the required EU/t for each additional parallel but actual consumed EU/t per parallel is only 5% of that value.

| Property | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Unlock Tier | UIV |
| Structure Size (LxWxH) | 34x19x19 |
| Power | Any Hatches allowed, includes Multi-Amp and Laser Hatches |

### Structure

The Entanglement Apparatus has no tiered components. 

The Entanglement Apparatus can be rotated or flipped.

### Wallsharing

The Entanglement Apparatus may wallshare each of its sides to save few blocks, but since Entanglement Apparatus can scale its processing indefinitely with unlimited parallel, and ability to run multiple recipes at once, more than one is generally not built.

## Usage

The Entanglement Apparatus or BEC Generator is the first step in the BEC Line and converts fluids into entangled condensate at the cost of power. The Entanglement Apparatus does not overclock but it has unlimited parallels to process as much as possible based on the amount of power provided.

Insert fluid through an input hatch on the front of the structure.  
The Entanglement Apparatus can entangle different fluids simultaneously but the processing time is always going to be the max duration of the active recipes.  
For example, if molten neutronium (20 ticks) and molten spacetime (60 ticks) are both present and there is enough power to support both of them, then the processing time will be 60 ticks because that is the maximum of the two. If there is not enough power to support both, then priority follows standard multiblock order with colored hatches, location, etc.

The entangled condensate is outputted through the Bose-Einstein Condensate Hatch on the back of the structure and stored in Containment Fields until the Observation Array pulls it into IO Nodes for recipes. The challenge, however, is that the Entanglement Apparatus does not check if there is enough space available for the condensate before it begins processing. It could unintentionally overflow the network's storage and void the condensate if not careful. The solution is using a Bose-Einstein Condensate Detector Hatch on the Containment Field to temporarily disable the Entanglement Apparatus if levels ever get too high, or dynamically adjusting the field strength of the Containment Field with OpenComputers.

If multiple Containment Fields are available on the same network, then the condensate from the Entanglement Apparatus is split proportional to their total field strength. For example, if one Containment Field has a 150,000 field strength and another has a 50,000 field strength, then the former receives 75% of the condensate and the latter receives only 25% of the condensate.

### Recipes

Every recipe consists of a single input fluid, an EU quota for entanglement, and a fixed duration.  
The quota is the required EU/t per parallel but the actual consumed EU/t per parallel is only 5% of that value.  
For example, neutronium has a quota of 7,864,320 EU which means every 7,864,320 EU/t in throughput grants an additional parallel but each one only ever consumes 393,216 EU/t.  
The durations are very long to encourage passive condensate production, and then later filtering for the correct ones with a Maxwell Gate.
