| Magic Automation | Item logistics, inventory control, fluid devices, production support and golem uses |
| Warp and Eldritch Knowledge | Warp management, Eldritch research, Opening the Eye, and exploration of the Outer Lands |
| Thaumic Tinkerer | Custom enchanting, durability repair, infused crops, elemental fire, and KAMI devices |
| Addons and GT Integration | Thaumic Energistics, other addon facilities, and GT's magical devices and material connections |

title: thaumcraft guide: Infusion Crafting
text:
# Infusion Crafting

  

**Infusion Crafting** infuses essentia and surrounding ingredients into a central item to create wand components, magical devices, equipment, and materials for mod integration.
As research progresses, the same altar can also handle equipment upgrades and infusion enchanting.

Using an Infusion Altar requires attention to recipes, stability, and essentia supply.
In GTNH, Thaumic Energistics, Infusion Claws, Infusion Intercepters, and other devices can handle supply and activation, allowing the altar to support continuous production.

## The Infusion Altar

The altar's main structure consists of one Runic Matrix, a central Arcane Pedestal, and four pillars. The pillars are built from Arcane Stone Block and Arcane Stone Bricks, becoming Infusion Pillars when activated with a wand.

The central pedestal sits two blocks directly below the matrix and holds the item being infused. Additional pedestals around it hold the recipe ingredients. The scene shows an activated altar and a set of outer pedestals, which can be expanded to suit recipes.

- **Structure activation:** Complete Infusion research, build the structure shown in the Thaumonomicon, and right-click the matrix with a wand. Leave the empty spaces within the main structure clear; logistics devices can be connected after activation.
- **Outer pedestal range:** Pedestals must be below the matrix, within 8 blocks along each horizontal axis, X and Z, and no more than 10 blocks below it.
- **Pedestal layers:** Only one outer pedestal is recognized per vertical column. Offset their horizontal positions when using multiple layers.
- **Space allocation:** Leave room below the central pedestal for an essentia connection and below the surrounding pedestals for item logistics. An Infusion Claw can be installed above the matrix.

## Recipes and the Crafting Process

An infusion recipe requires a central item, outer ingredients, the specified essentia, and the relevant research completed by the player activating it. The Thaumonomicon and NEI show the current recipe's items, essentia quantities, and instability.

A standard altar first draws essentia, then absorbs the outer ingredients one by one. The finished item remains on the central pedestal. Outer ingredient positions can be rearranged, provided their types and quantities match the recipe.

> [!WARNING]
> A standard altar does not check that all required essentia is available before starting. Missing essentia or ingredients knocked off pedestals stall the ritual while risk checks continue, increasing instability or essentia requirements. Prepare the essentia and ingredients and check altar stability before crafting.

Each outer ingredient entry occupies a separate pedestal. When a recipe requires the same ingredient several times, multiple pedestals are needed for matching. Returned containers or reusable ingredients may remain on their pedestals; arrange their collection for batch production.

## Pedestal Layout and Stability

The altar checks central symmetry: two positions at the same height correspond when rotated 180° around the matrix's vertical axis. For example, a pedestal three blocks east and one block north of the matrix pairs with one three blocks west and one block south.

- **Pair pedestals:** Each outer pedestal should have a corresponding pedestal on the opposite side. Empty pedestals also count toward symmetry.
- **Pair occupied positions:** Two opposite pedestals remain balanced when both hold ingredients, which can be different items. Additional stabilizers can compensate for the occupancy imbalance caused by an odd number of ingredients.
- **Remove unused ingredients:** Items on other pedestals within range participate in recipe matching. Leaving ingredients from another craft may prevent the recipe from being recognized.
- **Check after adjustments:** Use an Arcane Abacus after adding or removing pedestals, moving stabilizers, or connecting addon devices.

The recipe's instability and the altar's environmental modifier together determine the initial risk of the ritual. Stabilizers should offset the target recipe's risk and leave a margin for shortages and automatic activation devices.

An Arcane Abacus reads the matrix's stability, identifies unpaired stabilizers, and shows risk and essentia cost information for the current or available recipe.
Arrange the pedestals and stabilizers first, then place the target recipe's ingredients to check the result.

## Placing Stabilizers

Stabilizers include candles, skulls, crystals, and suitable blocks from addons. Blocks with a tooltip indicating that they can stabilize an Infusion Altar can be found in NEI and used around the altar.

A Quicksilver Block is a common choice in GTNH and suits a foundation with multiple layers of stabilizers. Candles, skulls, and other valid stabilizers can also be used according to the materials available.

- **Effective range:** Up to 12 blocks along each of the X and Z axes, 5 blocks above, and 10 blocks below the matrix.
- **Pairing:** Place valid stabilizers at the same height in positions centrally symmetric about the matrix. Unpaired stabilizers increase instability.
- **Multiple layers:** Each layer needs its own symmetry. Stabilizers can be placed beneath the altar to leave space at ground level for access and logistics.
- **Central column:** The vertical column directly above and below the matrix is excluded from ordinary stabilizer symmetry checks.

Every 10 ordinary stabilizers placed in pairs provide 1 point of stability in total. For larger foundations, keep each layer's boundary complete and use an Arcane Abacus to locate missing blocks.

Other valid blocks within the stabilizer range also count. Nearby decorations, another altar's stabilizers, and blocks added later can affect the existing altar's stability.

## Essentia Supply

A standard altar draws the required aspects from essentia sources near the matrix. Each Warded Jar holds 64 points; prepare several jars of the same type when an aspect's requirement exceeds one jar.

- **Jar supply:** Suitable for a small set of recipes or occasional infusions. Prepare each required aspect separately.
- Essentia Mirror: Linked pairs supply the altar with essentia from a distant storage area.
- Infusion Provider: Once connected to an ME network, it lets the altar draw essentia from network stocks. Place it within the altar's draw range to reduce jar transport.

When a required aspect is out of stock, an Infusion Provider can request essentia autocrafting in batches of 32 points.
This requires an available pattern and crafting CPU. Keeping common aspects in stock reduces waiting during continuous infusion.

A standard matrix still draws essentia in successive steps. More aspect types and larger quantities make this stage take longer. Recipes with high essentia demand can use an Infusion Intercepter or Advanced Infusion Provider.

Refer to the "Alchemy and Essentia" chapter for production, storage, and transport. When several altars share stocks, account for their combined demand during simultaneous operation.

## Infusion Accidents and Losses

Unstable infusions can knock ingredients off pedestals, destroy ingredients, release Flux, or harm nearby entities.
Missing ingredients delay crafting, increasing the chance of further accidents.

- **Destroyed ingredients:** Replace the missing items. For valuable recipes, prepare spare outer ingredients where possible.
- **Essentia stops flowing:** Check which aspects the matrix still needs, jar contents, provider stocks, and supply paths.
- **Essentia demand increases:** Replenish the quantities currently required by the ritual and address the shortage. Further waiting may cause additional losses.
- **Flux spills:** Place Flux cleanup devices near the altar and leave access for replenishing ingredients and collecting items.

> [!WARNING]
> Essentia and ingredients already absorbed are not automatically returned when an infusion is interrupted. Removing or replacing the central item may terminate the ritual. Automatic product collection should also wait until crafting is complete to avoid extracting the input early.

If accidents recur, improve altar stability and resolve supply problems before consuming more materials. For high-risk recipes, reduce the time spent waiting for essentia or missing ingredients.

## Infusion Enchanting

After completing **Infusion Enchantment** research, the altar can apply supported enchantments to tools, weapons, and armor. These recipes require experience as well as items and essentia, drawing it from players near the altar.

- **Higher enchantment levels:** Repeat the same enchantment until its permitted maximum level. Higher levels require more essentia and experience.
- **Existing enchantments:** Other enchantments on the item increase resource costs and instability. Check the base requirements in the book against the target item's current state.
- **Applicability and compatibility:** Enchantment rules still determine whether an enchantment applies to an item and can coexist with its existing enchantments.

When preparing a set of equipment, plan the processing order around the desired final enchantments and use an Arcane Abacus to check the costs for the current item. Equipment with several enchantments benefits from an altar with a larger stability margin.

NH's addons also provide devices such as the Osmotic Enchanter and Overchanting Table. Their recipes, resource costs, and level rules are described in their own research entries.

## Automatic Activation and Item Logistics

An Infusion Claw is installed above the Runic Matrix. With a wand or staff inside, it can trigger infusion through a redstone signal from a side. The device is bound to its owner and uses that player's research for recipe recognition.

The Infusion Claw needs Vis replenishment for its wand and can receive power from a Centi-Vis network.
It adds instability to the rituals it activates. A wand with greater capacity or a suitable staff reduces this effect.

Item automation mainly handles the following tasks:

- **Central item allocation:** Send the central item and outer ingredients to their assigned pedestals. Maintain correct allocation rules when several recipes share an altar.
- **Individual outer inputs:** Each ingredient entry needs a pedestal, including repeated occurrences of the same ingredient.
- **Activation control:** Trigger the Infusion Claw after the ingredients are in place. For continuous production, wait for the previous craft to finish.
- **Product collection:** Identify and extract the finished item from the central pedestal. Also handle containers or reusable ingredients left on outer pedestals.

An ME network can manage inputs and products, while redstone, OC, or other control devices coordinate activation and collection.
Handle returned containers or leftover ingredients before the next craft begins to prevent continuous production from stalling.

For Centi-Vis sources and connections, see Wands, Vis and Nodes.

## Increasing Infusion Speed

An Infusion Intercepter is installed directly below the central pedestal and receives essentia through its bottom face.
Connect essentia tubes or a Thaumic Energistics Essentia Provider below it to send the required essentia directly into the corresponding Runic Matrix.

With an ME Essentia Provider and sufficient stocks at the input, it can supply large amounts of essentia very quickly. With tubes, actual supply speed limits its performance. It serves only the altar directly above it; activate the main altar structure before installing it.

An Advanced Infusion Provider supplies all required essentia to an active infusion at once and requests autocrafting for the quantities missing.
It can bind to multiple matrices within 12 blocks along each of the X and Z axes and 5 blocks vertically.

- **Infusion Intercepters** provide fast essentia supply for individual altars.
- **Advanced Infusion Providers** let multiple altars share network stocks and essentia autocrafting.
- **World Accelerators** can speed up matrix operation further, but first ensure adequate stability and supply. Acceleration during shortages also speeds up risk checks while the ritual is stalled.

Once essentia supply takes less time, absorbing outer ingredients individually still contributes to crafting time. To expand production, arrange multiple altars according to the number of recipes and ingredients, with complete input and collection control for each.

## Troubleshooting

- **Right-clicking with a wand does not start infusion:** Check structure activation, research completion, the central item and outer ingredients, and any unrelated ingredients left within range.
- **Some outer ingredients are not recognized:** Check whether their pedestals are below the matrix, within range, and share a vertical column with another pedestal.
- **Risk remains high after placing stabilizers:** Use an Arcane Abacus to check asymmetric positions, stabilizer range, and occupied outer pedestals. Include the extra instability from an Infusion Claw when using one.
- **An Infusion Claw does not start the recipe:** Check the owner's research, the inserted wand, power supply, and redstone trigger, then verify the recipe ingredients on the altar.
- **An Intercepter supplies no essentia:** Check that it is directly below the central pedestal, its bottom face connects to a valid essentia source, and the source contains the required aspects.
- **Automation completes only the first craft:** Check collection of the central product and outer leftovers, allocation of the next set of ingredients, and whether the activation signal triggers again.

title: thaumcraft guide: Magic Automation
text:
# Magic Automation

  

Thaumcraft and **Automagy** provide facilities for item collection, inventory monitoring, transport over long distances, and fluid supply.
They can connect to existing pipes, ME networks, and redstone controls to handle particular parts of a production system.

Their main uses involve collection and distribution, inventory conditions, spatial transport, and production support.

## Item Collection and Distribution

**Collecting dropped items**

A Hungry Chest absorbs dropped items that touch it. Placed where a device ejects items, it collects products into an inventory for existing logistics to extract.

**Taking items from adjacent inventories**

A Greedy Chest watches for items added to neighboring inventories and transfers a portion into itself according to its settings.
Its default share is 50%. Open its settings with a wand to select extraction directions and operating modes.

- **Proportional distribution:** Take a chosen share of inputs to an adjacent inventory, dividing one source between different uses.
- **Maintaining stock:** Take items according to a target quantity, keeping a fixed supply for a branch of the production line.
- **Taking surplus:** Leave the required stock in an adjacent inventory and take the amount above the threshold.
- **Item filtering:** Use a Runic Whitelist or Runic Blacklist to select which items participate in distribution.

A Greedy Chest will not take items from a hopper directly beneath it. Transfers between two Greedy Chests also depend on their direction settings.
When using one beside a machine's recipe buffer, configure directions and filters first to avoid diverting required ingredients.

**Preserving item samples**

A Tenacious Chest preserves samples of each item type, preventing automation that follows its extraction rules from removing them all.
It attempts to split one item into a separate stack so the remaining stock can continue to be extracted. Players can still remove the reserved items manually.

This container suits seeds, saplings, and sorting samples. Once configured, logistics can continuously extract surplus stock while preserving samples needed to restart production or identify items.

## Mirrors and Transport over Long Distances

Linked pairs of Magic Mirror blocks transfer items over long distances and even between dimensions. Items can be thrown into a mirror or inserted through logistics. The receiving end needs an inventory or item collection device to handle the output.

Standard Magic Mirrors link in pairs. When removed, they retain their previous pairing information and can also be linked to a new target. After moving a mirror, check its receiving location and collection facilities.

Large amounts of continuous traffic build up strain on the mirrors, reducing output speed. This strain fades over time, and Ordo essentia can also help remove it.
When multiple production lines share a collection point, account for both mirror throughput and the receiving end's processing capacity.

**Sending items home while traveling**

A Magic Hand Mirror can be carried with you. Once bound to a fixed Magic Mirror, its interface sends items back to that location.
It is useful for sending items to the base while exploring, gathering resources, or moving supplies. Existing collection and sorting systems can receive them at the base.

**Combining multiple sources**

A Melding Mirror only accepts inputs. Use a Crystalline Eye to select a Magic Mirror that is already paired, connecting the device to that mirror transport channel.

Multiple Melding Mirrors can send items from different locations to a shared collection point, serving scattered farms, processing devices, and distant gathering sites. The target Magic Mirror must retain a valid pairing, and the output end needs continuous item collection.

> [!WARNING]
> Mirror outputs may produce dropped items. The receiving end's collection facilities, storage capacity, and output speed should handle the actual throughput to prevent items from remaining on the ground and despawning. Confirm the receiving location before sending valuable materials through mirrors.

## Inventory Monitoring and Automatic Control

**Signals based on item quantities**

A Tally Box reads items in a target inventory and outputs a redstone signal according to conditions set by a Runic Whitelist or Blacklist. It faces the inventory being checked and outputs the signal in the opposite direction.

Connect the result to a production device's redstone control to replenish low stocks, stop at a target quantity, or trigger another device once a set of materials is ready.

Tally Boxes can also use lenses to change what they detect:

- Tally Box Lens: Unbound: Detects loose items at the target location, allowing checks for a backlog at a collection point.
- Tally Box Lens: Yield: Checks the target block's possible drops, including ordinary and Silk Touch results, allowing the presence of a particular block to become a trigger condition.

**Reading inventories remotely**

A Remote Comparator uses a Crystalline Eye to bind to a target and reads the comparator state of an inventory or compatible block within 20 blocks. This lets detection devices sit near the control wiring, leaving the inventory's sides available for logistics connections.

Placed above a Tally Box, a Remote Comparator passes information about items in a distant inventory to the box for evaluation. Tally Boxes and Remote Comparators can also relay target information through a chain, carrying inventory conditions to more distant control points.

**Detecting entity counts**

A Signum Entia detects entities of a selected type within range, with their number affecting signal strength.
Use an Oculo Anima to select the target type. Adult or baby animals can be selected separately, making the device useful for breeding, slaughter, and other facilities controlled by entity counts.

The maximum detection area is 11×11×11. Solid blocks around the device change the detection directions and area: blocking one face limits detection in that direction and extends it toward the opposite side. Glass, water, and similar blocks do not obstruct detection in the same way.
When placing it near animal pens, check its coverage against the walls.

**Timed activation**

A Magic Hourglass provides repeatable timing and redstone output.
It can produce pulses when timing ends, continuous signals while timing, alternating output, and brief interruptions. Input signals can also start, reset, or stop the timer.

A Magic Hourglass provides timing for intermittent supply, periodic collection, or device activation. After adjusting its timing and modes with a wand, combine it with inventory conditions to decide when a device may operate.

**Redcrystal wiring**

Redcrystal can be attached to different block faces and connect around corners. A wand adjusts connections to neighboring redcrystal, helping route controls around compact installations.

- Amplified Redcrystal: Amplifies an incoming signal and outputs it in a selected direction.
- Dim Redcrystal: Limits the maximum output signal strength.
- Dense Redcrystal: Passes only signals that meet the chosen minimum strength.
- Resonating Redcrystal: When two crystals face each other, they transmit signals through space along a straight line, up to 15 blocks apart.
- Mercurial Redcrystal: Transmits redstone signals through paired Magic Mirrors. Bind each end to its corresponding mirror and place it within 8 blocks of that mirror.

Mercurial Redcrystal can send inventory conditions from the receiving end back to distant production lines, coordinating supply and collection through mirror logistics.

## Fluid Collection and Supply

A Thirsty Tank has a default capacity of 16,000 mB. It collects and stores one fluid type and can connect to fluid pipes. It absorbs connected liquids that can be collected with a bucket, finding sources through connected regions of the same liquid.

GTNH's default configuration preserves adjacent water sources, allowing a tank beside a source to draw water continuously. The current configuration also lets exposed tanks collect rainwater. For other fluids, position the tank according to the pool's connectivity.

**Adding functions with glyphs**

Each of a Thirsty Tank's six faces can hold one glyph. The chosen face matters for directional functions. Capacity, speed, and disposal effects can be configured as needed.

- Glyph of Siphoning: Outputs fluid to the container in that face's direction.
- Glyph of Envy: Takes fluid from the container in that face's direction.
- Glyph of Temperance: Performs active collection only while receiving a redstone signal.
- Glyph of Preservation: Retains some fluid to prevent the tank from being completely emptied.
- Glyph of the Guzzler: Increases collection frequency. Multiple glyphs of this type increase it further.
- Glyph of the Reservoir: Adds 16,000 mB of capacity per glyph.

Glyphs of Siphoning and Envy supply fluid between adjacent containers. A Glyph of Temperance can connect to inventory monitoring or production controls. To maintain a fixed fluid type, a Glyph of Preservation leaves a reserve that keeps the tank bound to that type.

> [!WARNING]
> A Glyph of the Void accepts and destroys fluid beyond the tank's capacity, while a Glyph of Consumption continuously destroys fluid inside it. When arranging fluid recovery or byproduct handling, ensure fluids you need to preserve do not enter tanks configured for disposal.

**Automatic milking**

With a Glyph of the Bovine installed, the tank searches for cows in the glyph's direction and collects milk, stopping its usual collection of surrounding liquids. Cows must be inside the relevant detection area, and the tank needs space for the output and a way to extract it.

In NH, each cow has a milking cooldown of 2000 game ticks, or about 100 seconds at normal speed. The cooldown is stored on the cow, so multiple tanks sharing one cow are subject to the same limit. Glyphs of the Guzzler increase search frequency; sustained output also depends on the number of cows available to milk in rotation.

## Production Support

**Accelerating crop growth**

A Lamp of Growth uses Plant (Herba) essentia to accelerate plants within its effective light coverage. It supports farms of ordinary crops such as wheat, carrots, and potatoes, with harvesting and collection handled by existing devices.

Position it so the light covers the planted area and maintain a supply of Herba.

**Animal breeding**

A Lamp of Fertility consumes Life (Victus) essentia to put eligible animals within range into breeding mode. Once eight or more animals of a species are present, the lamp stops encouraging that species to breed.

Combine it with a Signum Entia and existing animal harvesting devices so breeding, population control, and product processing each handle one part of the system. Baby animals within range also count toward the limit, so pen layout and downstream processing speed affect continuous production.

**Directional mining**

An Arcane Bore is installed above or below an Arcane Bore Base. With a Wand Focus: Excavation and pickaxe inserted, redstone controls mining in the selected direction.

Enchantments on the focus and pickaxe affect performance, while pickaxe durability affects how long operation can continue. Products leave through the base's output port or enter an inventory placed there. After changing direction, check the mining path and output position.

Entropy (Perditio) essentia or the corresponding Centi-Vis increases drilling speed. Arrange the direction, tools, and collection facilities around the area to be mined, with Centi-Vis supplied by an existing node network.

### Additional Golem Uses

Golems can supplement transport, harvesting, and item interactions between devices. Their installed core determines their work. Use a Golemancer's Bell to bind inventories, locations, and work targets.

- **Alchemy cores** transport essentia between alembics, jars, and compatible devices.
- **Harvest cores** handle compatible mature crops, using suitable upgrades to replant. Collection devices can gather the drops.
- **Use cores** simulate clicks with an item or an empty hand, serving targets that support these interactions.

When using a golem, choose its core, material, and upgrades for the task and leave a path to its targets. Once devices handle collection, distribution, and inventory control, golems can handle the remaining interactions.

title: thaumcraft guide: Thaumcraft Basics
text:
# Thaumcraft Basics

  

In Thaumcraft, stones, trees, creatures and even machines can all be described through aspects.
Through observation and research, thaumaturges learn to understand these properties, then use wands, alchemy and infusion to turn that knowledge into useful tools and facilities.

Aura nodes in the world provide magical energy, while the aspects within items provide materials for alchemy. Delving into forbidden knowledge can also bring Warp upon the researcher.
Together, these concepts form the world of Thaumcraft: **essentia, Warp, magical energy and aspects** are connected, but have different storage locations, sources and uses.
Aspects appear repeatedly in item descriptions, research tables, wands, nodes and recipes. Understanding an aspect means considering both where it appears and which aspects it can combine to form.

## Aspects

**Aspects** describe an object's composition and properties. They can represent natural attributes such as air and earth, as well as concepts such as life, metal and order.
Here, "composition" refers not only to the materials an object is made from, but also to its magical tendencies and meaning. Creatures, tools and magical items can therefore all be described using the same system.

The six primal aspects are aspectrecipeindex:aspect:1:{Aspect:Air (Aer), aspectrecipeindex:aspect:1:{Aspect:Earth (Terra), aspectrecipeindex:aspect:1:{Aspect:Fire (Ignis), aspectrecipeindex:aspect:1:{Aspect:Water (Aqua), aspectrecipeindex:aspect:1:{Aspect:Order (Ordo) and aspectrecipeindex:aspect:1:{Aspect:Entropy (Perditio).
They form the foundation of the aspect system. Compound aspects are formed by combining two other aspects.
For example, aspectrecipeindex:aspect:1:{Aspect:Life (Victus) is composed of Earth and Water.

Compound aspects can themselves contain other compound aspects, creating a network of relationships that extends through multiple layers.Connections in research notes follow these relationships. Understanding how aspects relate to one another helps explain both research connections and how alchemical materials provide essentia.

**The aspects contained in an item and the combinations that form an aspect are two different kinds of information.** The former tells you which aspects an item provides and in what amounts; the latter tells you which two aspects make up a compound aspect.An item can contain several aspects in different amounts. Different items may provide the same aspect, so there are often several possible materials for producing a particular type of essentia.

Addons also expand the aspect system. When you encounter an unfamiliar aspect, its name, composition and presence in actual items are more useful than simply memorizing every icon.**Discovering an aspect means you understand it; having research points for that aspect means you have a corresponding resource to spend on research.**

## The Thaumonomicon

Thaumonomiconis the main source of knowledge in Thaumcraft.It organizes research entries by topic and addon, recording lore, item uses, requirements and recipes. Completed research can be consulted at any time, while unfinished research shows the directions you can explore next.

Research in the book is not a collection of independent recipes. Connections between entries indicate prerequisites: a research may build on basic knowledge or require knowledge from several different areas.Some entries also require specific scans, other conditions or discoveries related to Eldritch knowledge before they appear. **An entry being absent does not necessarily mean that its content is missing from the modpack.**

Research can be completed in different ways. Entries that require research notes involve studying a note at a research table, completing its aspect connections, then obtaining and reading the resulting discovery.Other research unlocks directly by consuming the required research points. Both grant knowledge, but their resource costs and completion methods differ.

The Thaumonomicon reflects the player's research progress. Owning a book is the beginning of a thaumaturgical journey; unlocking research and obtaining items should be understood separately.

In GTNH, research progress is also closely connected to material processing, other magic mods and GT machines.
The book is useful for understanding mechanics and research relationships, while actual recipes should also be checked against the current instance's NEI and quest book. Some descriptions retained from the original mod do not fully reflect GTNH's changes.

## Scanning, Research Points and Aspects

Thaumometeris used to examine the aspects of items, blocks and creatures, and can also reveal aura nodes.Scanning yields research points from an object's aspects, reveals which aspects it contains and sometimes provides clues to new research.

Some objects cannot yet be scanned because their aspects are not understood. Aspect knowledge follows composition relationships, so researchers must first understand the relevant basic and component aspects before they can understand more complex objects. This is why exploration and research support each other.

**Research points** are recorded for each player by aspect type. They are the resource used by the research table and some directly unlocked research. The amounts of aspectrecipeindex:aspect:1:{Aspect:Air, aspectrecipeindex:aspect:1:{Aspect:Earth and other aspects shown in the research tableindicate the remaining research points for each aspect. Placing aspects in research notes costs research points; combining aspects to obtain points for a compound aspect also consumes points for its component aspects.

Aspect connections in research follow direct composition relationships. For example, Life is composed of Earth and Water, so Life is connected to both Earth and Water. **Understanding these relationships is knowledge; placing the aspects also requires research points.** Knowing an aspect without having its research points still prevents you from using it in research.

Scanning is an important source of research points, but repeatedly scanning the same kind of object cannot provide an unlimited supply. As research progresses, other ways to obtain research points or assist with research become available. The Vis stored in your wand and the essentia jars in your base do not directly determine your research point reserves.

## Vis: Magical Energy

Vis is an important term for magical energy in Thaumcraft. Energy drawn from nodes is stored in wands as Vis, mainly for arcane crafting, wand foci and similar uses. In Thaumcraft's lore, both Vis and essentia are related to aspects separated from objects and purified. In practice, wand reserves, device power supplies and essentia containers need to be distinguished.

**Wands store Vis separately for each of the six primal aspects.** Each has its own current reserve and capacity. If a recipe requires Air and Order, having more Fire cannot make up for missing Order.

Wands both store and use magical energy. Wand caps, rods and related equipment can affect capacity or the Vis cost of applicable operations. When reading a recipe, consider the required aspect types, their amounts and whether your current wand can meet those requirements.

## Vis Discounts

> [!NOTE]
> **Vis discounts** are a very important mechanic in GTNH. They reduce the Vis consumed by applicable operations.

The actual Vis cost of the same recipe can be reduced by using different wands or equipment. Discounts do not change the required aspect types, however, and the same discount does not necessarily apply to every magical system. Vis discounts cannot solve insufficient essentia, missing crafting materials or locked research.
In GTNH, crafting a wand with a higher Vis capacity often requires stacking discounts to meet the minimum requirements for crafting that wand.

## Aura Nodes

**Aura** is the magical energy present throughout the world, while **aura nodes** are concentrations of that energy. A node is more than a special object to scan: it contains particular aspect types and amounts, and is an important source of Vis for wands.

Goggles of Revealingprovide magical sight that helps you locate aura nodes.

> [!NOTE]
> Previously scanned nodes can be looked up with the I key.

When examining a node, distinguish its aspect composition, reserves and condition. The aspects it provides determine which magical energy it can replenish, while their amounts indicate the scale of its reserves.Its type and quality affect its properties and ability to supply energy. Most nodes replenish drained energy over time, but their recovery and uses are not all the same.

Aura nodes have six types and four quality states. The type determines a node's special effects, while its quality determines how quickly its aspects regenerate.
The core's appearance helps identify its type; scanning the node with a Thaumometer also reveals the type's name.

  

| Type | Description | Core Appearance | Effects |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Normal | The most common and ordinary type, with a stable core and no special effects. | White | None |
| Sinister | A relatively dangerous node type.Usually generated alongside obsidian totems, Eldritch altars, barrows or elven altars. | Dark purple | Gradually changes biomes in a 25×25 area centered on itself to Eerie.When a player enters within 24 blocks, it can spawn Furious Zombies in an 11×3×11 area in low light. |
| Pure | Usually generated inside Silverwood trees. | White,turbine-like | Changes Tainted Land within its range to Magical Forest.Those inside Silverwood trees can change any surrounding biome to Magical Forest. |
| Tainted | Naturally generated in Tainted Land. A non-Pure node in Tainted Land can also become Tainted over time. | Purple,smoky | Changes biomes in a 15×15 area centered on itself to Tainted Land.Also generates tainted growth on block surfaces within a 9×9×9 area. |
| Unstable | Similar to a Normal node, but its core constantly pulses. | White,radiating | Every 5 seconds, has a 50% chance to convert one stored point of a primal aspect into an aspect orb and release it. |
| Hungry | The rarest and most dangerous node type, appearing very rarely through natural world generation. | White,ring-shaped | Draws in and devours everything within 16 blocks, absorbing its aspects to increase the node's aspect capacity. |

  

- **Normal (not displayed): regenerates one aspect point every 30 seconds.**
- **Bright: regenerates one aspect point every 20 seconds and appears more vivid than a Normal node.**
- **Pale: regenerates one aspect point every 45 seconds and appears dimmer than a Normal node.**
- **Fading: does not regenerate aspects, appears extremely dim and flickers constantly.**

**A node's reserves and a wand's reserves are independent.** Drawing energy transfers Vis provided by the node into the wand. Spending Vis from a wand does not mean that a node will automatically refill it. A node that provides only some aspects cannot supply all the energy required by every recipe on its own.

Nodes usually contain primal aspects, but may also contain compound aspects. Their icons describe their magical composition; they do not make nodes into research point stores or essentia jars. Finding, scanning and using nodes involve observation, research rewards and actual energy supply respectively.

> [!WARNING]
> Draining an aspect from a node to zero with a wand can damage the node or even remove that aspect. Exhausting every aspect can make the node disappear entirely. The ability to regenerate magical reserves does not mean that damage to the node will automatically heal. Consider the node protection abilities you have unlocked when assessing charging risks.

Further node research introduces uses such as moving and stabilizing nodes. Device power systems require attention to node output and the facilities that supply the energy, and are related to the Vis stored and consumed in wands.

Replenishing multiple aspects in a wand and establishing a power supply for fixed devices have different requirements. A node's composition, condition and unlocked uses should all be considered in relation to its intended purpose.

## Essentia

Essentia consists of aspects separated and refined from items. It can be stored, transported and used through the appropriate containers and facilities.It turns an item's magical properties into a production resource that can be managed centrally, and is an important requirement for alchemy, infusion and some magical devices.

The aspects contained in a material determine which essentia it can provide. An item with several aspects may yield several types of essentia, while a recipe usually needs only some of them.Essentia production therefore involves more than material quantities: it also involves which aspects are needed, what additional output is produced and whether those products can be stored and used properly.

Essentia can belong to primal or compound aspects. Air, Life and Metal essentia are all resources classified by their corresponding aspects.Wands store only the six primal aspects separately, while essentia systems handle a wider range of types. Their containers and supply methods also differ.

Storage and availability should also be distinguished. Having a type of essentia in your base means you own that resource; whether a device can access it still depends on the appropriate containers, transport facilities and supply conditions.

## Arcane Crafting, Alchemy and Infusion

After research is unlocked, crafting still follows the requirements of its particular system. These systems share the language of aspects, but differ in how they obtain magical energy, consume materials and receive resources. When reading a recipe, first identify which system it belongs to.

**Alchemy** focuses on transformations between items and aspects. A Crucible breaks down added items into their aspects; a suitable catalyst then combines with the aspects required by a recipe to produce the target item. Understanding alchemy therefore involves knowing what the materials provide, what the recipe consumes and how unused aspects are handled.

**Infusion** imbues a central item with the properties of other items and with essentia. The infusion altar, placement of ingredients and essentia supply together form the conditions for this process. A wand can be used to start it, but the required essentia must come from the appropriate sources.

Infusion also involves stability and risks during the process. Completing the recipe's research and apparently having all the materials does not guarantee a smooth craft.Insufficient essentia or missing ingredients can stall crafting and increase the chance of unexpected events. Stability and supply conditions will be discussed further in the infusion guide.

## Warp and Forbidden Knowledge

**Warp** is an influence upon the researcher. Some Thaumcraft knowledge concerns forbidden and Eldritch subjects. Researching these subjects, as well as certain crafting activities or other actions, can change the researcher's mind and body. Warp is borne by the player.

The Thaumonomicon records both ordinary research and forbidden knowledge. Forbidden research carries corresponding warnings and purple effects, and learning it can increase Warp.A research entry's prerequisites, benefits and forbidden knowledge warnings are therefore all relevant to understanding it.

The relationship between Warp and knowledge also works in the other direction: discovering and unlocking some Eldritch knowledge depends on the player's Warp state and related events.Unusual events are not always purely negative; they can sometimes provide new insights. Forbidden research can cause Warp, while Warp can help a researcher encounter deeper knowledge, creating a connection between the two.

Warp can be divided into three types:

- Temporary Warp: can gradually fade.
- Sticky Warp: does not naturally fade like temporary Warp and requires appropriate methods to remove.
- Permanent Warp: does not naturally fade; dealing with it in NH depends on additional research and methods.

Warp can manifest as hallucinations, physical discomfort, unusual creatures or other events. Their severity depends on the player's Warp level.
Higher Warp brings more effects and causes Warp events to occur more frequently.

The **Warp Ward** buff can protect the player from Warp effects.

> [!WARNING]
> Warp Theory expands the range of Warp events in GTNH. High Warp can cause dangerous events that may damage your base.

## Warp and Environmental Pollution

Warp mainly describes effects upon the player, while **Flux** and **Taint** concern magical hazards in the environment.Wasteful or abnormal magical processes can generate Flux, such as aspects left unused in a Crucible. Taint affects terrain, blocks and creatures. Contact with Flux can also cause adverse status effects that affect magic use.

## How the Concepts Relate

| Concept | Where It Is Recorded or Exists | Connections to Other Concepts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Aspects | The magical properties of items and other objects, and composition relationships used in research | Provide a shared classification system for research, Vis and essentia |
| Research points | The player's research resources, recorded by aspect | Used for research; costs are not paid with wand Vis or stored essentia |
| Unlocked research | The player's knowledge progress, consulted through the Thaumonomicon | Grants knowledge and crafting access without also supplying materials or magical energy |
| Wand Vis | Magical energy stored separately in a wand for each of the six primal aspects | Can be drawn from nodes and used for arcane crafting, foci and similar purposes |
| Aura nodes | Concentrations of magical energy in the world | Provide energy for wands and, after further research, can also supply devices |
| Essentia | Appropriate containers and magical production facilities | Obtained from aspects in materials and used for alchemy, infusion and some devices |
| Warp | A state borne by the player | Can result from forbidden research and other actions, and is also connected to the discovery of some Eldritch knowledge |
| Flux and Taint | Environmental magical hazards and their related effects | Connected to magical production and the environment; dealing with them does not remove Warp |

These connections show that exploration, research and production in Thaumcraft are not three isolated systems. Exploration provides objects and clues, research explains aspects and unlocks their uses, nodes and materials provide actual magical resources, and facilities use those resources for crafting and automation.

title: thaumcraft guide: Thaumic Tinkerer
text:
# Thaumic Tinkerer

  

**Thaumic Tinkerer (TT)** adds customizable enchanting, durability repair, block transport, infused crops, and a wide range of functional devices to Thaumcraft.
Later, KAMI research builds on Ichor to provide Ichorcloth armor, Ichorium tools, teleportation devices, and more.

Its content supports equipment upgrades, material production, and base construction. The Osmotic Enchanter and Thaumic Restorer fit into existing equipment and essentia systems;
infused crops are bred through aspect combinations, while KAMI makes further use of void materials, Osmiridium, and higher wand Vis capacity.

NH rewrites many research prerequisites and recipes, so check current materials in NEI. This page focuses on device mechanics, uses, and NH-specific changes.

## Osmotic Enchanter

The Osmotic Enchanter is a powerful enchanting table added by TT.
It lets you choose the enchantments and levels to apply to equipment, using Vis from a wand.
Different enchantments require different primal aspects, and the costs rise quickly at higher levels.

**Surrounding pillars**

The enchanter requires **6 nearby pillars**. Their bases must be at the same height as the enchanter and within **4 blocks** along both the X and Z axes.
Each pillar consists of **2–12 Obsidian Totem** stacked vertically, topped with Nitor.

The scene shows a layout with two totems per pillar.
Other positions meeting the range and height requirements also work; the pillars do not require a fixed hexagonal layout.

**Items and power supply**

- The item must be **unenchanted** and have the item type and enchantability required by the chosen enchantment.
- The interface only offers registered enchantments that apply to the item and whose research requirements are met. Restrictions such as the incompatibility between Silk Touch and Fortune still apply.
- The wand's caps must have a base Vis consumption modifier of **100% or less**. Iron and copper caps do not qualify; staves are also not accepted.
- Vis is absorbed gradually during processing, so the total requirement can exceed the wand's current reserves. If it runs short, remove the wand, recharge it, and return it to continue supplying Vis.
- The item is locked while the enchanter is working, preventing removal or changes to the selected enchantments. Invalid pillars interrupt the process.

The Osmotic Enchanter is made through infusion, with an ordinary Enchanting Table as the central ingredient and Obsidian Totems, Thaumium Plates, and Spellbinding Cloth around it.
The recipe has an instability of **12**, and the research adds **3 Warp**.

**Spellbinding Cloth**

Combining Spellbinding Cloth with an item in a crafting recipe removes its enchantments, allowing you to redesign the combination.

> [!WARNING]
> Spellbinding Cloth removes the item's existing enchantments. Before using it on equipment with rare enchantments or effects that are difficult to obtain again, check which ones you intend to keep.

## Useful Enchantments

Thaumic Tinkerer's enchantment research appears in its research tab. Complete the corresponding research to select these enchantments in the Osmotic Enchanter.
They affect mining, combat, or movement, so choose them according to the equipment's intended use.

**Mining and harvesting**

- **Tunnel**: Increases mining speed when repeatedly digging in a straight line, making it useful for tunnels.
- **Shatter**: Increases mining speed against blocks with high hardness.
- **Disintegrate**: Provides very high mining speed against ordinary blocks suited to the tool, such as stone, dirt, and netherrack. It reduces effectiveness against other targets and doubles durability consumption.
- **Flaming Touch**: Specializes in fast mining of wooden blocks, reducing effectiveness against other targets and also doubling durability consumption.

**Combat and movement**

- **Vampirism**: Converts part of the damage dealt by an attack into healing for the wielder.
- **Quick Draw**: Speeds up drawing a bow.
- **Ascent Boost**: Applied to leggings to increase jump height.
- **Slow Fall**: Applied to boots to reduce falling speed and fall damage; sneaking temporarily disables the effect.

Other combat enchantments include Dispersed Strikes, Focused Strikes, Final Strike, Valiance, Pounce, and Shockwave. Their research entries describe their effects and applicable equipment.
Mining enchantments with high durability consumption pair well with repair facilities or unbreakable Ichorium tools.

## Durability Repair and Status Protection

**Thaumic Restorer**

The Thaumic Restorer repairs inserted items using Instrumentum essentia. Each point of Instrumentum restores **8 durability**.

Supply essentia through the restorer's connection face, using tubes connected to your Instrumentum stock. Goggles of Revealing show the remaining damage, and the restorer emits a redstone signal while repairing.

Automation can insert damaged items and extract them once repairs are complete, supporting a cycle of equipment collection, repair, and resupply.
It accepts items according to their repairability; **Tinkers' Construct tools cannot be repaired**.

See Alchemy and Essentia for essentia storage and distribution.

**Talisman of Remedium**

When worn and enabled, the Talisman of Remedium absorbs several negative status effects, consuming its durability to remove them. It can also handle some Warp-related effects, at a high durability cost.

**Wand Focus: Mending**

The Wand Focus: Mending consumes wand Vis during continuous use to slowly heal the caster. It is useful for recovering between fights and requires reserves of the relevant Vis.

## Transport, Collection, and Device Interfaces

**Wand Focus: Dislocation**

The Wand Focus: Dislocation picks up a block, stores it, and places it elsewhere. Containers, furnaces, and some mob spawners can also be moved. Vis is charged when picking up the block; placing it back costs no additional Vis.

Blocks with tile entities cost **5 times** as much Vis as ordinary blocks, while mob spawners cost **20 times** as much.
The focus cannot move certain blocks, including aura nodes, some AE blocks, bundled conduits, reinforced essentia jars, and other special devices.

**Transvector Interface and Dislocator**

- A Transvector Interface bound to a target block extends its item, fluid, and other interfaces.
Bind it with a Transvector Binder, within a range of **4 blocks**. It shares the target's corresponding capabilities, providing additional connection points around a device.

- A Transvector Dislocator swaps the block in front of it with the bound location when triggered by redstone, also moving entities at those positions.
Its binding range is **16 blocks**, and its facing can be adjusted with a wand.

**Attractors and automated tool use**

- The Kinetic Attractor affects dropped items, while the Corporeal Attractor affects living creatures. Blue mode attracts and red mode repels;
the range is half the redstone signal strength, up to **7.5 blocks**. The Corporeal Attractor also uses Soul Molds to filter creature types and distinguish adults from babies.

- The Dynamism Tablet performs left-click or right-click actions with the inserted tool or item, either continuously or under redstone control.
Tool type and durability also affect its work when harvesting, placing blocks, or performing other automated actions.

These devices supplement existing logistics and redstone controls. See Magic Automation for more on collection, inventory monitoring, and production support.

## Lighting, Movement, and Portable Devices

**Lighting and darkening**

Hyperenergetic Nitor illuminates the area around its carrier even while stored in the inventory, making it useful in caves and areas without fixed lighting.

Gaseous Illuminae and Gaseous Tenebrae release spreading gases that respectively light up or darken the surrounding area.

The Fume Dissipator dissipates both types of nearby gas, allowing you to change an area that has already been prepared.

**Movement and storage**

- The Wand Focus: Uprising consumes Vis to lift the caster into the air, providing short-distance movement and a way over obstacles.
- The Wand Focus: Ender Rift provides remote access to Ender storage. With EnderStorage integration, it can also be bound to an Ender Chest's color combination.
- When worn and enabled, the Talisman of Withhold collects nearby experience orbs. Glass bottles in the inventory can be used to convert stored experience into Bottles o' Enchanting for storage and transfer.
- The Helmet of Revealing combines Thaumium helmet protection with the observation abilities of Goggles of Revealing, retaining head protection while using those abilities.

## Elemental Fire

Thaumic Tinkerer's six elemental fires are involved in environmental transformation and later Infused Seeds research.

- Ignis Imbued Fire: Converts some ordinary blocks into their Nether counterparts, such as stone into netherrack.
- Aqua Imbued Fire: Transforms terrain toward water, ice, and snow, including some Nether terrain.
- Aer Imbued Fire: Converts some blocks into desert counterparts.
- Terra Imbued Fire: Turns stone, cobblestone, and other blocks into dirt, with additional transformations such as gravel into clay.
- Ordo Imbued Fire: Has no usable block transformation results in the current version, but its research remains a prerequisite for Infused Seeds.
- Perditio Imbued Fire: Removes the magic from other elemental fires, turning them back into ordinary fire.

> [!WARNING]
> NH allows elemental fire to spread and transform blocks by default. Control its area of effect and avoid releasing it near bases, farms, wooden buildings, or important facilities. Ordinary fire left by Perditio Imbued Fire can also continue burning.

## Infused Crops

ThaumicTinkerer:infusedSeeds:0:{mainAspect:{Aspects:{key: carry a main aspect and primal aspect tendencies. Each main aspect has a different loot pool; aspect combinations allow you to breed crops that produce particular materials.

Infused Seeds research requires all six elemental fire research entries. The six primal seeds are made through infusion, using Wheat Seeds as the central ingredient and **4 crystal clusters of the corresponding aspect**.
Each recipe requires **32 Messis, 32 Meto, and 16 essentia of the corresponding primal aspect**, with an instability of **4**. Compound aspect seeds are obtained through further breeding.

Seeds can be planted on ordinary farmland, converting it into Infused Farmland. Growth requires at least **light level 9**. Harvesting mature crops produces seeds and the corresponding loot, and leaves aspect residue in the soil.

A mature crop leaves its main aspect in the farmland below when harvested. Farmland holds up to **20 points** of residue in total; excess residue causes some aspects to be reduced at random.

When a mature crop is harvested, its main aspect may combine with an aspect in the soil, turning the dropped seed into a new compound aspect seed.
For example, Aer + Ignis = Lux. Growing Ignis crops in soil with accumulated Aer residue can yield Lux seeds when harvested. Following further aspect combinations leads to more complex main aspects.

**Primal aspect tendencies**

Tendencies affect growth, yield, and mutation. A crop can have at most **50 tendency points** in total; excess points cause some tendencies to be reduced at random.

| Tendency | Main Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Aqua | Speeds up growth |
| Terra | Increases soil residue left after harvesting a mature crop |
| Ignis | Improves the chance of producing compound aspect seeds |
| Ordo | Increases the number of loot rolls |
| Perditio | Increases seed drops |
| Aer | Speeds up the acquisition of tendencies from adjacent crops |

Compound aspect crops can acquire the corresponding tendency from adjacent primal crops, up to **5 points** per tendency through this method. Adjacent compound crops also transfer tendencies between themselves; higher values require further breeding through this exchange.

**Loot and NEI**

Thaumic Tinkerer provides NEI loot lookup for Infused Seeds, showing the possible outputs and their probabilities for a given aspect crop. These probabilities come from its loot pool, while Ordo tendency also affects the number of loot rolls per harvest.

- Crops of the **four natural elements** produce the corresponding Imbued Grain, which can be used in alchemy to make Aer, Ignis, Aqua, and Terra potions.
- **Ordo and Perditio** crops produce glass and sand, respectively.
- The **Cognitio** loot pool includes paper, books, bookshelves, and Knowledge Fragments.
- The **Alienis** loot pool includes Ender Pearls, Eyes of Ender, and Void Seeds.
- Other compound aspects have their own loot pools. Look up a target item's recipes in NEI to find a suitable main aspect to breed.

For long-term harvesting, preserve the seeds and their tendencies, soil residue, and growing locations, assigning suitable planting areas to breeding and production.

## Unlocking KAMI Research

The main entry point to KAMI is **Ichor** research. Its prerequisites cover the main Thaumcraft categories and relevant Thaumic Tinkerer research. Completing them opens the way to Ichorcloth, Ichorium, and their advanced devices.

Unlocking Ichor research is demanding and often leaves the researcher with 300+ Warp, so prepare suitable Warp protection.

Check the prerequisites of the Ichor recipe in `NEI` to see what remains locked and identify hidden prerequisites. The quest book also highlights easily missed research such as the Thaumium Crowbar and Cursed Spirit's Blade.

## Ichor, Ichorcloth, and Ichorium

**Dimensional shards**

Nether Shard and Ender Shard are important ingredients for Ichor.

- Zombie Pigmen killed by a player in the **Nether** have a **1/16** chance to drop a Nether Shard.
- Endermen killed by a player in the **End** have a **1/32** chance to drop an Ender Shard.
- NH also provides infusion recipes for dimensional shards, using various Forbidden Magic shards, infused shards, and the corresponding central ingredients. Beekeeping offers another route for a continuous supply.

The drops require the corresponding dimension and a player kill; account for these conditions when designing a mob supply.
An `EEC` processing the corresponding mobs in their required dimension also produces shards.

**Ichor**

Ichor is made by infusing a Nether Star.

The recipe uses one Nether Star as the central ingredient, surrounded by a Flawless Diamond, Nether Shard, Eye of Ender, and Ender Shard, producing **2 Ichor**.
Its essentia requirements are **32 Humanus, 32 Lux, 64 Spiritus, 16 Alienis, and 16 Ordo**, with an instability of **10**. Ichor research itself adds **5 Warp**.

**Ichorcloth and Ichorium**

- Ichorcloth combines Ichor, Enchanted Fabric, Void Metal Foil, Osmiridium Foil, and Flawless Diamonds. It is a main material for Ichorcloth Robes and their awakened upgrades.
- **Ichorium** combines Ichor, void metal, Osmiridium, and Flawless Diamonds. GT's Ichorium ingots and material forms are used to make plates, screws, rings, and various tool components.

Both arcane crafting recipes require **125 Vis of each of the six primal aspects**. Wand capacity and Vis discounts affect which recipes you can actually craft. See [Wands, Vis and Nodes for the relevant equipment and discount sources.

**Ichorium wand components**

The Ichorium Cap provides a **30%** Vis discount for all primal aspects. The Ichor Woven Silverwood Wand Core gives a wand a capacity of **1000 Vis per primal aspect**.

This path supports large arcane recipes and sustained focus use. The caps, core, and finished wand each require their corresponding research and crafting.

## Ichorcloth Armor and Awakening

Ordinary Ichorcloth armor consists of the Ichorcloth Cowl, Ichorcloth Robe, Ichorcloth Leggings, and Ichorcloth Boots.
These pieces do not lose durability. Infusion can awaken them to grant additional movement, protection, and observation abilities.

- Cowl of the Abyssal Depths: Provides revealing abilities, underwater breathing, clear underwater vision, and continued health regeneration while hungry.
- Robes of the Stratosphere: Provides sustained flight, fall protection, and protection against ordinary projectiles.
- Leggings of the Burning Mantle: Provides fire protection and converts incoming fire damage into healing.
- Boots of the Horizontal Shield: Improves movement, jumping, and reach across gaps, allows automatic stepping up one-block rises, and provides Haste and fall protection.

Awakened armor effects are controlled by the **Toggle Awakened Armor** keybinding, which defaults to `U`.
NH disables the awakened leggings' automatic light placement by default, while retaining the awakened boots' ability to turn dirt beneath the wearer into grass.

Awakening recipes use advanced gems, Ichorium components, and other magical devices, with high instability.
Once material production is established, a stable Infusion Altar and sufficient essentia reserves are needed. See Infusion Crafting for altar supply and stability.

## Ichorium Tools and the Bedrock Dimension

The Ichorium Pickaxe, Ichorium Shovel, Ichorium Axe, and Ichorium Sword do not lose durability and can be awakened further.

Sneak-right-click to switch an awakened tool's working mode:

- Awakened Ichorium Pickaxe: Single-block, **5×5 area**, and **10-block line** mining, with the ability to break bedrock.
- Awakened Ichorium Shovel: Single-block, **5×5 area**, and vertical column mining of the same block type.
- Awakened Ichorium Axe: Single-block, **5×5 area**, and whole-tree chopping.
- Awakened Ichorium Sword: Single-target attacks, area attacks against nearby creatures of the same type, and a mode that grants Soul Hearts.

> [!WARNING]
> Area and line mining affect several blocks at once. Before using awakened tools near your base or devices, check the current mode and direction to avoid breaking blocks you intend to keep.

**Bedrock Dimension**

The Awakened Ichorium Pickaxe's bedrock-breaking ability also provides access to the **Bedrock Dimension**. Mining bedrock at **Y=0–4** in the Overworld while sneaking creates an entrance. Inside, you can continue mining bedrock and the vertical ore veins within it.

This dimension provides a special mining space. GTNH adjusts its ore content; conventional miners first need room to work, so plan a suitable means of clearing bedrock.

The quest book warns that leaving may place you on the nearby surface or inside blocks. Prepare return methods, mining tools, and location records before entering to reduce problems caused by changing entry and exit points.

## KAMI Building and Teleportation Devices

**Storing and placing large quantities of blocks**

- Once bound to a block type, the Black Hole Ring absorbs matching blocks from the inventory beyond one stack, leaving a stack available for use. It stores over 2 billion blocks of one type and can deposit them into containers or place them in the world.
- The Worldshaper's Looking Glass previews and places blocks in a selected area. Materials can come from the inventory or Black Hole Rings holding the required block.
- Protoclay switches between the holder's Awakened Ichorium tools to use a suitable tool for the current target.
- The Bottomless Pouch provides a large portable inventory while retaining the functions of a Focus Pouch. NH prevents its use in Witchery's dream dimension.

**Celestial Gateways and Recall**

A Celestial Gateway uses a Celestial Pearl to record another gateway's position. Each gateway holds **10 destinations**, connecting bases, mining sites, and other frequently used locations.

Bind a Celestial Pearl to a destination gateway and insert it into the departure gateway to create a one-way connection. A return route requires a pearl configured at each end. The gateway's interface can also restrict connections from other gateways.

The Wand Focus: Celestial Recall uses a bound Celestial Pearl in the hotbar and consumes Vis to teleport the caster to its destination, extending a fixed teleportation network into a portable way home.

title: thaumcraft guide: Wands, Vis and Nodes
text:
# Wands, Vis and Nodes

  

**Thaumcraft:WandCasting:0:{rod: Wands** store and use Vis in Thaumcraft, enabling arcane crafting, activating magical facilities, and using wand foci.As research progresses, you need to improve wand capacity, Vis discounts, and your energy supply to support new recipes and facilities.

In GTNH, wand crafting also requires **Twilight Forest trophies and technological materials**.
More advanced wands offer greater capacity, so upgrading involves both obtaining new materials and reducing the Vis needed to craft the next wand.

This page covers wand properties and crafting requirements, along with energy sources such as nodes, aspect orbs, and Centi-Vis. For aspects and research points, see Thaumcraft Basics.

## Wand Components and Uses

Wands consist of a **rod or staff core** and **caps**. The rod mainly determines Vis capacity, while the caps mainly determine the cost modifier. Some addon components also provide automatic recharging or energy conversion.

Capacity is counted separately for each of the six primal aspects. A capacity of "50 Vis" means that up to 50 Vis of each primal aspect can be stored.

| Type | Arcane Crafting | Wand Foci | Main Features |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Wand | Yes | Yes | Suitable for crafting, interacting with facilities, and using foci |
| Sceptre | Yes | No | With the same ordinary rod, capacity increases by 50%, with an additional 10 percentage point reduction in Vis cost |
| Staff | No | Yes | Uses a staff core, usually with greater capacity, for foci and facility interactions |

A sceptre's extra capacity and discount make it suitable for keeping in an Arcane Worktable.
Staves offer greater capacity but cannot be used for arcane crafting.

Staff capacity depends on the specific core. For example, a Greatwood Staff Core holds 125 Vis, a Silverwood Staff Core holds 250 Vis, and the six elemental staff cores hold 175 Vis.

**Wand foci** provide active abilities such as mining, combat, and movement; a staff core is the component that determines the staff's capacity.
## Wand Crafting Requirements

In GTNH, crafting a wand also requires screws and Twilight Forest boss trophies, with the materials determined by the component's recipe tier.

| Recipe Tier | Screw Material | Boss Trophy | Typical Acquisition Stage |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 (LV) | Aluminium | Naga Scale | LV |
| 1 (MV) | Stainless Steel | Lich Bone | MV |
| 2 (HV) | Energetic Alloy | Lich Bone | MV |
| 3 (EV) | Vibrant Alloy | Fiery Blood | HV |
| 4 (IV) | Tungstensteel | Fiery Tears | EV |
| 5 (LuV) | Enderium (TE) | Carminite | EV |
| 6 (ZPM) | Oriharukon | Carminite | EV |
| 7 (UV) | Osmiridium | Snow Queen Blood | IV |

The standard recipes for ordinary Wooden, Greatwood, the six elemental, and Silverwood rods use tier 0, 1, 2, and 3 materials respectively. These tiers group wand recipes; some materials from higher tiers can be obtained earlier, without reaching the voltage stage of the same name.

The assembly Vis cost of an ordinary wand is **the rod's base cost + the rod's cap cost increment × the cap's assembly coefficient**, with the same amount required for each primal aspect. Sceptres additionally apply the rod's sceptre multiplier.
For example, Greatwood uses 20 + 5 × the cap coefficient. Gold caps have a coefficient of 2, so assembling a wand requires 30 Vis of each aspect, while the corresponding sceptre requires 60 Vis of each. Check NEI for material quantities and addon rod parameters.

## Vis Discounts and Advanced Wands

Vis discounts are important for crafting advanced wands.

- Caps | Determine the wand's base cost modifier; some caps only provide discounts for particular aspects
- Equipment and baubles | Provide Vis discounts for the relevant aspects when worn in the appropriate slots
- Sceptres | Reduce costs by another 10 percentage points in addition to cap and equipment effects

Among basic equipment, Goggles of Revealing provide a 5% discount, Thaumaturge's Robe and Thaumaturge's Leggings each provide 2%, and Thaumaturge's Boots provide 1%. Together, the four pieces provide 10%.

Bewitched Robe and Bewitched Leggings provide 5% and 4% respectively, further reducing crafting costs.

In general, the actual cost is **recipe requirement × (cap cost modifier − equipment discount − sceptre discount)**, with a minimum modifier of 0.1. Equipment and sceptre effects subtract percentage points.

A practical example is a Gold Capped Greatwood Sceptre, whose base assembly cost is 60 Vis of each primal aspect.
A Gold Capped Greatwood Wand holds 50 Vis. Even with the basic four-piece set's 10% discount, crafting the sceptre requires 54 Vis, exceeding that capacity.
A cheaper combination using the same rod, or additional discounts, can overcome this requirement.

Thaumic Machina's **Vis Channels** augmentation first multiplies the cap cost modifier by 0.9, before applying equipment and sceptre discounts.
For example, Thaumium caps' 90% modifier becomes 81%, or 61% with the basic four-piece set and a sceptre.

## Wand Caps

| Registry Name | Cap | Assembly Coefficient | Base Vis Cost | Features |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| terrasteel | Terrasteel Cap | 1 | 180% | — |
| iron | Iron Cap | 0 | 110% | Node Preserver does not apply |
| copper | Copper Cap | 1 | 110% | Order and Entropy cost 100% |
| gold | Gold Cap | 2 | 100% | — |
| silver | Charged Silver Cap | 3 | 100% | Air, Earth, Fire, and Water cost 95% |
| SOJOURNER | Sojourner's Cap | 5 | 95% | Passively draws Vis from nearby nodes while held |
| MECHANIST | Mechanist's Cap | 5 | 95% | Increases the rate of drawing Vis from nodes |
| cloth | Enchanted Cloth Cap | 3 | 95% | — |
| thaumium | Charged Thaumium Cap | 5 | 90% | — |
| manasteel | Manasteel Cap | 6 | 85% | Reduces Mana conversion costs when paired with Livingwood or Dreamwood rods |
| vinteum | Vinteum Cap | 5 | 90% | — |
| alchemical | Alchemical Cap | 6 | 90% | Water costs 80%; reduces LP conversion costs with Blood or Blood Infused Wooden rods; wand attacks inflict Weakness |
| shadowcloth | Shadow-Imbued Cloth Cap | 5 | 85% | — |
| thauminite | Thauminite Cap | 6 | 85% | — |
| blood_iron | Blood Infused Iron Cap | 6 | 85% | Water costs 80%; further reduces LP conversion costs with Blood Infused Wooden rods |
| void | Charged Void metal Cap | 7 | 80% | — |
| elementium | Elementium Cap | 7 | 70% | Reduces Mana conversion costs when paired with Livingwood or Dreamwood rods |
| crimsoncloth | Crimson-Stained Cloth Cap | 6 | 80% | — |
| shadowmetal | Shadowmetal Cap | 8 | 70% | — |
| ICHOR | Ichorium Cap | 8 | 70% | — |

Version 2.9 buffed some Forbidden Magic wand components. See "Wand Component Buffs" under "New in 2.9" for the related changes.

### Component Replacement and Wand Augmentation

Salis Arcana adds research for **replacing caps and rods or staff cores**, with the corresponding recipes available in NEI. Replacement consumes the new component and destroys the old one, with the same Vis requirement as directly assembling the target wand.
Permanent augmentations are retained, and replacing sceptre components also saves the Primal Charm required to craft a new sceptre. Replacement cannot change a wand, sceptre, or staff into another type.
Wand augmentations are installed through infusion. Each augmentation can be installed once per wand, and different augmentations can coexist.

- Charge Buffer: increases capacity by 25%
- Vis Channels: multiplies the caps' Vis cost by 0.9, before equipment and sceptre discounts
- Contact Discharge: melee attacks with the wand consume Vis to deal magical damage that bypasses ordinary armor

## Sources of Vis

| Source or Facility | What It Provides | Characteristics |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Drawing directly from ordinary aura nodes | Primal aspect Vis stored in the node | Easy to use, but limited by the node's aspects, reserves, and regeneration rate |
| Aspect orbs | Vis of the corresponding primal aspect | A wand in the hotbar can absorb nearby orbs if it has room for that aspect |
| Primal Shrooms | Aspect orbs released when mature plants are harvested | A renewable supplementary source with random aspect output |
| Special rods or staff cores | Automatic recharging or conversion specified by the component | May only replenish one aspect or recharge to a low reserve level |
| Wand Recharge Pedestal | Draws Vis from nearby nodes to recharge a wand | Suitable for base charging; using compound aspects requires an additional device |
| Energized nodes and Centi-Vis networks | Continuous Centi-Vis output | Powers fixed devices and can recharge wands through appropriate charging facilities |
| Essentia Dynamo | Converts essentia into Centi-Vis | Requires a supply network, charging facilities, and a continuous supply of the relevant materials |

Hungry nodes, Ethereal Shards, and Empowering bees offer ways to cultivate or customize nodes for a lasting energy supply.

## Vishrooms, Primal Shrooms, and Aspect Orbs

Vishroom is Thaumcraft's Vishroom and an ingredient for Primal Shroom. **Primal Shrooms are the plants that release Vis orbs when harvested at maturity.**

The Primal Shroom alchemy recipe uses a Vishroom as its catalyst, along with aspectrecipeindex:aspect:1:{Aspect: Entropy and aspectrecipeindex:aspect:1:{Aspect: Crop aspects.
Check NEI and the corresponding research for quantities. Breaking a mature plant with left-click drops the plant itself and 8–20 orbs of random primal aspects, each providing 1 Vis. The plant can then be replanted.

Primal Shrooms take time to grow, need a full supporting block below, and require a light level of at least 9 above.
They cannot be harvested with right-click, and breaking them before maturity does not provide the same Vis yield. Growing and harvesting them provides a repeatable source of Vis.

Creatures can also leave aspect orbs when they die, which are absorbed by a wand in the hotbar with room for the corresponding aspect.

Ordinary elemental rods generally recharge only one aspect, and only to a small fraction of their capacity.
Botania integration rods can convert Mana into Vis, provided their charging requirements are met and Mana is available.

## Observing Nodes and Reading Their Reserves

**Aura nodes** are concentrations of magical energy in the world. They can be scanned and used as a source of Vis for wands. Observing through a Thaumometer or wearing Goggles of Revealing makes nodes easier to identify.

When examining a node, consider four kinds of information:

| Information | What It Determines |
| --- | --- |
| Aspect composition | Which primal aspects it can supply directly, and whether it contains compound aspects for other uses |
| Current reserves | How much Vis is available to draw immediately |
| Base capacity | The amount its normal regeneration can restore, which also affects energized node output |
| Type and quality | Special behavior, regeneration speed, and performance after conversion |

NH's node records help manage previously scanned nodes and can be opened with the I key by default.

### Node Types

Nodes have six main types. Type describes special behavior rather than a ranking; nodes of the same type can have different qualities and aspect compositions.

  

| Type | Core Appearance | Properties and Considerations |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Normal | White, with a stable core | The most common ordinary node, with no additional type effects |
| Sinister | Dark purple | Often associated with obsidian totems and Eldritch structures; changes nearby biomes and may spawn dangerous creatures |
| Pure | White vortex | Often found in Silverwood trees; can turn nearby biomes into Magical Forest, helping contain Taint |
| Tainted | Purple haze | Associated with Tainted Land; spreads Taint and its related hazards |
| Unstable | White, with a constantly pulsing core | Releases aspect orbs and loses Vis, making it unsuitable as a stable long-term energy source |
| Hungry | White ring | Draws in and devours nearby entities and items, and destroys blocks; its capacity can be cultivated by feeding it items with aspects |

> [!WARNING]
> Hungry nodes devour items, harm players, and affect nearby blocks. Valuable items, drops, and production facilities can be lost. Cultivate and modify them in a separate, protected area.

## Node Quality and Natural Regeneration

Node quality can be Normal, Bright, Pale, or Fading. Quality describes regeneration and is independent of type; a Pure node can also be Bright.

  

| Quality | Natural Regeneration | Appearance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Normal | A regeneration event roughly every 30 seconds | No additional quality name |
| Bright | A regeneration event roughly every 20 seconds | More vivid than a Normal node |
| Pale | A regeneration event roughly every 45 seconds | Dimmer |
| Fading | Does not naturally regenerate Vis | Very dim and constantly flickering |

### Drawing from Nodes and Node Preserver

Wands can directly draw primal aspects from nodes, but cannot store compound aspects directly. A node containing only compound aspects requires another method of use.

**Advanced Node Tapping** and **Master Node Tapping** increase the drawing rate to twice and three times the normal rate respectively.
These improve transfer speed, without increasing the node's natural regeneration rate or aspect capacity.

**Node Preserver** leaves at least 1 point of each aspect during normal drawing, reducing the risk of damage from draining the node.
There are exceptions: sneaking bypasses protection, and low-end wands with ordinary Wooden rods or Iron caps cannot rely on it.

> [!WARNING]
> Draining an aspect to zero can remove that aspect or damage the node's quality. Exhausting every aspect can also make the node disappear.

## Moving, Stabilizing, and Cultivating Nodes

**Nodes in jars** provide a way to move nodes. Jarring risks damage, and jarred nodes do not naturally regenerate Vis, so they cannot serve as portable batteries to draw from at any time.
