Before jarring, consider the node's current condition and the research explaining how to seal and release it. Once moved to your base, nearby node interactions and hazardous node types also need attention.

- Node Stabilizer: prevents the stabilized node and other nodes from drawing Vis from each other, halves natural regeneration, and gradually repairs certain adverse conditions
- Advanced Node Stabilizer: protects the node from being drained while allowing it to draw Vis from less stable neighbors; greatly suppresses natural regeneration and is better suited to planned node cultivation

Node Stabilizers sit below the node. **Applying redstone to a stabilizer disables it**, unlike the Node Transducer above the node, which requires redstone to activate.

Larger nodes can draw Vis from smaller neighbors, while Hungry nodes can grow by absorbing the aspects of consumed items.
Cultivation requires time and suitable conditions; placing any two nodes close together will not necessarily merge them. Node quality, stabilizers, and the aspects in items affect whether a method suits the intended use.

## Node Manipulators and Quality Repair

Node Manipulator and **Node Manipulator Foci** provide ways to actively modify nodes.
Different foci have different effects, described by their respective research.

| Manipulator Focus | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Node Manipulator Focus: Stability | Repairs Fading and Pale quality, and can also address the Unstable type |
| Node Manipulator Focus: Brightness | Raises Normal quality to Bright |
| Node Manipulator Focus: Speed | Replenishes missing Vis and improves recharging |
| Node Manipulator Focus: Efficiency | Has a chance to restore some Vis after consumption, without increasing capacity |

The manipulator sits directly above the node and operates through its installed focus. In the current implementation, the stabilizing focus takes about 5 minutes to repair Fading quality to Pale, and about 10 minutes to repair Pale to Normal.
The brightening focus takes about 20 minutes to turn Normal quality into Bright. These times assume the node remains loaded and the game runs at normal speed.

Improving quality increases regeneration and can improve subsequent energized node output, but does not add aspect types or increase base capacity.

The Node Manipulator and Node Transducer both occupy the position above the node, so quality adjustment and later conversion are separate stages.

### Changing Base Aspects and Random Node Modification

To change a node's base aspects, you can also use Node Manipulator. Unlike the previous manipulator, it **randomly changes aspect composition, base amounts, quality, or type**.

| Possible Modification | Changes |
| --- | --- |
| Split compound aspects | Transfers a compound aspect's base amount to its component aspects |
| Combine aspects | Changes the base composition to form compound aspects |
| Add aspects | Adds missing primal aspects |
| Change quality | Quality may improve or deteriorate |
| Change type | Can produce another type, including the additional Growing type |

Each modification requires **at least 70 Vis of each primal aspect to be supplied cumulatively** to the manipulator, paid by the wand or staff placed inside.

Changing base aspects can help nodes with unsuitable compositions, but random modifications can also have negative results.
To obtain an energy source with all six aspects, compare the materials, time, and risks of artificial node customization, node bees, and quality adjustment.

> [!WARNING]
> Random modifications by the Node Manipulator can lower quality or change the node's type. Assess these risks before using it on a node.

### Ethereal Shards and Artificial Nodes

Ethereal Shard is an artificial Vis container.
Unlike natural nodes, **its aspect types and capacities can be set using materials, but it does not regenerate Vis on its own** and requires an external Centi-Vis supply.

Ethereal Essence increases its capacity. Each Ethereal Essence adds 4 points to the capacity of its aspect, without filling the added capacity.

Compound aspects can also be added to the shard. Charging them requires the supply network to provide their component primal aspects; an incomplete supply cannot fully charge the compound aspect.

**Ethereal Shards can also be used to customize ordinary nodes.** Once charged with Centi-Vis, a shard can be sealed into a jarred node and released as an ordinary aura node. This turns a composition defined by materials into a node that can regenerate naturally or undergo further modification.

This method needs an existing Centi-Vis source for the initial charge, such as an energized node or Essentia Dynamo.
An Essentia Dynamo consumes essentia to produce Centi-Vis, while a dynamo that consumes wand Vis transfers energy.

### Empowering Bees and Node Cultivation

Empowering bees bring beekeeping into magical energy production. Effects operate within the hive's effective working area, influenced by territory genes and hive multipliers; check the effect gene the bee has actually inherited.

- Empowering: randomly increases an aspect's base capacity and current reserves, and may add new aspects
- Rejuvenating: refills existing Vis without increasing capacity through this effect
- Nexus: improves quality progressively from Fading to Bright, and can also address the Unstable type

Empowering bees select aspects randomly, while Nexus bees' quality improvements can complement capacity growth to improve later energy output.
Bee effects must reach the target node, and cultivation requires continued operation.
Jarred nodes can be cultivated this way, but artificial containers such as Ethereal Shards are excluded. A customized node must first be converted through jarring before node bees can affect it.

Industrial Apiary acceleration can greatly change cultivation speed. See the Forestry content for beekeeping mechanics, genetics, and acceleration requirements; this page focuses on their effects on nodes.

### Energized Nodes and Centi-Vis

**Energized nodes** change node use from storing Vis for gradual drawing to continuously producing Centi-Vis (CV).
1 CV equals 0.01 Vis, and the node's displayed output indicates how much CV it supplies per game tick.

Node Transducer performs the conversion. A stabilizer below the node must operate throughout the process, while the transducer above the node is activated by redstone. Both facilities must remain in their required operating states after conversion.

**Conversion uses the node's base aspect amounts.** Compound aspects can also contribute to primal aspect output, so a node containing compound aspects is not necessarily worse than one containing only primal aspects.

Output does not increase in direct proportion to the node's reserves. Aspects are first broken down into primal aspects. For each primal aspect, the largest contribution from different sources is used rather than adding them together. The quality multiplier is then applied and the result rounded down, followed by taking the square root and rounding down again.

For example, a Normal-quality node contains 100 Fire and 100 Energy. Energy breaks down into Fire and Order, so the effective Fire amount remains 100 rather than 200, yielding 10 CV/t each of Fire and Order.
Adding all the displayed aspect amounts together therefore does not give the correct output.

The quality multipliers for Bright, Normal, Pale, and Fading are 1.2, 1, 0.8, and 0.5 respectively, applied before taking the square root. Larger nodes generally provide more Centi-Vis.

**Energized nodes cannot be drawn from directly with a wand and do not regenerate like ordinary nodes.** They supply energy through Vis Relays and the relevant devices. Output remains limited separately for each of the six aspects, so high total output cannot compensate for a missing aspect.

> [!WARNING]
> Disabling or breaking the stabilizer below an energized node causes an explosion and Flux pollution. To dismantle the setup, first remove the **transducer's** redstone signal while keeping the stabilizer active. Wait until the node has completely returned to its ordinary form before removing the facilities. The restored node is drained and still risks damage, so avoid repeated switching.

### Centi-Vis Networks and Automatic Wand Charging

Vis Relay transmits Centi-Vis. Connections between nodes and relays require a distance of no more than 8 blocks and a clear line of sight. Relays can connect to other relays to extend the supply to devices around the base.

The network uses a tree structure: each relay has one upstream source and can supply multiple downstream devices. Distance, connections, and available output for each aspect determine whether a device receives energy.

| Charging Facility | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Wand Recharge Pedestal | Automatically charges a placed wand using nearby ordinary nodes; GTNH also enables charging from the Centi-Vis network |
| Compound Recharge Focus | Allows the pedestal to use compound aspects from ordinary nodes, with conversion losses |
| Vis Charge Relay | Sits above an Arcane Worktable and uses Centi-Vis to recharge the wand inside |

Wand Recharge Pedestals and worktable Charging Relays make node energy available for everyday crafting at the base.
For sustained use, consider node output, network connections, wand capacity, and crafting costs together.

## Common Problems

| Symptom | What to Check |
| --- | --- |
| Caps and rod are ready, but the wand cannot be crafted | Check research, Twilight Forest trophies, screw materials, and the actual Vis cost |
| The wand is full but cannot craft an advanced wand | Compare each aspect's actual requirement with capacity; check cap, equipment, and sceptre discounts |
| Vis costs remain higher than expected despite discount equipment | Iron caps impose a cost penalty, and different caps can use different modifiers for different aspects |
| A staff has high capacity but cannot be used in the worktable | Staves do not support arcane crafting; use a wand or sceptre |
| A node has Vis, but the wand cannot draw it | Check for compound aspects, a jarred node, or an already energized node |
| A node regenerates very slowly | Check quality, stabilizer effects, and nearby nodes; Fading quality does not regenerate naturally |
| A node is drained despite Node Preserver research | Check for sneaking or low-quality components such as ordinary Wooden rods or Iron caps |
| Planted Vishrooms do not produce Vis orbs | Vishrooms are an ingredient; harvest mature Primal Shrooms and let a wand with available capacity absorb the orbs |
| An Ethereal Shard has capacity, but the wand cannot draw Vis | Capacity is not the current reserve; provide the complete Centi-Vis supply first |
| An artificial node is smaller than expected after jarring | Jarring uses the amounts currently charged; check actual reserves before sealing |
| A node cultivated by Empowering bees has unbalanced aspects | The effect increases aspects randomly; high total capacity does not ensure all six required aspects are present |
| The original supply method stops working after node conversion | Energized nodes use Centi-Vis networks and cannot be drawn from directly with a wand |
| Centi-Vis devices work intermittently | Check network connections, loaded chunks, aspect output, and competing consumption from other devices |

title: thaumcraft guide: Warp and Eldritch Knowledge
text:
# Warp and Eldritch Knowledge

  

Eldritch knowledge explores the world's deepest secrets, but often leads its students astray.
Delving into forbidden research gradually builds up Warp.
The whispers, hallucinations, and physical changes it brings can also lead to discoveries in Eldritch Studies.

Eldritch Studies covers void metal, primal energy, and exploration of the Outer Lands, connecting to the Advanced Alchemical Furnace, the Staff Core of the Primal, and later KAMI research.
GTNH's **Warp Theory** expands Warp events and provides ways to deal with permanent Warp.

## Sources and Types of Warp

Research marked with purple forbidden knowledge warnings in the Thaumonomicon is a major source of Warp.
Crafting certain items, eating some foods, and using magical tools can also add Warp; look for the relevant markings in research entries and item tooltips.

| Type | Properties | Treatment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Temporary Warp** | Gradually fades during Warp checks | Wait, or remove it with items such as Sanitizing Soap |
| **Sticky Warp** | Does not fade naturally; also called normal Warp | Sanitizing Soap has a chance to reduce it; cleansing items from addons can also remove it |
| **Permanent Warp** | Ordinary Sanitizing Soap cannot remove it | In NH, items such as Pure Tears and Purification Talismans can remove it |

Equipment with the **Warping** property also adds Warp to event calculations.
This contribution comes from items currently worn or held and disappears when they are unequipped; cleansing items do not remove the property from the equipment itself.

**Checking your Warp**

GTNH's IGI overlay can display Warp directly. You can also check it with the following items:

- Arcane Litmus Paper: Shows the exact amounts of permanent, sticky, and temporary Warp in chat when used. Color changes, burning, and other reactions also indicate the danger level.
- Sanity Checker: Displays a Warp bar while held. Dark purple represents permanent Warp, light purple represents sticky Warp, and pink represents temporary Warp. The bar is full at a combined total of 100; use litmus paper to check higher values.

## Warp Events and the Timer

Thaumcraft's own Warp events include Unnatural Hunger, Sun Scorned, blurred vision, increased Vis costs, and Eldritch Guardians appearing in dense fog. Some whispers also grant research points or new discoveries.

- **Vis drained from your wand**, affecting subsequent crafting and combat.
- **Inventory items swapped or shuffled**, along with random teleportation and unusual movement.
- **Poison, Wither, Blindness**, and other effects, or the appearance of Firebats and hostile creatures.
- Events that cause lasting damage, such as **countdown explosions, nearby block decay, and spawning a Wither**.

Events are triggered by random checks. The available events also depend on Warp strength, the timer, and configuration.
The table below lists some event thresholds in NH's default configuration. The **effective strength** used to select an event depends on current Warp and the timer, and equipment such as faceplates can reduce it.

| Effective Strength Threshold | Additional Risk |
| --- | --- |
| 50 | Draining Vis from your wand |
| 125 | Swapping inventory items |
| 130 | Random teleportation |
| 150 | Shuffling inventory items |
| 160 | Countdown explosion |
| 180 | Nearby block decay |
| 200 | Spawning a Wither |

Block decay affects blocks, plants, and leaves that the event can transform; countdown explosions and Withers can cause further damage to nearby facilities.
Where you stay while accumulating Warp also determines how much these events can damage.

**Event decay in 2.9**

After you stop gaining new Warp, events gradually weaken; ordinary random events stop once the timer runs out.
**Gaining Warp again reactivates the timer.** Forbidden research, related crafting, and other sources can all end this quiet period.
Equipment with the Warping property affects event strength but **does not reset the timer**. Existing sticky and permanent Warp remains after events stop.

> [!WARNING]
> High Warp events can cause explosions, damage terrain, or spawn a Wither near the player. Stay away from important machines, storage, and other players' facilities when gaining large amounts of Warp, waiting for Eldritch discoveries, or using cleansing items with backlash.

## Warp Ward and Symptom Relief

Warp Ward prevents ordinary Warp events for its duration. Your existing Warp remains, making it useful for suppressing events while crafting, exploring, or going about daily activities.

**Purifying Bath Salts and the Arcane Spa**

Throwing Purifying Bath Salts into water creates Purifying Fluid. Bathing in it grants Warp Ward; higher permanent Warp shortens the protection.

An Arcane Spa uses water and Purifying Bath Salts to replenish Purifying Fluid in the area above it, providing a convenient way to renew protection at your base.

Botania's Botania:brewFlask:0:{brewKey: also provides Warp Ward. Each dose from a regular flask grants 10 minutes of protection.

An equipped Portable Shower reapplies Warp Ward when it expires, making it useful when regularly wearing equipment with the Warping property.

Rosehip Syrup reduces the level of effects such as blurred vision, Unnatural Hunger, and Vis Exhaustion, removing them when they are already at the lowest level. It also treats some ordinary negative potion effects.

## Reducing and Removing Warp

**Sanitizing Soap**

Finishing the use animation of Sanitizing Soap removes all temporary Warp and has a chance to reduce sticky Warp by 1.

- The base chance is **33%**.
- Warp Ward adds **25 percentage points**.
- Standing in Purifying Fluid adds another **25 percentage points**, for **83%** when both conditions are met.

Keep using the soap until the animation finishes. Using it in Purifying Fluid saves materials when removing large amounts of sticky Warp.

**Thaumic Insurgence soaps**

Thaumic Insurgence provides additional cleansing options:

- Trosma Sláintíochta Soap (α soap): Also removes temporary Warp and has a chance to reduce sticky Warp by 1, with a higher base chance of 50%. Warp Ward and Purifying Fluid raise this to 100%.

- Alastor's Soap: On success, converts **1 permanent Warp into 2 sticky Warp**, which can then be removed with ordinary or α soap. The base chance is 10%, with Warp Ward and Purifying Fluid each adding 15 percentage points. Failure adds 2 temporary Warp.

**Impure Tear**

Impure Tear removes 5 Warp when your combined permanent, sticky, and temporary Warp is **at least 50**.
It removes temporary Warp first, then sticky Warp, then permanent Warp. It can lower high Warp, but cannot continue cleansing once the total falls below the threshold. Its research requires Eldritch Epiphany, Arcane Litmus Paper, and other prerequisites.

**Pure Tear**

Pure Tear removes all accumulated temporary, sticky, and permanent Warp at once.
Its powerful effect places its research behind Eldritch Revelation, Ichor, and other prerequisites, with demanding material requirements.

The **Purge Your Warp** quest offers another way to obtain a Pure Tear. Check its required submissions and rewards even if you have not completed the corresponding research.

> [!WARNING]
> A Pure Tear queues a series of backlash events based on your Warp before cleansing. **Warp Ward cannot prevent this backlash.** After using it, stay away from your base until the concentrated events have finished.

**Purification Talisman**

An equipped Purification Talisman periodically attempts to reduce Warp, gradually removing permanent Warp as well. It is suitable for ongoing cleansing.

The cleansing process still queues ordinary Warp events. Warp Ward delays these events, which may resume after the protection ends; choose a suitable place to stay while cleansing.

## Discovering Eldritch Research

The two Eldritch discoveries come from random checks during Thaumcraft Warp events. They use the **sum of the player's permanent and sticky Warp**:

- **Eldritch Epiphany**: Can unlock when the total is **greater than 25**, revealing the Eldritch tab in the Thaumonomicon and opening research paths such as void metal and the Sanity Checker.
- **Eldritch Revelation**: Can unlock when the total is **greater than 50**. It is a prerequisite for Opening the Eye and some advanced Eldritch research.

Temporary Warp and equipment Warp do not count toward these thresholds. Reaching the required amount still leaves you waiting for a random check, so the time required varies.

**Warp Ward prevents this check.** If you regularly wear a Portable Shower or maintain another source of protection, remove it and wait in an area prepared for Warp events.
You can reduce your Warp after receiving the discoveries; unlocked research remains available.

## Crimson Cult and Opening the Eye

Ordinary Eldritch Obelisk

Crimson Cult Obelisk

While exploring, you may discover two kinds of Eldritch Obelisks. Crimson Clerics and Crimson Knights can be found near Crimson Cult obelisks, and defeating them can yield Crimson Rites.

Scanning the relevant enemies helps reveal research clues. Hold the book and right-click to read it, unlocking **Crimson Cult**.
Crimson Knights fight in melee, while Crimson Clerics use ranged magic.

(Crimson Clerics do not attack unprovoked. Leaving some clerics alive allows Crimson Knights to keep spawning, greatly increasing your opportunities to obtain Crimson Rites.)

Eldritch Guardians may also appear around the ritual area. These sites are useful sources of Crimson Rites, Eldritch Eyes, and related scans.

After completing **Crimson Cult** and **Eldritch Revelation**, you can research **Opening the Eye** to gain access to the Outer Lands.

The ritual requires an intact naturally generated Eldritch Obelisk of either kind, with its Eldritch Altar at the base and Sinister Node above preserved.
Insert **4 Eldritch Eye** into the altar, then right-click it with a wand to open an Eldritch Portal.
The ritual has a base requirement of **100 Vis of each of the six primal aspects**. **Arcane crafting Vis discounts apply.**

Eldritch Eyes can drop from Eldritch Guardians or be made through infusion after completing Opening the Eye research.
The node above the altar participates in opening the portal; bottling or converting it affects the ritual.

Gadomancy provides the **Gate of the Voidwalkers**, an artificial entrance built using a Node Manipulator and a Redirection Focus.
It also requires Eldritch Eyes and wand Vis. The corresponding research shows its structure.

> [!WARNING]
> The Gate of the Voidwalkers allows only one entity to pass through, after which the entrance disappears. Prepare another means of returning, or be ready to complete the Outer Lands challenge before leaving.

## Exploring the Outer Lands

The Outer Lands is a separate maze built from Ancient Stone. Corridors connect rooms containing enemies, Ancient Urns, research clues, and boss areas. An expedition usually involves finding a key room, obtaining a Runed Tablet, opening a boss room, and returning with a Primordial Pearl.

Entering through an Eldritch Portal grants **The Outer Lands** research. Special blocks and glyphs reveal further research clues; obtaining a pearl opens additional Eldritch and addon research paths in the Thaumonomicon.

**The maze and research clues**

Key Room

- Glyphed Stone and Ancient Stone: Scan these after entering the Outer Lands to discover **Revelations in the Outer Lands** and learn more about the maze.
- **Libraries and other special rooms**: Their layouts differ from ordinary corridors and contain special blocks and loot related to research.
- **Ancient Urns**: Found in corridors and rooms, they release loot when broken. Higher-quality urns may also appear around boss rooms.
- **Key rooms**: A Runed Tablet floats above the central stone pedestal, guarded by Eldritch Guardians. These rooms are the source of naturally generated tablets.
- **Boss room entrances**: An Ancient Locking Mechanism requires a Runed Tablet to activate.

Enemies in the maze include Eldritch Guardians, Shambling Husks, and Eldritch Crabs. Narrow corridors affect ranged attacks and movement; dense fog, negative effects, and branching paths can also slow exploration.

The Outer Lands restricts common forms of creative flight and Thaumcraft levitation, so changes in elevation along the corridors matter.
Marking the entrance, explored branches, and boss rooms helps you find your way back.

## Runed Tablets and Ancient Locking Mechanisms

A Runed Tablet is the key to opening an Outer Lands boss room.
Naturally generated tablets appear at the center of dedicated key rooms. Search the maze to find one, then bring it to a boss room entrance.

After completing Opening the Eye, you can research **Runed Tablet** and craft tablets through infusion. The research itself adds 5 Warp, and the recipe has an instability of **10**.

The main ingredients include:

- Draconic Evolution Information Tablet as the central ingredient.
- **2 Eldritch Eyes** and **4 Void Seeds**.
- Cured Zombie Brain.
- Crystalline Brain: Earth.

Boss Room Door

The essentia requirements are **128 Praecantatio, 64 Alienis, 64 Cognitio, 32 Iter, 32 Tenebrae, and 32 Vacuos**.
Crafted tablets are useful once you have the materials and essentia supply, reducing the time spent searching for a key room on each expedition.

**Use and consumption**

Right-clicking the locking mechanism with a tablet consumes **1 tablet**. After a brief charging period, the mechanism transforms the room and creates its challenge.

Each mechanism can only be activated once. After obtaining more tablets, look for unopened boss rooms in new mazes.
Outer Lands challenges include an Eldritch Construct, an Eldritch Warden, the Crimson Cult, and Taint. The room type is determined by world generation.

## Boss Challenges in the Outer Lands

**Eldritch Construct**

The construct has two combat forms. An attack that would defeat its initial body causes it to shed its head and enter a headless form, continuing the fight.
Losing its head also causes an explosion. Defeat the transformed body to obtain a Primordial Pearl.

This transformation interrupts the pace of combat; watch for the explosion and subsequent attacks when fighting at close range.

**Eldritch Warden**

The warden primarily attacks with ranged Eldritch projectiles and can apply Wither, Weakness, and other effects.
It appears with additional absorption health. Depleting this shield triggers a frenzy, briefly making it invulnerable and creating a force field.

Leave enough room to dodge its projectiles and force field. Defeating the warden yields a Primordial Pearl and a Rare Treasure Bag.

**Crimson Cult**

The Crimson Portal at the center of the room continually spawns Crimson Knights and Clerics, followed by a Crimson Praetor. The praetor restores the health of nearby cultists; dealing with it first makes the remaining enemies easier to clear.

The portal has strong health regeneration before the praetor appears. **The Primordial Pearl in this room drops from the Crimson Portal**, which must be defeated. The praetor also drops a Rare Treasure Bag.

**Taint**

These rooms contain tainted terrain and several tentacles, including Giant Taintacles. Their attacks and the tainted environment interfere with movement, so consider your footing and attacks from other tentacles while clearing them.

The last Giant Taintacle defeated drops a Primordial Pearl. Defeating just one may leave other Giant Taintacles in the room.

Maintain Warp Ward during an Outer Lands expedition to reduce additional Warp events during combat. After completing the challenge, use the return portal to leave.

### Void Metal and Primal Energy

**Void metal**

After Eldritch Epiphany and Thaumium research, you can research void metal. Void Seed is used to make Void metal Ingot, and is also required for Eldritch Eyes, Runed Tablets, and various addon devices.

Void metal opens several paths:

- **Void metal tools and armor**: Some tools and equipment repair their own durability and have the Warping property.
- **Void metal wand caps**: Reduce wand Vis costs and support further wand upgrades.
- **Advanced essentia storage**: Expands storage capacity for individual aspects, supporting larger alchemy and infusion recipes.
- **Void Thaumaturge Robes**: Combine protection, Vis discounts, and abilities such as those of the Goggles of Revealing.
- **Addon material paths**: Research into Shadowmetal, Shadow Fortress equipment, and Primordial equipment continues to build on void metal discoveries.

**Primal energy and the Staff Core of the Primal**

Primal Charm is an important ingredient in Eldritch crafting, used for Eldritch Eyes, the Primal Crusher, and several advanced magical recipes.

**Wand Focus: Primal** fires powerful orbs of primal energy that can damage the surrounding environment. Both the focus and its orbs are part of the scanning prerequisites for the Staff Core of the Primal.
The staff core builds on research into several elemental staff cores. See Wands, Vis and Nodes for its capacity, charging, and prerequisites.

## Primordial Pearls and Their Research Uses

A Primordial Pearl is an important reward from the Outer Lands and a key material for developing more advanced Eldritch devices.
Scanning it reveals **Primordial Pearl** research, connecting to the Advanced Alchemical Furnace, Primal Crusher, Primordial Node Manipulation, and several addon research paths.

**Advanced Alchemical Furnace**

The Advanced Alchemical Furnace increases the buffer and processing capacity of essentia extraction, using Ignis, Perditio, and Aqua Centi-Vis.
Its research also requires knowledge of Essentia Distillation and Centi-Vis power. Once the constructs and furnace are ready, it can connect to existing essentia storage and logistics to meet the demands of large infusion recipes.

See Alchemy and Essentia for its components, inputs, outputs, and power supply.

**Primal Crusher**

The Primal Crusher combines abilities from the Shovel of the Earthmover, Pickaxe of the Core, and void metal tools. It mines earth and stone in a **3×3** area and has a chance to turn eligible ores into Native Clusters.
It repairs its own durability, making it useful for large excavations as well as combat.

**Primordial Gauntlet and addon devices**

Witching Gadgets' Primordial Gauntlet holds an aura node and uses it to recharge socketed Infused Gems. Its sockets stabilize the gems, allowing their abilities to be reused after recharging.

Pearls are also used for advanced rings, Primordial equipment, and content from addons such as Thaumic Horizons and Tainted Magic.
These paths consume substantial amounts of essentia and advanced materials. A steady pearl supply allows you to develop production devices, tools, and protection separately.

### Primordial Node Manipulation

**Primordial Node Manipulation** research provides a way to modify ordinary aura nodes with pearls. Using a Primordial Pearl on a node consumes the pearl and changes the node's base aspect amounts, with a chance to improve its quality.

- The base amounts of **existing primal aspects** may increase or decrease.
- **Missing primal aspects** have a chance to be added.
- The base amounts of **compound aspects** may decrease.
- Nodes of **Fading, Pale, or Normal quality** have a chance to improve.

A pearl can react with a node even before this research is completed; completing it improves the chances of some favorable changes. With an established pearl supply, it offers another way to modify nodes, taking both random outcomes and pearl costs into account.

See Wands, Vis and Nodes for custom nodes, Node Manipulators, and Energized Nodes.

## Obtaining a Steady Supply of Primordial Pearls

**Primordial Berry**

CropsNH's **Primordial Berry** produces pearls when harvested at maturity. Plant a Primordial Pearl in Crop Sticks as the seed to establish the first crop.

- Primordial Berry cannot be obtained through crossbreeding, spread naturally, or be bred with other plants.
- Improving its stats requires devices such as the **Crop Gene Extractor and Crop Synthesizer**.
- Its preferred biome tags include **End and Magical**. At least one suitable biome tag or sufficient biome humidity is needed to prevent crop sickness.
- It has a long growth cycle and needs a stable growing environment with suitable acceleration.

**Reassembling pearl fragments**

GTNH also provides a Inert Pearl Fragment route: processing a Primordial Pearl in a Forge Hammer produces **3 fragments**. The corresponding Witching Gadgets research and infusion recipe then turn each fragment back into a pearl.

The reassembly research requires Primordial Pearl and Ichor-related prerequisites. Its recipe consumes Eldritch Eyes, Ichor materials, Aurora Blocks, and large amounts of essentia, with an instability of **20**.
This route turns one pearl into several, making it suitable once you have a complete Ichor material supply and infusion infrastructure.

## Pearl Revitalization and the Extremely Primordial Pearl

**Pearl Revitalization in Witching Gadgets**

Some Witching Gadgets recipes for Primordial equipment draw the energy from a pearl, leaving a Powerless Pearl.
After completing **Pearl Revitalization** research, infusion can restore it to a Primordial Pearl.

The recipe uses one shard of each of the six primal aspects and a Mixed Crystal Cluster. It requires **64 essentia of each primal aspect** and **384 Praecantatio**, with an instability of **10**.
When making Primordial Gauntlets, weapons, and armor, these leftover pearls can be returned to your material supply.

**Extremely Primordial Pearl**

The Extremely Primordial Pearl comes from Avaritia's integration with Thaumcraft, unlocked after Primordial Pearl research.
Its infusion uses one ordinary Primordial Pearl as the central ingredient and **7 more** around it, consuming **8 pearls** in total.

This infusion has an instability of **12** and requires 64 essentia each of the six primal aspects, Alienis, and Praecantatio, plus 32 Terminus. Producing it in quantity requires the corresponding essentia reserves and altar stability.

When used as a catalyst in later recipes, the Extremely Primordial Pearl can be retained. It is used for the Akashic Record and several Infinity equipment recipes. It does not stack; recipes requiring several pearls at once need that many separate pearls.

## Further Protection: Primordial Armor

**Primordial Armor** consists of Primordial Helm, Primordial Cuirass, Primordial Greaves, and Primordial Boots.
Its material path uses Shadow Fortress equipment, void metal, and pearls, making it worth considering when developing advanced magical protection.

Each piece can be independently tuned to a **primal affinity** by sneak-right-clicking while holding it. Several pieces tuned to the same aspect also meet the item counts required by some abilities.

- **Aer affinity**: Reflects projectiles; at least two Aer-tuned pieces provide creative flight.
- **Terra affinity**: Grants regeneration when injured, while the boots also provide knockback resistance.
- **Ignis affinity**: Extinguishes you automatically and reduces fire and explosion damage; the helm can provide Night Vision.
- **Aqua affinity**: Removes several negative effects; the helm can provide Water Breathing and underwater Night Vision.
- **Ordo affinity**: Provides regeneration and reduces the level and duration of Thaumcraft's Warp-related negative status effects.
- **Perditio affinity**: Applies Blindness and Slowness to attackers when you are hit.

The Primordial Helm also reduces the effective strength of Warp Theory events. When wearing it regularly, combine it with protection such as a Portable Shower to manage the Warp contributed by your equipment.

title: gregguns guide: Ammo and magazines
text:
# Ammo and magazines

Bullets are a production line. Feed GregTech parts into an Ammo Press, load magazines, and keep the line running.

## The line

1. **Materials:** Brass, Lead, Steel, Gunpowder, and higher-tier metals for later ammo.
2. **Parts:** Brass foil and casings make cases, lead rounds make the slugs, plates and small springs make magazines. Lathes, Bending Machines, Extruders and Assemblers make the parts.
3. **Ammo Press:** presses rounds and magazines. The press has its own recipe tab in NEI. A press runs every recipe at or below its tier. The **Ammunition Works** does the same in bulk.
4. **Magazines:** a loaded magazine is an empty one plus loose rounds, made in the press or by hand in a crafting grid.
5. **Reload:** press **R** to swap in a loaded magazine. The empty one comes back to your inventory.

Sneak and right-click a magazine to empty it back into loose rounds. Press **R** early to swap out a half-used magazine; the leftover rounds come back too.

A magazine gun with no loaded magazine at hand loads loose rounds instead: one round per reload (two on the Akimbo Mac10s), at the full reload time, one loose round from your inventory per round loaded. A magazine swap is quicker for the rounds, so keep magazines filled. Akimbo pairs load one shot's worth per reload in total. The ammo display shows a "Loose rounds" line for the rounds you carry.

## Magazines

- 9mm Pistol Magazine: made from 3 9mm Bullets; holds 18 rounds. Used by 9mm Pistol, Akimbo Pistols.
- SMG Magazine: made from 2 9mm Bullets; holds 20 to 32 rounds. Used by Thompson, Mac10, Vector.
- Assault Rifle Magazine: made from 3 Rifle Bullets; holds 30 rounds. Used by M4, AK47, AUG, SCAR, Infiltrator.
- AS50 Magazine: made from 2 High Caliber Rounds; holds 10 rounds. Used by AS50.
- LMG Magazine: made from 8 Rifle Bullets; holds 100 rounds. Used by LMG.
- Advanced Magazine: made from 3 Advanced Bullets; holds 12 to 20 rounds. Used by PDW, Pulse Rifle.
- Minigun Ammo Drum: made from 16 Rifle Bullets; holds 200 rounds. Used by Minigun.

Revolvers, shotguns, the Bolt Action Rifle and the launchers take loose rounds straight from your inventory. No magazines needed. See "Reloading" in Guns by tier for how the chamber guns load.

## What to stock at each tier

### Steam age

- Stone Bullets

### LV (Low Voltage)

- 9mm Bullets
- Shotgun Shells
- Rifle Bullets
- 9mm Pistol Magazine

### MV (Medium Voltage)

- 40mm Grenade
- SMG Magazine
- Assault Rifle Magazine

### HV (High Voltage)

- High Caliber Rounds
- Rocket
- AS50 Magazine
- LMG Magazine
- Fuel Tank
- Compressed Air Tank

### EV (Extreme Voltage)

- Advanced Bullets
- Advanced Magazine
- Minigun Ammo Drum
- Bio Tank

### LuV (Ludicrous Voltage)

- Nether Charge

### ZPM (Zero Point Module)

- Rocket (Tactical Nuke)

## Energy, tanks and endgame ammo

- **Energy weapons** have no cells to craft; charge the gun itself in a Charger or Battery Buffer of its own tier.
- **Fluid tanks:** fill Fuel Tank (diesel, gasoline, ethanol), Compressed Air Tank and Bio Tank in a GregTech Fluid Canner. The Bio Tank takes E. coli culture: Biomass from a Brewery, grown in an EV Bacterial Vat. Empty tanks come back to you.
- **Endgame ammo:** Nether Charge and Rocket (Tactical Nuke) are too big for the press. Build them on the GregTech Assembly Line.

title: gregguns guide: Ammunition Works
text:
# Ammunition Works

Ammunition Works

The Ammo Press, built as a production hall. It runs every Ammo Press recipe, many at once. The controller is an HV block.

**Size:** 5 wide, 7 tall and 13 to 31 long.

## Build it in sections

- **Feeder**, once, at the front.
- **Press bay**, 2 to 8 in a row.
- **Packing station**, once, at the back.

Use a hologram projector with a stack of 2 to 8 to preview the hall at that many bays.

## Interior lamps

Every feeder, press bay and the packing station needs one lamp under its roof (6 in the 4-bay hall). Use glowstone, a redstone lamp or any block with light level 12 or more.

## Hatches

- **Input Bus and Input Hatch:** on the feeder.
- **Energy, Maintenance and Muffler Hatches:** anywhere on the feeder. It does need a Muffler.
- **Output Bus and Output Hatch:** on the packing station's back wall.
- **The belt:** Item Pipe Casings down the middle of the floor, all of one tier.
- **The insides** are part of the build: pipe runs under the roof, a press rod and gearboxes in every bay, feed motors, an assembler arch and a lamp in every section. The glass windows show it running.

## Magazine filling bench (optional)

A 5 by 3 by 3 annex built against the packing station's lower back wall: Ammunition Works Casing around six tables in two rows of three. Natura's Workbench is the pick; a crafting table or Dire Crafting Table also works. It has its own Input Bus for empty magazines and its own Output Bus for loaded ones. Rounds come from the station's Output Bus, which must be a plain bus (an ME bus pushes its rounds away). The hall works without it.

## Make it bigger

- **More press bays:** parallels equal 4 times the bays times the voltage tier. At HV, 4 bays run 48 at once and 8 bays run 96.
- **A faster belt:** a higher-tier Item Pipe Casing belt shortens every run.
- **Bigger hatches:** power is the real limit. Feed a long hall with more amps or a higher-tier Energy Hatch.

A screwdriver toggles the ram animation.

title: gregguns guide: Armor and gear
text:
# Armor and gear

Twelve armor sets from the Steam age to IV, plus masks, goggles and back gear for the equipment slots GregTech New Horizons already has. Worn-out armor protects nothing until it is repaired, so keep a Repair Bench handy. Powered perks need a charged chestplate; the base protection never does.

## Armor sets

- Bandit Vest (Steam): **Bandit set.** Faster, jumps higher; light protection.
- Miner's Jacket (Steam): **Miner set.** Faster, and digs faster.
- Steam Chestplate (Steam): **Steam armor.** Bronze plates and Tanned Leather. Burn Coal or Charcoal in the chestplate for extra hearts, speed and a firmer stance; a Compressed Air Tank refills it too.
- Soldier's Vest (LV): **Soldier set.** Solid bullet protection, resists knockback.
- Combat Vest (MV): **Combat set.** Faster and tougher, in many camo patterns.
- Commando Vest (MV): **Commando set.** Better aim, digs fast underwater.
- Ranger Veteran Jacket (MV): **Ranger Veteran set.** Best at MV; shrugs off poison and radiation.
- Advanced Combat Chestplate (EV): **Advanced Combat set.** High protection, resists armor piercing.
- Hazardous Environment Chestplate (EV): **Hazardous Environment suit.** Powered: fireproof, hazard-proof, big jumps.
- Power Armor Chestplate (IV): **Power Armor.** Powered: the toughest set, extra hearts.
- Exo Suit Chestplate (IV): **Exo Suit.** Powered: fast, light, soft landings.
- Beret (MV): **Beret.** A hat with style, and 10% more speed.

## Masks, goggles and back gear

- Night Vision Goggles (MV): Head slot, electric. Toggle with M.
- Gas Mask (MV): Blocks gas hazards, cures poison while the filter lasts.
- Tactical Mask (HV): Gas mask, night vision and oxygen in one.
- Oxygen Mask (HV): Breathe in space, together with the Oxygen Tanks. Refill the tanks with compressed air.
- Oxygen Tanks (HV): Back slot. Pairs with the Oxygen Mask.
- Glider (HV): Back slot. Hold J or sneak while falling to glide.
- Jump Pack (HV): Back slot, electric. Big jumps, soft landings.
- Anti Gravity Device (IV): Back slot, electric. Press ; then fly.

## Extras

- Ammo Pouch: quiver slot. Holds six stacks of ammo; open it with **]**.
- Bandages and Medkit: hold right-click while hurt to heal. Bandages (LV) take 3 seconds and heal 1 heart at once, then Regeneration I for 15 seconds; the Medkit (MV) takes 2.5 seconds and heals 3 hearts, then Regeneration II for 20 seconds. At full health there is nothing to heal.
- **Camo Bench:** cycles the camo on your gun and all four armor pieces. No power needed.

## Damage types

Ten damage types, and armor resists each one separately: Physical (melee, chainsaw, hammers), Projectile (bullets and pellets), Fire (flamethrower, blasters), Explosion (rockets, grenades, nukes), Energy (lasers and blasters), Poison (Bio Gun), Lightning (Tesla Rifle), Radiation (Nuclear Death Ray), Ice (resisted by some armor) and Unresistable (ignores armor).

title: gregguns guide: Armory Gantry
text:
# Armory Gantry

Armory Gantry

The Repair Bench, built as a row of repair arches. It mends armor and guns from buses, ready for automation. The controller is an HV block.

**Size:** 7 wide, 7 tall and 7 to 19 long.

## Build it in sections

- **Booth**, once, at the front.
- **Repair bay**, 2 to 8 in a row.
- **Back wall**, once, at the back.

## Interior lamps

The booth and every repair bay need one lamp under the beam (5 in the 4-bay gantry). Use glowstone, a redstone lamp or any block with light level 12 or more.

## Hatches

- **Input Bus:** damaged items and repair parts go in.
- **Output Bus:** repaired items come out.
- **Energy and Maintenance Hatches:** on any Gantry Casing of the booth or the back wall.
- **No Muffler:** it makes no pollution.
- **The insides** are part of the build: a lamp in the booth and every bay, hoist motors and a gearbox, hooks, floor rails and a pipe run.

## Make it bigger

- **More bays:** one item per bay per cycle. A cycle takes about 2 seconds, plus up to 8 for badly damaged items.
- **A higher Energy Hatch:** the weakest Energy Hatch sets the highest item tier it repairs. LuV and ZPM gear needs a LuV or ZPM hatch.
- **Nothing lost:** repaired items keep their camo, charge, enchantments and names.

Hook it up to an ME system and it becomes a repair service for your whole base.

title: gregguns guide: Enemies and loot
text:
# Enemies and loot

Who shoots back, where you will meet them, and what they carry and drop. Every faction can be switched off in the config. They do not fight each other, but they will shoot your turrets. Their guns hit softer than yours as the gun's tier climbs, and their aim wanders with distance.

## In the wild: the Overworld

The danger level rises the farther you travel from world spawn, and in harsh biomes: deserts, wastelands, frozen lands and swamps. Higher danger opens tougher spawns.

| Enemy | Danger | Carries | Drops |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Zombie Farmer | 0+ | A hoe or a Hand Cannon, in Miner's clothes. | Wheat, seeds, leather, bread, apples, Tanned Leather, and 2 to 6 Stone Bullets. |
| Zombie Miner | 0+ | A pickaxe or a Hand Cannon, and a Miner's Helmet. | Coal, redstone, iron, gunpowder, Tanned Leather, and 2 to 6 Stone Bullets. |
| Zombie Soldier | 1+ | A revolver, a Thompson or a shovel, in Soldier armor. | Shotgun shells, 9mm bullets, iron, gunpowder, Tanned Leather. |
| Skeleton Soldier | 1+ | A revolver, Thompson or Hand Cannon; a helmet and boots. | Bones, coal, gunpowder, iron, Tanned Leather, 9mm and Stone Bullets. |
| Psycho Steve | 1+, rare boss | A Chainsaw and red Miner armor. Very fast, very angry. | Always his Chainsaw and 4 to 8 full Fuel Tanks. |
| Bandit | 2+ | A pistol, revolver, Sawed Off, Thompson, AK47 or Bolt Action Rifle, in Bandit armor. | Ammo, iron, gunpowder, Tanned Leather. |

## In the Nether

Nether biomes only. The Nether's danger is the Overworld distance a spot leads to (eight blocks per Nether block), plus 1, so the tougher spawns sit farther from your portal.

| Enemy | Where | Carries | Drops |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Zombie Pigman Soldier | Anywhere, alone or in pairs. The common one. | Combat armor and a Thompson, AK47, Flamethrower, LMG, Rocket Launcher or more. | Steel, gold, gunpowder, shotgun shells, rifle bullets, 9mm bullets, 1 or 2 rockets and a full Fuel Tank. |
| Super Mutants (Basic, Heavy, Elite) | Basic from about 60 Nether blocks out, Heavy from about 125, Elite from about 310. | Each rank is bigger. A Rocket Launcher, AK47, Combat Shotgun or Laser Rifle. | Cybernetic Parts, blaze rods, ghast tears, rockets, rifle bullets, shotgun shells. |
| Cyberdemon (boss) | Rare, deep in the Nether, always alone, never within 128 blocks of another. | Fireproof, with a Nether Blaster. | Cybernetic Parts, blaze rods, ghast tears. |

## In the End

Commando squads of two or three roam the End's outer islands. None spawn within 256 blocks of the End's center, so the dragon's island stays clear, and the farther out you go the better their gear.

## At camps, bases and nests

Military Camps, Military Bases and Aircraft Carriers fly a Camp Flag that keeps calling in soldiers until you break it. Breaking it brings the helicopter. About one Military Base in five is a red base: it flies a red flag over a red pad, with red standards at its corners, and Dictator Dave holds the post by the flag and stays there. Blue bases and the Aircraft Carrier fly blue flags and have no commander.

| Enemy | Where | Carries | Drops |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Army Soldier | Camps and bases | An M4, Combat Shotgun or Bolt Action Rifle; Combat armor or a beret. | Shotgun shells, rifle bullets, iron, Tanned Leather. |
| Commando | Aircraft Carriers, silo guard and elite posts | An M4 and full Commando armor. | Steel, rubber, rifle bullets, Explosive Charges. |
| Dictator Dave (boss) | Red Military Bases | A Golden Revolver, a beret and a hundred hit points. | Always the Golden Revolver and 8 to 16 9mm bullets. |
| Camp Turret | Camps | An AK47 behind iron plating. Shoots you and your turrets. | Nothing; just break it. |
| Attack Helicopter | Boss: break a camp flag | Machine-gun bursts and rockets from the air. | 16 to 31 rifle bullets, 8 to 15 rockets, 2 or 3 Cybernetic Parts, 4 to 7 iron blocks. |
| Alien Bug | Bug nests | Fast, climbs walls, bites. Pours out of the monster spawners in desert and wasteland nests. | String and spider eyes. |

## Silo complexes

The guard spawners of an abandoned silo complex call up Army Soldiers. Rooms far from the hub hold elite spawners that call up Commandos and Stormtroopers. In a complex whose ceiling is LuV or higher, the elite posts are command posts that also call up the Outcast.

| Enemy | Carries | Drops |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stormtrooper | A silver Hazardous Environment suit and a Blaster or Laser Rifle. | Steel, rubber, redstone, circuits, batteries, and the parts of an energy gun: Laser Barrels and Focuses, Carbon Stocks and Receivers, tungstensteel plates and screws, titanium plates. |
| Outcast | Dark Power Armor and the heavy guns: Minigun, Tesla Rifle, Grim Reaper, Laser Rifle, Bio Gun, Flamethrower or LMG. | The richest table: rifle bullets, rockets, full Fuel and Bio Tanks, energy-gun parts, Mechanical Parts T3, Power Plating, Rhodium-Plated Palladium and tungstensteel plates, HSS-G ingots. |

## Ruins and bases

Chests hold loot up to the tier shown, and never above the server's loot limit (`loot.maxTier`, EV by default). Alien Bug Nests have no chests, only monster spawners. The Big Bunker's two spawners call up zombies. Every structure above ground stands on level, solid ground that is filled down to the natural ground, and the Military Base is one level pad with its roads, fence, tents and buildings.

- Small Factory, Train Station, House, Gas Station: LV
- Big Bunker: MV
- Military Base and camps: MV
- Aircraft Carrier, Submarine: MV

## What they drop

Up to two picks from their loot list, plus one more per level of Looting. Every NPC that carries a gun also drops rounds for it: a quarter to three quarters of a magazine, loose, one item per round. A Thompson gives 5 to 15 9mm bullets, and no stack is bigger than 64. Flame and bio guns drop one full tank. Energy guns drop the parts of their recipe, never the gun. A player kill has a small chance to drop the gun itself (2%, plus 1% per level of Looting; bosses never) and sometimes the armor they wear. Mobs Info lists the drops. Nothing an NPC drops goes above the server's loot limit (`loot.maxTier`, EV by default), worn armor included: a drop above it stays with the body. A drop's tier is its whole crafting chain, so a plate of a high-tier metal counts as that tier wherever it comes from.

With Infernal Mobs installed, any of them can spawn with an Elite, Ultra or Infernal rank and better loot: LV items for Elite, MV for Ultra, and a rare HV drop from Infernal (an AS50 magazine). The helicopter and camp turrets never do.

## How hard they hit

An NPC's gun damage follows the tier of the gun it fires: full damage up to MV, 85% at HV (the Attack Helicopter counts as HV), 70% at EV, 55% at IV, 45% at LuV and 40% at ZPM. Elite, Ultra and Infernal NPCs and bosses shoot at 75% on top of that, and NPC guns get half their armor penetration against players. NPCs aim true within 5 blocks; past that their aim error grows with distance, so almost every shot lands at 10 blocks, about half at 20 and about one in ten at 30. Gun and projectile hits do not knock their target back, for players and NPCs alike; explosions still throw. Your own guns and the Rampart turret are unchanged.

For a harder game, set every `combat.npcDamage*` key and `combat.npcEliteDamage` to 1.0, `damagefactors.armorPenetrationMultiplierNPCtoPlayer` to 1.0, `combat.npcSpreadPerBlock` to 0 and `combat.knockback` to true. All four together give every NPC gun its full stats.

title: gregguns guide: Getting started
text:
# Getting started

From a Steam-age hand cannon to a magazine-fed pistol, in six steps. The GregGuns questbook tab walks you up the tiers one weapon at a time.

## 1. Steam age: the Hand Cannon

Craft a Stone Barrel and a Wooden Stock, then the Hand Cannon. It fires one Stone Bullets per shot. Make bullets by hand, or 24 at a time in a Steam Ammo Press.

Steam Ammo Press

## 2. LV: your first pistol

Guns are put together from GregTech parts in an Assembler. Each tier needs its gate material: **Steel** for LV, Aluminum for MV, Stainless Steel for HV. For the 9mm Pistol you need a Hardened Steel Barrel and Mechanical Parts T2.

## 3. Build an Ammo Press

Basic Ammo Press

The press has its own recipe tab in NEI. A press runs every recipe at or below its tier: the Steam press runs LV recipes too, and higher tiers overclock as usual.

## 4. Press rounds and magazines

Brass foil, lead rounds and gunpowder become 9mm Bullets. Plates, springs and Mechanical Parts become empty magazines. Fill them in the press, or craft one 9mm Pistol Magazine with 3 bullets.

## 5. Reload and fight

Press **R** to swap in a loaded magazine. The empty one comes back to your inventory, so refill it and go again. With no loaded magazine to hand, **R** loads one loose round instead, so the rounds a soldier drops are never wasted. Shoot the soldiers, bandits and mutants for loot.

## 6. Repair, then climb the tiers

Worn armor and guns go back on a Repair Bench of at least their tier, with GregTech plates and Tanned Leather.

Basic Repair Bench

## Default keys

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Left mouse | Fire (hold for auto) |
| Right mouse | Scope, or charge a beam |
| R | Reload |
| M | Night vision |
| ] | Ammo pouch |
| ; | Back device: Glider, Anti Gravity Device |

See Guns by tier, Ammo and magazines and Machines next.

title: gregguns guide: Guns by tier
text:
# Guns by tier

Every gun is built from GregTech parts in an Assembler, and each tier needs its gate material, so a gun arrives exactly when you can make it. Hold **Shift** over any gun to see its damage type, range, spread and magazine size.

Energy guns are their own batteries. Charge them in a GregTech Charger or Battery Buffer of exactly the gun's tier; a wrong-tier charger will not touch them.

## Reloading

- **Magazine guns** swap in a loaded magazine with **R**. With none at hand they load one loose round per reload instead (two on the Akimbo Mac10s), taking the full reload time.
- **Chamber guns** load one chamber at a time: the Revolver, Golden Revolver, Akimbo Revolvers, Akimbo Golden Revolvers, Combat Shotgun and Sawed Off. The reload time is split across the chambers, so a reload from empty takes as long as ever, and pulling the trigger stops it and fires what is loaded. A revolver bullet fills the whole cylinder: the rounds it holds beyond the chamber being filled wait on the gun for the next chambers.
- **Top-up when idle.** A chamber gun in your hand that is not full starts reloading by itself after 2 seconds without a shot, if you carry its ammo. `guns.idleReloadDelayTicks` sets the delay in ticks; 0 turns it off.
- The launchers and the Hand Cannon take loose rounds in a single reload, and energy guns charge instead.
- Hold **Shift** over a gun for its reload rule.

## Steam age

Gate material: **Bronze, Wrought Iron**. Power: steam.

- Hand Cannon: Slow, single-shot stone cannon; uses Stone Bullets.

## LV (Low Voltage)

Gate material: **Steel**. Power: 32 EU/t.

- 9mm Pistol: Semi-auto sidearm, 18 rounds; uses 9mm Pistol Magazine.
- Revolver: Six shots, hits harder; uses 9mm Bullets.
- Sawed Off: Two barrels, close range; uses Shotgun Shells.
- Bolt Action Rifle: Scoped long-range rifle; uses Rifle Bullets.
- Combat Knife: Fast steel melee; needs no ammo.
- Crowbar: Melee that mines like iron; needs no ammo.
- Stielgranate: Thrown stick grenade; thrown by hand.
- Akimbo Pistols: Two pistols, alternating; uses 9mm Pistol Magazine.
- Akimbo Revolvers: Two revolvers, alternating; uses 9mm Bullets.

## MV (Medium Voltage)

Gate material: **Aluminum**. Power: 128 EU/t.

- Thompson SMG: Full auto, 20 rounds; uses SMG Magazine.
- Mac10: Very fast, loose spread; uses SMG Magazine.
- Combat Shotgun: Eight-shell pump action; uses Shotgun Shells.
- M4 Assault Rifle: Accurate, scoped, 30 rounds; uses Assault Rifle Magazine.
- AK47: Hits harder, 30 rounds; uses Assault Rifle Magazine.
- Akimbo Mac10s: Both fire every pull; uses SMG Magazine.
- Frag Grenade: Hold to throw harder; thrown by hand.
- Flashbang: Blinds anyone looking; thrown by hand.

## HV (High Voltage)

Gate material: **Stainless Steel**. Power: 512 EU/t.

- AUG: Scoped, very accurate; uses Assault Rifle Magazine.
- SCAR: Heavy hits, pierces armor; uses Assault Rifle Magazine.
- Vector: Fast-firing SMG; uses SMG Magazine.
- The Infiltrator: Silenced M4; uses Assault Rifle Magazine.
- AS50 Sniper Rifle: Anti-armor sniper rifle; uses AS50 Magazine.
- LMG: 100-round suppressor; uses LMG Magazine.
- Grenade Launcher: Six bouncing 40mm shells; uses 40mm Grenade.
- Rocket Launcher: One big explosive rocket; uses Rocket.
- Flamethrower: Short-range fire stream; uses Fuel Tank.
- Chainsaw: Fuel-powered melee saw; uses Fuel Tank.
- Power Hammer: Air-powered smash; uses Compressed Air Tank.

## EV (Extreme Voltage)

Gate material: **Titanium**. Power: 2,048 EU/t.

- Laser Rifle: Instant beam, four shots a second; charged in a EV Charger or Battery Buffer.
- PDW: Armor-piercing bursts; uses Advanced Magazine.
- Pulse Rifle: Long-range three-round bursts; uses Advanced Magazine.
- Minigun: 200 rounds, 20 shots a second; uses Minigun Ammo Drum.
- Tesla Rifle: Lightning jumps to three more targets; charged in a EV Charger or Battery Buffer.
- Sonic Rifle: Ring-shaped shockwave volley; charged in a EV Charger or Battery Buffer.
- Bio Gun: Poison blobs, charge to grow; uses Bio Tank.
- Power Hammer (Advanced): Harder, faster smash; uses Compressed Air Tank.

## IV (Insane Voltage)

Gate material: **Tungstensteel**. Power: 8,192 EU/t.

- Blaster Rifle: Scoped energy rifle; charged in a IV Charger or Battery Buffer.
- De-Atomizer Pistol: Armor-piercing energy sidearm; charged in a IV Charger or Battery Buffer.
- Akimbo De-Atomizer Pistols: Two of them, twice the charge; charged in a IV Charger or Battery Buffer.
- Scatter Laser Rifle: Five-beam spread; charged in a IV Charger or Battery Buffer.
- Golden Revolver: Gold-plated heavy revolver; uses 9mm Bullets.
- Akimbo Golden Revolvers: A matched pair; uses 9mm Bullets.

## LuV (Ludicrous Voltage)

Gate material: **HSS-G**. Power: 32,768 EU/t.

- Nether Blaster: Slow bolts that set targets alight; uses Nether Charge.
- Alien Blaster: Full-auto energy pistol; charged in a LuV Charger or Battery Buffer.
- Grim Reaper: Four rockets per load; uses Rocket.

## ZPM (Zero Point Module)

Gate material: **Naquadah Alloy**. Power: 131,072 EU/t.

- Nuclear Death Ray: Held radiation beam, 48 blocks; charged in a ZPM Charger or Battery Buffer.
- Nuke Launcher: One tactical nuke; uses Rocket (Tactical Nuke).

title: gregguns guide: GregGuns
text:
# GregGuns

Guns, armor and military tech for GregTech New Horizons. Everything here is made from GregTech parts on GregTech machines, and it unlocks with GregTech tiers. If you can make Steel, you can make a pistol.

Hand Cannon 9mm Pistol M4 Assault Rifle AS50 Sniper Rifle Laser Rifle Nuclear Death Ray

Hold **G** over any GregGuns gun, magazine or piece of armor to jump to its page.

title: gregguns guide: Machines
text:
# Machines

Every GregGuns machine starts as a single block. The ones you will run all day also come as a multiblock: same recipes, many at once. Start with the single blocks.

## Ammo Press

Steam to EV. Presses bullets, shells, rockets and magazines from GregTech parts. It has its own recipe tab in NEI.

Steam Ammo Press Basic Ammo Press Advanced Ammo Press Advanced Ammo Press II Advanced Ammo Press III

Its multiblock is the Ammunition Works.

## Repair Bench

LV to IV. Restores worn armor and guns with GregTech plates and Tanned Leather. Its tier must be at least the item's.

Basic Repair Bench Advanced Repair Bench Advanced Repair Bench II Advanced Repair Bench III Advanced Repair Bench IV

Its multiblock is the Armory Gantry.

## Turret

MV to IV. Give it a gun, ammo and an armor plate. It guards your base and rebuilds itself after a hit.

Gun Turret Advanced Gun Turret Advanced Gun Turret II Advanced Gun Turret III

Its multiblock is the Rampart.

## Camo Bench

LV. Swaps camo patterns on your gun and armor, one click per piece, so it never needs a bigger version. No power needed.

Camo Bench

## Explosive Charges

MV and HV. Stick one on a wall, set depth and fuse, arm it and step back. It bores a clean tunnel and drops the blocks as items. The Advanced charge cuts obsidian.

Explosive Charge

## Storage and camp gear

Weapon and Reinforced Chests store your kit. Break an enemy camp's flag and an Attack Helicopter comes looking for you.

Weapon Chest Reinforced Chest

title: gregguns guide: Pack integration notes
text:
# Pack integration notes

GregGuns is built on GregTech, so most of what you already know applies.

- **GregTech tiers and materials.** Guns, ammo and armor are made from GregTech materials and parts, in GregTech machines, and unlock with GregTech tiers (Steam to ZPM). Nothing here has its own power system.
- **EU and charging.** Energy guns and powered armor store EU. Charge each one in a GregTech Charger or Battery Buffer of exactly its tier.
- **NEI.** The Ammo Press has its own recipe tab, and every GregGuns item is listed in build order.
- **Questbook.** GregGuns has its own tab in the GregTech New Horizons questbook, after Kill All the Things. Early quests pay ammo or a magazine for the gun they teach, and chapter ends and boss hunts pay a GregTech loot bag of their tier. A reward never outruns its tier.
- **Infernal Mobs.** Infernal GregGuns enemies drop tiered ammo, magazines and a gun of their own tier.
- **Teams.** On a server with ServerUtilities, your team's members and allies count as friends for turret and Rampart security.
- **Equipment slots.** Back gear, masks and the ammo pouch use the extra slots the pack already provides.
- **Guide.** Hold **G** over a GregGuns item for its page, or press **G** and pick GregGuns.

Back to the start.

title: gregguns guide: Rampart
text:
# Rampart

Rampart

The Turret, built as a battlement. Up to ten turrets share one ammo feed and one power feed. The controller is an HV block.

**Size:** 6 tall, 3 deep and 8 to 24 long.

## Build it in sections

- **Gatehouse**, once, at one end.
- **Wall bay with a mount**, 2 to 10 in a row.
- **End cap**, once, at the other end.

## Hatches

- **Input Bus:** the shared ammo store for every mount (ME works).
- **Output Bus:** empty magazines come back here.
- **Energy and Maintenance Hatches:** on the gatehouse plating.
- **Gun Mount Hatch:** exactly one on each bay's sill. Right-click it with a gun to arm it. Gun Mount Hatch (MV)

A mount takes any GregGuns gun up to its own tier, except akimbo pairs. Right-click it empty-handed to take the gun back.

## Make it bigger

- **More mounts:** another turret every two blocks of wall, on the same feed.
- **Better plating:** every mount gets the armor of the weakest turret armor plate used: Iron Turret Armor 5, Steel Turret Armor 10, Aluminum Turret Armor 15, Carbon Turret Armor 20.
- **Security:** a screwdriver cycles who it spares: everyone, your friends, or only you. Friends are the members and allies of your ServerUtilities team.

title: guidenh guide: Welcome to GuideNH
text:
# Welcome to GuideNH

Welcome, .

You are reading this page through **GuideNH**, an in-game guide framework designed for rich, data-driven documentation.

GuideNH is far more than a simple guide. It brings multiple features together in a single guide interface: Markdown text, item links, crafting recipes, keybind hints, tooltips, and interactive scene previews.

## Getting Around

Use the **navigation panel** on the left to browse guide pages.

Use the buttons in the top-right corner to search, return home, move backward or forward, and close the guide.

When a page has an item index, hover over the corresponding item in your inventory and hold  to jump directly to the related page.

  Hover here for a quick tip.

## What You May Find Here

| Section | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Book Articles | Explanations, tutorials, and reference pages |
| Compass Navigation | Page trees, categories, and related topics |
| Crafting Table Recipes | Crafting, processing, and usage information |
| Stone Bricks Structures | Multiblock previews and build guidance |

## Interactive Content

Some pages may contain interactive previews. These can help explain machines, structures, layouts, or special mechanics without requiring you to leave the game.

You may be able to:

- rotate and zoom the scene
- inspect individual blocks
- switch layers or variants
- compare different structure states
- follow annotations placed directly in the preview

## For Readers

Start with the navigation panel, then search for the item, machine, or concept you want to understand.

If you are not sure where to begin, try opening the recommended pages on the home screen once they become available.

After closing this welcome page, you can show it again by enabling **Welcome Popup** in the GuideNH configuration.

Tip: GuideNH usually splits content into multiple small, connected pages instead of turning everything into one overly long document.

## For Authors

GuideNH pages are written as Markdown files with frontmatter metadata.

Authors can use GuideNH-specific tags such as Paper, , tooltips, item references, recipe previews, and scene components to make documentation easier to read and maintain in-game.

Our goal is not only to explain content, but also to make complex information clear, intuitive, and easy to explore.

## Enjoy the Guide

GuideNH helps you find answers faster, while also helping authors organize content more effectively.

It is your guide map, your reference manual, and a practical tool for understanding complex systems.
